DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 3, LINK ROUND

# LINK ROUND

**LINK 1: NARROWED TO:** Matthew 1:18 puts the finding of the child "of the Holy Ghost" before the couple's coming together, and Matthew 1:19–20 show Joseph reasoning as a husband who is not the cause. I drop the claim that "came together" is the first knowing by lexical force alone, and the claim that the verb's gloss names a fleshly begetter.

**Footing**
- [L1] Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- [L2] *prin* (G4250), "before, sooner". *synerchomai* (G4905), "to convene... or (specially), cohabit (conjugally)".
- [L1] Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
- [L3] Deuteronomy 22:24: "the man, because he hath humbled his neighbour's wife." The law treats a betrothed woman found with another man as a capital matter.
- [L4] A husband who had known his wife in the espousal would find the pregnancy his own, and a just man would have no ground to put her away. Joseph's minding to put her away privily is the reasoning of a man who knows he is not the cause. The angel's "for" in Matthew 1:20 answers that reasoning with a source ("of the Holy Ghost"), not with "it is yours".

**Presses**
- Matthew 1:18, "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost". I grant the finding comes before the taking. Matthew 1:18 uses *synerchomai*, a different word from *paralambanō* in Matthew 1:24. The order stands: espoused, found with child of the Holy Ghost, then coming together.
- Matthew 1:24, "took unto him his wife". I grant that the taking follows the finding. [L2] *paralambanō* (G3880), "to receive near". [L3] Matthew 1:20, "that which is conceived in her", is said of her before the taking, so the child was already there when he took her.
- Deuteronomy 20:7, "hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her". [L2] *laqach* (H3947), "to take". Here the betrothed is already "a wife" before the taking, so the title "Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20) dates no knowing.
- Deuteronomy 22:24, "his neighbour's wife". [L2] *ishshah* (H802), "wife". [L3] Deuteronomy 22:23: "If a damsel [that is] a virgin be betrothed unto an husband." The same law calls her "a virgin" and betrothed to "an husband" together. Wife-titles and virginity stand side by side in the espousal.
- Matthew 1:20, "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." I grant the address to David's son and the title "wife". [L2] *enthymeomai* (G1760), "to ponder", is the verb for "while he thought on these things". The "for" gives the reason for "fear not", and the reason is the source "of the Holy Ghost". I do not rest on the verb's gloss.
- 1 John 5:1, "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God". [L2] *gennaō* (G1080) is glossed "figuratively, to regenerate". [L3] John 1:13: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God." That is regeneration, set against "the will of man". Matthew 1:20 says "conceived in her", a conception in the womb.
- Matthew 1:19, "was minded to put her away privily". [L2] *boulomai* (G1014), "to be minded". I grant it states intent with two stated grounds, "a just [man]" and "not willing to make her a publick example". Those grounds explain how he would put her away. The reason to put her away at all is her being with child, which fits only a husband who is not the cause (Deuteronomy 22:24).
- John 3:6, "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit." I grant two kinds. [L3] Luke 1:35: "that holy thing which shall be born of thee". The flesh is said to be born of Mary. John 3:6 names the kind of the thing born, and does not say what the Spirit cannot do.

---

**LINK 2: NARROWED TO:** From the taking to the birth Joseph did not know her (Matthew 1:25). The child was already "of the Holy Ghost" when he took her (Matthew 1:18, 1:20), and Mary had said before the conception "I know not a man" (Luke 1:34). I drop the claim that Matthew 1:25 by itself reaches back across the espousal.

**Footing**
- [L1] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
- [L2] *heōs* (G2193), "until". *ginōskō* (G1097), "to know".
- [L3] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" The same verb of knowing stands in both verses.
- [L4] Luke 1:34 covers the time before the conception and Matthew 1:25 the time from the taking to the birth. Matthew 1:18 (found with child before coming together) lies between them. The challenger's union within the espousal is a step no verse states.

**Presses**
- Matthew 1:25: I grant the abstinence runs from the taking and "till" is the birth. [L3] Matthew 1:24.
- Matthew 1:24, "took unto him his wife". I grant the span opens at the taking. [L2] *paralambanō* (G3880). Matthew 1:20 already gives "Mary thy wife" and the child as conceived, so the note says the child's coming was not joined to any knowing by him.
- Genesis 4:1, "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived". [L2] *yada'* (H3045), "to know". Where knowing is the cause, the text states it before the conceiving. [L3] Matthew 1:18 gives in that place "found with child of the Holy Ghost".
- Matthew 1:21, "thou shalt call his name JESUS". [L2] *kaleō* (G2564), "to call". [L3] Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS." The same naming is given to Mary, so naming does not identify a begetter. [L3] Luke 1:63, where Zacharias writes "His name is John", records a naming by command, not the begetting.
- Deuteronomy 22:23, "If a damsel [that is] a virgin be betrothed unto an husband". [L2] *aras* (H781), "to betroth". I grant she has an husband. The law's own words keep "virgin" and "betrothed" together, so the espousal does not date a union.

---

**LINK 3: NARROWED TO:** Luke 1:34 puts the question of manner on the ground "I know not a man", and Luke 1:35 answers with the Holy Ghost, the power of the Highest, and "born of thee", naming no man. I drop the claim that "come upon" and "overshadow" are seed-words by themselves.

**Footing**
- [L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- [L2] *pōs* (G4459), "an interrogative particle of manner; in what way?"
- [L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee."
- [L4] A question of manner receives an answer of manner. The answer names the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest, and the child is "born of thee". If a husband's union were the manner, the question would have no force and the answer no point.

**Presses**
- Luke 1:31, "thou shalt conceive in thy womb". [L2] *syllambanō* (G4815), "to conceive". I grant it is future. [L3] Luke 1:35, also future, gives the Holy Ghost as what follows the angel's word.
- Luke 1:27, "a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David". [L2] *parthenos* (G3933), "virgin". [L3] Deuteronomy 22:23. Luke names her "a virgin" while "espoused", at the time the angel speaks.
- Luke 1:36, "she hath also conceived a son in her old age... who was called barren". I grant the "also". [L3] Luke 1:13 says "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son", with "thee" (Zacharias). [L3] Luke 1:31 says to Mary "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son", with no "bear thee". Elisabeth's trouble is "barren" and "old age". Mary's is "I know not a man". The "also" joins two signs of God's power and does not make the means alike.
- Acts 1:8, "ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you". [L2] *eperchomai* (G1904), "to come upon". I grant it is power. [L3] Luke 1:35 joins it to "the power of the Highest", and the sentence ends in what is "born of thee".
- Luke 9:34, "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them". [L2] *episkiazō* (G1982), "to overshadow". I grant it says nothing of seed. In Luke 1:35 it stands with "the power of the Highest". I rest on the sentence's answer to "how", not on the verb alone.
- Luke 1:32, "shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David". I grant the title and throne are given before Mary asks. [L3] Luke 1:35: "therefore also that holy thing". The "also" adds the Holy Ghost's coming as a further ground for the title. [L4] "Therefore" follows the clause just before it.
- Acts 13:33, "in that he hath raised up Jesus again". I grant Psalm 2:7 is applied to the raising. I do not rest the conception on Psalm 2:7. [L3] Romans 1:4: "declared [to be] the Son of God with power... by the resurrection from the dead". The resurrection declares the Son, while Luke 1:35 gives the title before it.
- Luke 1:13, "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son". Answered above under Luke 1:36.

---

**LINK 4: NARROWED TO:** Matthew 1:16 changes the pattern at its last step. Every earlier step is "begat"; the last is "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus", with a passive verb and a feminine "of whom". Luke 3:23 words "son of Joseph" with "as was supposed". I drop "only".

**Footing**
- [L1] Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus."
- [L2] *hēs* (the relative "of whom", feminine singular) can refer only to Mary. *egennēthē* is the passive "was born".
- [L3] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob." Every earlier step takes the child as the object of "begat".
- [L4] The line is carried to Joseph, named "husband". It does not carry "begat" to Jesus.

**Presses**
- Matthew 1:3, "Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar", and Matthew 1:5, "Booz begat Obed of Ruth". I grant "of" with the mother's name. In both the father is the subject of "begat" and the child its object. In 1:16 "begat" ends at Joseph.
- Matthew 1:16: see the footing.
- Matthew 1:20, "Joseph, thou son of David". I grant Joseph's descent (Luke 2:4). That is his house, not a begetting of Jesus.
- Luke 3:23, "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph". [L2] *nomizō* (G3543), "to deem", behind "supposed". [L3] Acts 16:13, "where prayer was wont to be made", renders the same root as custom. [L3] Luke 2:44, "But they, supposing him to have been in the company, went a day's journey", renders it as a thought that proved wrong. The KJV puts "supposed" where an opinion is meant, as here beside a genealogy.
- Luke 2:41, "his parents went to Jerusalem every year". I grant the household title (Luke 2:48). [L2] *patēr* (G3962), "father". A household title is not a statement of begetting.
- Luke 2:33, "Joseph and his mother marvelled". The narrator writes "Joseph and his mother", not "his father and mother". [L3] John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" That is the crowd's speech.
- John 1:45, "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph". It is Philip's speech, not the narrator's verdict. [L3] John 6:42 shows speech of this kind.
- Luke 2:49, "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" [L3] Luke 2:48: "thy father and I". I grant the household title. The child answers the mother's "thy father" with "my Father's". [L3] 1 Chronicles 28:6 says "Solomon thy son", and no verse says "Joseph begat Jesus" in that place.

---

**LINK 5: NARROWED TO:** The one of whom the child was "born" is the woman (Luke 1:35 "born of thee"; Matthew 1:16 "of whom", feminine). Paul's clause "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" says what the flesh is, so the flesh reaches him as David's seed through her, if Links 1–3 stand. I drop any claim that a row states Mary's tribe, and I drop "of a woman" as load-bearing.

**Footing**
- [L1] Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh".
- [L2] *sperma* (G4690), "seed".
- [L3] Luke 1:35: "that holy thing which shall be born of thee".
- [L4] With the conception by the Holy Ghost and the child born of one human parent, the flesh named as David's seed passes through that parent.

**Presses**
- Galatians 4:4, "made of a woman, made under the law". [L2] *ginomai* (G1096), "to be made". I grant the idiom is said of men with fathers. [L3] Job 14:1 and Matthew 11:11 are the same idiom. I rest on Luke 1:35 and Romans 1:3.
- Matthew 11:11, "born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist". Granted, as above.
- Romans 1:3: see the footing. It names the flesh and does not say through which parent it reaches him.
- Luke 1:27, "a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David". [L2] *oikos* (G3624), "house". I grant the clause belongs to the man. It is silent on Mary's house, and I do not claim it for her.
- Luke 1:36, "thy cousin Elisabeth". [L3] Luke 1:5, "of the daughters of Aaron". The word *syngenis*, "kinswoman", names a relation and no tribe. It fixes nothing about Mary's father's house.
- Numbers 1:18, "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers". [L2] *bayith* (H1004), "house". I grant that pedigrees were declared by fathers' houses. [L3] Ezra 2:61 shows a man "called after their name", the wife's house.
- Isaiah 8:3, "I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son". Margin: "Heb. approached". Where the husband's approach is the cause, the text states it. [L3] Genesis 4:1 is the same. Matthew 1:18 states "found with child of the Holy Ghost" in that place. [L3] Isaiah 7:11, "ask it either in the depth, or in the height above", then Isaiah 7:14, "a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son", is a sign of that scale.
- Genesis 24:16, "a virgin, neither had any man known her". I grant "virgin" names her state when spoken of, defined by "neither had any man known her". [L3] Luke 1:27 names Mary "a virgin" at the angel's word.

---

**LINK 6: NARROWED TO:** The conception was by the Holy Ghost apart from a man (Links 1–3 as narrowed). The child is "the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" as the one God raises up (Acts 2:30), born of Mary. I do not claim a row names Mary's house. No quoted row says David's seed passes through a living father's loins at the last step.

**Footing**
- [L1] Acts 2:30: "that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne".
- [L3] Psalms 132:11: "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne". God sets him and God raises him up.
- [L3] Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me".
- [L4] The promise names David's body and God's act, and the child's body is described as prepared. Neither verse routes the seed through a father at the last step.

**Presses**
- Acts 2:30: see the footing.
- Hebrews 7:5, "though they come out of the loins of Abraham". [L2] *osphys* (G3751), "loin". I grant loins reach descendants across generations through begetters. [L3] Matthew 1:2 gives that pattern, and Matthew 1:16 does not repeat it at the last step.
- Hebrews 7:14, "our Lord sprang out of Juda". I grant it names his tribe. Joseph's house gives the legal reckoning (Luke 2:4), which I granted. The verb says origin and not route.
- 2 Samuel 7:12, "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels". [L2] *zera'* (H2233), "seed". I grant the seed proceeds from David's body. "I will set up" is God's act (Psalms 132:11).
- Ezra 2:59, "they could not shew their father's house, and their seed". Margin: "or, pedigree". I grant that registers were by fathers' houses. This is a priesthood register and not a statement of how a child is conceived.
- Ezra 2:61, "took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name". [L3] Ezra 2:62: "These sought their register [among] those that were reckoned by genealogy, but they were not found: therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood." The cause given is the register not found. The verse shows a man reckoned after his wife's house.
- Luke 2:48, "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing". [L2] *patēr* (G3962). Granted as a household title, as answered under Link 4.
- 1 Chronicles 28:6, "I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father". I grant it stands beside "Solomon thy son". For Jesus no verse says "Joseph begat" him.

---

## CHALLENGER'S UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES

1. The inference that "came together" is only the taking into the house, which props the objection that a union could have fallen inside the espousal. Quote: "So "before they came together" (Matthew 1:18) is before the taking into his house."
PRESSED WITH:
Matthew 1:18 "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" -- MEANS: the verb is a different word from the one in Matthew 1:24, and it carries conjugal cohabiting. -- [L2] synerchomai (to convene, cohabit conjugally) | [L3] Matthew 1:24 "took unto him his wife"
Deuteronomy 20:7 "hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her" -- MEANS: the wife-title is given before the taking, so it dates no knowing. -- [L2] laqach (to take) | [L3] Matthew 1:20 "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife"
Deuteronomy 22:23 "If a damsel [that is] a virgin be betrothed unto an husband" -- MEANS: the law calls the betrothed one a virgin with an husband. -- [L2] aras (to betroth) | [L3] Luke 1:27 "a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph"

2. The inference that a knowing fell within the espousal and made the child Joseph's, which props the claim that the child came from his loins. Quote: "Footed on these rows: Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins."
PRESSED WITH:
Matthew 1:18 "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" -- MEANS: the child is attributed to the Holy Ghost at the finding, with no knowing stated. -- [L2] heuriskō (to find) | [L3] Matthew 1:20 "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost"
Matthew 1:19 "was minded to put her away privily" -- MEANS: a husband who knew he was the cause would have no ground to put her away. -- [L2] boulomai (to be minded) | [L3] Deuteronomy 22:24 "he hath humbled his neighbour's wife"
Luke 1:34 "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" -- MEANS: she gives no man known as the ground of her question about manner. -- [L2] pōs (in what way?) | [L3] Luke 1:35 "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee"
Genesis 4:1 "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived" -- MEANS: the text states the knowing before the conceiving where it is the cause. -- [L2] yada' (to know) | [L3] Matthew 1:25 "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son"

3. The inference that Elisabeth's case sets God's power beside a husband's act in Mary's case. Quote: "So the appeal to God's power stands beside a husband."
PRESSED WITH:
Luke 1:36 "she hath also conceived a son in her old age... who was called barren" -- MEANS: Elisabeth's difficulty is barrenness and age, and the "also" joins signs without making the means alike. -- [L2] syllambanō (to conceive) | [L3] Luke 1:34 "seeing I know not a man"
Luke 1:13 "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son" -- MEANS: "bear thee" is said to Zacharias. -- [L3] Luke 1:31 "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son" | [L2] syllambanō (to conceive)
Luke 1:35 "that holy thing which shall be born of thee" -- MEANS: the answer to "how" names no husband. -- [L2] kaleō (to call) | [L3] Luke 1:34 "How shall this be"

4. The inference that "as was supposed" carries no verdict and is Luke's usual way of speaking of Joseph. Quote: "So "by usage" is Luke's own way of speaking of Joseph."
PRESSED WITH:
Luke 3:23 "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph" -- MEANS: the narrator qualifies this one statement beside the genealogy. -- [L2] nomizō (to deem) | [L3] Luke 2:44 "But they, supposing him to have been in the company, went a day's journey"
Acts 16:13 "where prayer was wont to be made" -- MEANS: the KJV renders the same root as "wont" for custom and "supposed" for opinion. -- [L2] nomizō (to deem) | [L3] Luke 3:23 "as was supposed"
John 6:42 "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" -- MEANS: the claim of a father is the crowd's speech. -- [L3] John 1:45 "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph" | [L2] patēr (father)

5. The inference that the Holy Ghost cannot be the source of the flesh because flesh goes only with flesh. Quote: "John 3:6 keeps flesh with flesh."
PRESSED WITH:
Luke 1:35 "that holy thing which shall be born of thee" -- MEANS: the flesh is born of Mary, with the Holy Ghost's coming as the cause. -- [L2] kaleō (to call) | [L3] Matthew 1:20 "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost"
Hebrews 10:5 "a body hast thou prepared me" -- MEANS: the body is described as prepared by God. -- [L3] Romans 1:3 "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" | [L2] sperma (seed)
Romans 1:4 "declared [to be] the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness" -- MEANS: the second clause names the Spirit's part without denying the first. -- [L2] pneuma (spirit) | [L3] Romans 1:3 "according to the flesh"

6. The inference that Acts 2:30's loins reach Christ through a father's line to its last step. Quote: "So "the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" (Acts 2:30) reaches Christ through the fathers' line."
PRESSED WITH:
Hebrews 7:10 "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him." -- MEANS: "his father" is an ancestor, so the verse says nothing of how the last step is made. -- [L2] osphys (loin) | [L3] Hebrews 7:5 "though they come out of the loins of Abraham"
Psalms 132:11 "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne" -- MEANS: the promise names David's body and God's setting up, not a father at the last step. -- [L2] zera' (seed) | [L3] 2 Samuel 7:12 "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels"
Matthew 1:16 "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus" -- MEANS: the "begat" pattern of Matthew 1:2 ends at Joseph, and the child is "born" of the woman. -- [L2] anēr (husband) | [L3] Matthew 1:2 "Abraham begat Isaac"
Ezra 2:62 "therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood" -- MEANS: the stated cause is the register not found, and Ezra 2:61 shows a man called after his wife's house. -- [L3] Ezra 2:61 "was called after their name" | [L2] bayith (house)

# LINK ROUND

**LINK 1: NARROWED TO:** Matthew 1:18 puts the finding of the child "of the Holy Ghost" before the couple's coming together, and Matthew 1:19–20 show Joseph reasoning as a husband who is not the cause. I drop the claim that "came together" is the first knowing by lexical force alone, and the claim that the verb's gloss names a fleshly begetter.

**Footing**
- [L1] Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- [L2] *prin* (G4250), "before, sooner". *synerchomai* (G4905), "to convene... or (specially), cohabit (conjugally)".
- [L1] Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
- [L3] Deuteronomy 22:24: "the man, because he hath humbled his neighbour's wife." The law treats a betrothed woman found with another man as a capital matter.
- [L4] A husband who had known his wife in the espousal would find the pregnancy his own, and a just man would have no ground to put her away. Joseph's minding to put her away privily is the reasoning of a man who knows he is not the cause. The angel's "for" in Matthew 1:20 answers that reasoning with a source ("of the Holy Ghost"), not with "it is yours".

**Presses**
- Matthew 1:18, "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost". I grant the finding comes before the taking. Matthew 1:18 uses *synerchomai*, a different word from *paralambanō* in Matthew 1:24. The order stands: espoused, found with child of the Holy Ghost, then coming together.
- Matthew 1:24, "took unto him his wife". I grant that the taking follows the finding. [L2] *paralambanō* (G3880), "to receive near". [L3] Matthew 1:20, "that which is conceived in her", is said of her before the taking, so the child was already there when he took her.
- Deuteronomy 20:7, "hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her". [L2] *laqach* (H3947), "to take". Here the betrothed is already "a wife" before the taking, so the title "Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20) dates no knowing.
- Deuteronomy 22:24, "his neighbour's wife". [L2] *ishshah* (H802), "wife". [L3] Deuteronomy 22:23: "If a damsel [that is] a virgin be betrothed unto an husband." The same law calls her "a virgin" and betrothed to "an husband" together. Wife-titles and virginity stand side by side in the espousal.
- Matthew 1:20, "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." I grant the address to David's son and the title "wife". [L2] *enthymeomai* (G1760), "to ponder", is the verb for "while he thought on these things". The "for" gives the reason for "fear not", and the reason is the source "of the Holy Ghost". I do not rest on the verb's gloss.
- 1 John 5:1, "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God". [L2] *gennaō* (G1080) is glossed "figuratively, to regenerate". [L3] John 1:13: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God." That is regeneration, set against "the will of man". Matthew 1:20 says "conceived in her", a conception in the womb.
- Matthew 1:19, "was minded to put her away privily". [L2] *boulomai* (G1014), "to be minded". I grant it states intent with two stated grounds, "a just [man]" and "not willing to make her a publick example". Those grounds explain how he would put her away. The reason to put her away at all is her being with child, which fits only a husband who is not the cause (Deuteronomy 22:24).
- John 3:6, "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit." I grant two kinds. [L3] Luke 1:35: "that holy thing which shall be born of thee". The flesh is said to be born of Mary. John 3:6 names the kind of the thing born, and does not say what the Spirit cannot do.

**LINK 2: NARROWED TO:** From the taking to the birth Joseph did not know her (Matthew 1:25). **Presses**

**LINK 3: NARROWED TO:** Luke 1:34 puts the question of manner on the ground "I know not a man", and Luke 1:35 answers with the Holy Ghost, the power of the Highest, and "born of thee", naming no man. I drop the claim that "come upon" and "overshadow" are seed-words by themselves.

[L3] Luke 1:31 says to Mary "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son", with no "bear thee". Elisabeth's trouble is "barren" and "old age". Mary's is "I know not a man". **LINK 4: NARROWED TO:** Matthew 1:16 changes the pattern at its last step. Every earlier step is "begat"; the last is "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus", with a passive verb and a feminine "of whom". Luke 3:23 words "son of Joseph" with "as was supposed". I drop "only".

# LINK ROUND

**LINK 1: NARROWED TO:** Matthew 1:18 puts the finding of the child "of the Holy Ghost" before the couple's coming together, and Matthew 1:19–20 show Joseph reasoning as a husband who is not the cause. I drop the claim that "came together" is the first knowing by lexical force alone, and the claim that the verb's gloss names a fleshly begetter.

**Footing**
- [L1] Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- [L2] *prin* (G4250), "before, sooner". *synerchomai* (G4905), "to convene... or (specially), cohabit (conjugally)".
- [L1] Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
- [L3] Deuteronomy 22:24: "the man, because he hath humbled his neighbour's wife." The law treats a betrothed woman found with another man as a capital matter.
- [L4] A husband who had known his wife in the espousal would find the pregnancy his own, and a just man would have no ground to put her away. Joseph's minding to put her away privily is the reasoning of a man who knows he is not the cause. The angel's "for" in Matthew 1:20 answers that reasoning with a source ("of the Holy Ghost"), not with "it is yours".

**Presses**
- Matthew 1:18, "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost". I grant the finding comes before the taking. Matthew 1:18 uses *synerchomai*, a different word from *paralambanō* in Matthew 1:24. The order stands: espoused, found with child of the Holy Ghost, then coming together.
- Matthew 1:24, "took unto him his wife". I grant that the taking follows the finding. [L2] *paralambanō* (G3880), "to receive near". [L3] Matthew 1:20, "that which is conceived in her", is said of her before the taking, so the child was already there when he took her.
- Deuteronomy 20:7, "hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her". [L2] *laqach* (H3947), "to take". Here the betrothed is already "a wife" before the taking, so the title "Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20) dates no knowing.
- Deuteronomy 22:24, "his neighbour's wife". [L2] *ishshah* (H802), "wife". [L3] Deuteronomy 22:23: "If a damsel [that is] a virgin be betrothed unto an husband." The same law calls her "a virgin" and betrothed to "an husband" together. Wife-titles and virginity stand side by side in the espousal.
- Matthew 1:20, "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." I grant the address to David's son and the title "wife". [L2] *enthymeomai* (G1760), "to ponder", is the verb for "while he thought on these things". The "for" gives the reason for "fear not", and the reason is the source "of the Holy Ghost". I do not rest on the verb's gloss.
- 1 John 5:1, "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God". [L2] *gennaō* (G1080) is glossed "figuratively, to regenerate". [L3] John 1:13: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God." That is regeneration, set against "the will of man". Matthew 1:20 says "conceived in her", a conception in the womb.
- Matthew 1:19, "was minded to put her away privily". [L2] *boulomai* (G1014), "to be minded". I grant it states intent with two stated grounds, "a just [man]" and "not willing to make her a publick example". Those grounds explain how he would put her away. The reason to put her away at all is her being with child, which fits only a husband who is not the cause (Deuteronomy 22:24).
- John 3:6, "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit." I grant two kinds. [L3] Luke 1:35: "that holy thing which shall be born of thee". The flesh is said to be born of Mary. John 3:6 names the kind of the thing born, and does not say what the Spirit cannot do.

---

**LINK 2: NARROWED TO:** From the taking to the birth Joseph did not know her (Matthew 1:25). The child was already "of the Holy Ghost" when he took her (Matthew 1:18, 1:20), and Mary had said before the conception "I know not a man" (Luke 1:34). I drop the claim that Matthew 1:25 by itself reaches back across the espousal.

**Footing**
- [L1] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
- [L2] *heōs* (G2193), "until". *ginōskō* (G1097), "to know".
- [L3] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" The same verb of knowing stands in both verses.
- [L4] Luke 1:34 covers the time before the conception and Matthew 1:25 the time from the taking to the birth. Matthew 1:18 (found with child before coming together) lies between them. The challenger's union within the espousal is a step no verse states.

**Presses**
- Matthew 1:25: I grant the abstinence runs from the taking and "till" is the birth. [L3] Matthew 1:24.
- Matthew 1:24, "took unto him his wife". I grant the span opens at the taking. [L2] *paralambanō* (G3880). Matthew 1:20 already gives "Mary thy wife" and the child as conceived, so the note says the child's coming was not joined to any knowing by him.
- Genesis 4:1, "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived". [L2] *yada'* (H3045), "to know". Where knowing is the cause, the text states it before the conceiving. [L3] Matthew 1:18 gives in that place "found with child of the Holy Ghost".
- Matthew 1:21, "thou shalt call his name JESUS". [L2] *kaleō* (G2564), "to call". [L3] Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS." The same naming is given to Mary, so naming does not identify a begetter. [L3] Luke 1:63, where Zacharias writes "His name is John", records a naming by command, not the begetting.
- Deuteronomy 22:23, "If a damsel [that is] a virgin be betrothed unto an husband". [L2] *aras* (H781), "to betroth". I grant she has an husband. The law's own words keep "virgin" and "betrothed" together, so the espousal does not date a union.

---

**LINK 3: NARROWED TO:** Luke 1:34 puts the question of manner on the ground "I know not a man", and Luke 1:35 answers with the Holy Ghost, the power of the Highest, and "born of thee", naming no man. I drop the claim that "come upon" and "overshadow" are seed-words by themselves.

**Footing**
- [L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- [L2] *pōs* (G4459), "an interrogative particle of manner; in what way?"
- [L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee."
- [L4] A question of manner receives an answer of manner. The answer names the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest, and the child is "born of thee". If a husband's union were the manner, the question would have no force and the answer no point.

**Presses**
- Luke 1:31, "thou shalt conceive in thy womb". [L2] *syllambanō* (G4815), "to conceive". I grant it is future. [L3] Luke 1:35, also future, gives the Holy Ghost as what follows the angel's word.
- Luke 1:27, "a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David". [L2] *parthenos* (G3933), "virgin". [L3] Deuteronomy 22:23. Luke names her "a virgin" while "espoused", at the time the angel speaks.
- Luke 1:36, "she hath also conceived a son in her old age... who was called barren". I grant the "also". [L3] Luke 1:13 says "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son", with "thee" (Zacharias). [L3] Luke 1:31 says to Mary "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son", with no "bear thee". Elisabeth's trouble is "barren" and "old age". Mary's is "I know not a man". The "also" joins two signs of God's power and does not make the means alike.
- Acts 1:8, "ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you". [L2] *eperchomai* (G1904), "to come upon". I grant it is power. [L3] Luke 1:35 joins it to "the power of the Highest", and the sentence ends in what is "born of thee".
- Luke 9:34, "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them". [L2] *episkiazō* (G1982), "to overshadow". I grant it says nothing of seed. In Luke 1:35 it stands with "the power of the Highest". I rest on the sentence's answer to "how", not on the verb alone.
- Luke 1:32, "shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David". I grant the title and throne are given before Mary asks. [L3] Luke 1:35: "therefore also that holy thing". The "also" adds the Holy Ghost's coming as a further ground for the title. [L4] "Therefore" follows the clause just before it.
- Acts 13:33, "in that he hath raised up Jesus again". I grant Psalm 2:7 is applied to the raising. I do not rest the conception on Psalm 2:7. [L3] Romans 1:4: "declared [to be] the Son of God with power... by the resurrection from the dead". The resurrection declares the Son, while Luke 1:35 gives the title before it.
- Luke 1:13, "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son". Answered above under Luke 1:36.

---

**LINK 4: NARROWED TO:** Matthew 1:16 changes the pattern at its last step. Every earlier step is "begat"; the last is "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus", with a passive verb and a feminine "of whom". Luke 3:23 words "son of Joseph" with "as was supposed". I drop "only".

**Footing**
- [L1] Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus."
- [L2] *hēs* (the relative "of whom", feminine singular) can refer only to Mary. *egennēthē* is the passive "was born".
- [L3] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob." Every earlier step takes the child as the object of "begat".
- [L4] The line is carried to Joseph, named "husband". It does not carry "begat" to Jesus.

**Presses**
- Matthew 1:3, "Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar", and Matthew 1:5, "Booz begat Obed of Ruth". I grant "of" with the mother's name. In both the father is the subject of "begat" and the child its object. In 1:16 "begat" ends at Joseph.
- Matthew 1:16: see the footing.
- Matthew 1:20, "Joseph, thou son of David". I grant Joseph's descent (Luke 2:4). That is his house, not a begetting of Jesus.
- Luke 3:23, "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph". [L2] *nomizō* (G3543), "to deem", behind "supposed". [L3] Acts 16:13, "where prayer was wont to be made", renders the same root as custom. [L3] Luke 2:44, "But they, supposing him to have been in the company, went a day's journey", renders it as a thought that proved wrong. The KJV puts "supposed" where an opinion is meant, as here beside a genealogy.
- Luke 2:41, "his parents went to Jerusalem every year". I grant the household title (Luke 2:48). [L2] *patēr* (G3962), "father". A household title is not a statement of begetting.
- Luke 2:33, "Joseph and his mother marvelled". The narrator writes "Joseph and his mother", not "his father and mother". [L3] John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" That is the crowd's speech.
- John 1:45, "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph". It is Philip's speech, not the narrator's verdict. [L3] John 6:42 shows speech of this kind.
- Luke 2:49, "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" [L3] Luke 2:48: "thy father and I". I grant the household title. The child answers the mother's "thy father" with "my Father's". [L3] 1 Chronicles 28:6 says "Solomon thy son", and no verse says "Joseph begat Jesus" in that place.

---

**LINK 5: NARROWED TO:** The one of whom the child was "born" is the woman (Luke 1:35 "born of thee"; Matthew 1:16 "of whom", feminine). Paul's clause "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" says what the flesh is, so the flesh reaches him as David's seed through her, if Links 1–3 stand. I drop any claim that a row states Mary's tribe, and I drop "of a woman" as load-bearing.

**Footing**

- [L2] *sperma* (G4690), "seed".
- [L3] Luke 1:35: "that holy thing which shall be born of thee".
- [L4] With the conception by the Holy Ghost and the child born of one human parent, the flesh named as David's seed passes through that parent.

**Presses**

- Matthew 11:11, "born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist". Granted, as above.
- Romans 1:3: see the footing. It names the flesh and does not say through which parent it reaches him.
- Luke 1:27, "a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David". [L2] *oikos* (G3624), "house". I grant the clause belongs to the man. It is silent on Mary's house, and I do not claim it for her.
- Luke 1:36, "thy cousin Elisabeth". [L3] Luke 1:5, "of the daughters of Aaron". The word *syngenis*, "kinswoman", names a relation and no tribe. It fixes nothing about Mary's father's house.

[L3] Isaiah 7:11, "ask it either in the depth, or in the height above", then Isaiah 7:14, "a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son", is a sign of that scale.
- Genesis 24:16, "a virgin, neither had any man known her". I grant "virgin" names her state when spoken of, defined by "neither had any man known her". [L3] Luke 1:27 names Mary "a virgin" at the angel's word.

---

**LINK 6: NARROWED TO:** The conception was by the Holy Ghost apart from a man (Links 1–3 as narrowed). The child is "the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" as the one God raises up (Acts 2:30), born of Mary. I do not claim a row names Mary's house. No quoted row says David's seed passes through a living father's loins at the last step.

**Footing**
- [L1] Acts 2:30: "that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne".
- [L3] Psalms 132:11: "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne". God sets him and God raises him up.
- [L3] Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me".
- [L4] The promise names David's body and God's act, and the child's body is described as prepared. Neither verse routes the seed through a father at the last step.

**Presses**
- Acts 2:30: see the footing.
- Hebrews 7:5, "though they come out of the loins of Abraham". [L2] *osphys* (G3751), "loin". I grant loins reach descendants across generations through begetters. [L3] Matthew 1:2 gives that pattern, and Matthew 1:16 does not repeat it at the last step.
- Hebrews 7:14, "our Lord sprang out of Juda". I grant it names his tribe. Joseph's house gives the legal reckoning (Luke 2:4), which I granted. The verb says origin and not route.
- 2 Samuel 7:12, "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels". [L2] *zera'* (H2233), "seed". I grant the seed proceeds from David's body. "I will set up" is God's act (Psalms 132:11).

- Ezra 2:61, "took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name". [L3] Ezra 2:62: "These sought their register [among] those that were reckoned by genealogy, but they were not found: therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood." The cause given is the register not found. The verse shows a man reckoned after his wife's house.
- Luke 2:48, "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing". [L2] *patēr* (G3962). Granted as a household title, as answered under Link 4.
- 1 Chronicles 28:6, "I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father". I grant it stands beside "Solomon thy son". For Jesus no verse says "Joseph begat" him.

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 3, LINK ROUND

# LINK ROUND

**LINK 1: NARROWED TO:** Matthew 1:18 puts the finding of the child "of the Holy Ghost" before the couple's coming together, and Matthew 1:19–20 show Joseph reasoning as a husband who is not the cause. I drop the claim that "came together" is the first knowing by lexical force alone, and the claim that the verb's gloss names a fleshly begetter.

**Footing**
- [L1] Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- [L2] *prin* (G4250), "before, sooner". *synerchomai* (G4905), "to convene... or (specially), cohabit (conjugally)".
- [L1] Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
- [L3] Deuteronomy 22:24: "the man, because he hath humbled his neighbour's wife." The law treats a betrothed woman found with another man as a capital matter.
- [L4] A husband who had known his wife in the espousal would find the pregnancy his own, and a just man would have no ground to put her away. Joseph's minding to put her away privily is the reasoning of a man who knows he is not the cause. The angel's "for" in Matthew 1:20 answers that reasoning with a source ("of the Holy Ghost"), not with "it is yours".

**Presses**
- Matthew 1:18, "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost". I grant the finding comes before the taking. Matthew 1:18 uses *synerchomai*, a different word from *paralambanō* in Matthew 1:24. The order stands: espoused, found with child of the Holy Ghost, then coming together.
- Matthew 1:24, "took unto him his wife". I grant that the taking follows the finding. [L2] *paralambanō* (G3880), "to receive near". [L3] Matthew 1:20, "that which is conceived in her", is said of her before the taking, so the child was already there when he took her.
- Deuteronomy 20:7, "hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her". [L2] *laqach* (H3947), "to take". Here the betrothed is already "a wife" before the taking, so the title "Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20) dates no knowing.
- Deuteronomy 22:24, "his neighbour's wife". [L2] *ishshah* (H802), "wife". [L3] Deuteronomy 22:23: "If a damsel [that is] a virgin be betrothed unto an husband." The same law calls her "a virgin" and betrothed to "an husband" together. Wife-titles and virginity stand side by side in the espousal.
- Matthew 1:20, "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." I grant the address to David's son and the title "wife". [L2] *enthymeomai* (G1760), "to ponder", is the verb for "while he thought on these things". The "for" gives the reason for "fear not", and the reason is the source "of the Holy Ghost". I do not rest on the verb's gloss.
- 1 John 5:1, "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God". [L2] *gennaō* (G1080) is glossed "figuratively, to regenerate". [L3] John 1:13: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God." That is regeneration, set against "the will of man". Matthew 1:20 says "conceived in her", a conception in the womb.
- Matthew 1:19, "was minded to put her away privily". [L2] *boulomai* (G1014), "to be minded". I grant it states intent with two stated grounds, "a just [man]" and "not willing to make her a publick example". Those grounds explain how he would put her away. The reason to put her away at all is her being with child, which fits only a husband who is not the cause (Deuteronomy 22:24).
- John 3:6, "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit." I grant two kinds. [L3] Luke 1:35: "that holy thing which shall be born of thee". The flesh is said to be born of Mary. John 3:6 names the kind of the thing born, and does not say what the Spirit cannot do.

---

**LINK 2: NARROWED TO:** From the taking to the birth Joseph did not know her (Matthew 1:25). The child was already "of the Holy Ghost" when he took her (Matthew 1:18, 1:20), and Mary had said before the conception "I know not a man" (Luke 1:34). I drop the claim that Matthew 1:25 by itself reaches back across the espousal.

**Footing**
- [L1] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
- [L2] *heōs* (G2193), "until". *ginōskō* (G1097), "to know".
- [L3] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" The same verb of knowing stands in both verses.
- [L4] Luke 1:34 covers the time before the conception and Matthew 1:25 the time from the taking to the birth. Matthew 1:18 (found with child before coming together) lies between them. The challenger's union within the espousal is a step no verse states.

**Presses**
- Matthew 1:25: I grant the abstinence runs from the taking and "till" is the birth. [L3] Matthew 1:24.
- Matthew 1:24, "took unto him his wife". I grant the span opens at the taking. [L2] *paralambanō* (G3880). Matthew 1:20 already gives "Mary thy wife" and the child as conceived, so the note says the child's coming was not joined to any knowing by him.
- Genesis 4:1, "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived". [L2] *yada'* (H3045), "to know". Where knowing is the cause, the text states it before the conceiving. [L3] Matthew 1:18 gives in that place "found with child of the Holy Ghost".
- Matthew 1:21, "thou shalt call his name JESUS". [L2] *kaleō* (G2564), "to call". [L3] Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS." The same naming is given to Mary, so naming does not identify a begetter. [L3] Luke 1:63, where Zacharias writes "His name is John", records a naming by command, not the begetting.
- Deuteronomy 22:23, "If a damsel [that is] a virgin be betrothed unto an husband". [L2] *aras* (H781), "to betroth". I grant she has an husband. The law's own words keep "virgin" and "betrothed" together, so the espousal does not date a union.

---

**LINK 3: NARROWED TO:** Luke 1:34 puts the question of manner on the ground "I know not a man", and Luke 1:35 answers with the Holy Ghost, the power of the Highest, and "born of thee", naming no man. I drop the claim that "come upon" and "overshadow" are seed-words by themselves.

**Footing**
- [L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- [L2] *pōs* (G4459), "an interrogative particle of manner; in what way?"
- [L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee."
- [L4] A question of manner receives an answer of manner. The answer names the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest, and the child is "born of thee". If a husband's union were the manner, the question would have no force and the answer no point.

**Presses**
- Luke 1:31, "thou shalt conceive in thy womb". [L2] *syllambanō* (G4815), "to conceive". I grant it is future. [L3] Luke 1:35, also future, gives the Holy Ghost as what follows the angel's word.
- Luke 1:27, "a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David". [L2] *parthenos* (G3933), "virgin". [L3] Deuteronomy 22:23. Luke names her "a virgin" while "espoused", at the time the angel speaks.
- Luke 1:36, "she hath also conceived a son in her old age... who was called barren". I grant the "also". [L3] Luke 1:13 says "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son", with "thee" (Zacharias). [L3] Luke 1:31 says to Mary "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son", with no "bear thee". Elisabeth's trouble is "barren" and "old age". Mary's is "I know not a man". The "also" joins two signs of God's power and does not make the means alike.
- Acts 1:8, "ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you". [L2] *eperchomai* (G1904), "to come upon". I grant it is power. [L3] Luke 1:35 joins it to "the power of the Highest", and the sentence ends in what is "born of thee".
- Luke 9:34, "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them". [L2] *episkiazō* (G1982), "to overshadow". I grant it says nothing of seed. In Luke 1:35 it stands with "the power of the Highest". I rest on the sentence's answer to "how", not on the verb alone.
- Luke 1:32, "shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David". I grant the title and throne are given before Mary asks. [L3] Luke 1:35: "therefore also that holy thing". The "also" adds the Holy Ghost's coming as a further ground for the title. [L4] "Therefore" follows the clause just before it.
- Acts 13:33, "in that he hath raised up Jesus again". I grant Psalm 2:7 is applied to the raising. I do not rest the conception on Psalm 2:7. [L3] Romans 1:4: "declared [to be] the Son of God with power... by the resurrection from the dead". The resurrection declares the Son, while Luke 1:35 gives the title before it.
- Luke 1:13, "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son". Answered above under Luke 1:36.

---

**LINK 4: NARROWED TO:** Matthew 1:16 changes the pattern at its last step. Every earlier step is "begat"; the last is "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus", with a passive verb and a feminine "of whom". Luke 3:23 words "son of Joseph" with "as was supposed". I drop "only".

**Footing**
- [L1] Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus."
- [L2] *hēs* (the relative "of whom", feminine singular) can refer only to Mary. *egennēthē* is the passive "was born".
- [L3] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob." Every earlier step takes the child as the object of "begat".
- [L4] The line is carried to Joseph, named "husband". It does not carry "begat" to Jesus.

**Presses**
- Matthew 1:3, "Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar", and Matthew 1:5, "Booz begat Obed of Ruth". I grant "of" with the mother's name. In both the father is the subject of "begat" and the child its object. In 1:16 "begat" ends at Joseph.
- Matthew 1:16: see the footing.
- Matthew 1:20, "Joseph, thou son of David". I grant Joseph's descent (Luke 2:4). That is his house, not a begetting of Jesus.
- Luke 3:23, "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph". [L2] *nomizō* (G3543), "to deem", behind "supposed". [L3] Acts 16:13, "where prayer was wont to be made", renders the same root as custom. [L3] Luke 2:44, "But they, supposing him to have been in the company, went a day's journey", renders it as a thought that proved wrong. The KJV puts "supposed" where an opinion is meant, as here beside a genealogy.
- Luke 2:41, "his parents went to Jerusalem every year". I grant the household title (Luke 2:48). [L2] *patēr* (G3962), "father". A household title is not a statement of begetting.
- Luke 2:33, "Joseph and his mother marvelled". The narrator writes "Joseph and his mother", not "his father and mother". [L3] John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" That is the crowd's speech.
- John 1:45, "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph". It is Philip's speech, not the narrator's verdict. [L3] John 6:42 shows speech of this kind.
- Luke 2:49, "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" [L3] Luke 2:48: "thy father and I". I grant the household title. The child answers the mother's "thy father" with "my Father's". [L3] 1 Chronicles 28:6 says "Solomon thy son", and no verse says "Joseph begat Jesus" in that place.

---

**LINK 5: NARROWED TO:** The one of whom the child was "born" is the woman (Luke 1:35 "born of thee"; Matthew 1:16 "of whom", feminine). Paul's clause "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" says what the flesh is, so the flesh reaches him as David's seed through her, if Links 1–3 stand. I drop any claim that a row states Mary's tribe, and I drop "of a woman" as load-bearing.

**Footing**
- [L1] Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh".
- [L2] *sperma* (G4690), "seed".
- [L3] Luke 1:35: "that holy thing which shall be born of thee".
- [L4] With the conception by the Holy Ghost and the child born of one human parent, the flesh named as David's seed passes through that parent.

**Presses**
- Galatians 4:4, "made of a woman, made under the law". [L2] *ginomai* (G1096), "to be made". I grant the idiom is said of men with fathers. [L3] Job 14:1 and Matthew 11:11 are the same idiom. I rest on Luke 1:35 and Romans 1:3.
- Matthew 11:11, "born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist". Granted, as above.
- Romans 1:3: see the footing. It names the flesh and does not say through which parent it reaches him.
- Luke 1:27, "a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David". [L2] *oikos* (G3624), "house". I grant the clause belongs to the man. It is silent on Mary's house, and I do not claim it for her.
- Luke 1:36, "thy cousin Elisabeth". [L3] Luke 1:5, "of the daughters of Aaron". The word *syngenis*, "kinswoman", names a relation and no tribe. It fixes nothing about Mary's father's house.
- Numbers 1:18, "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers". [L2] *bayith* (H1004), "house". I grant that pedigrees were declared by fathers' houses. [L3] Ezra 2:61 shows a man "called after their name", the wife's house.
- Isaiah 8:3, "I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son". Margin: "Heb. approached". Where the husband's approach is the cause, the text states it. [L3] Genesis 4:1 is the same. Matthew 1:18 states "found with child of the Holy Ghost" in that place. [L3] Isaiah 7:11, "ask it either in the depth, or in the height above", then Isaiah 7:14, "a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son", is a sign of that scale.
- Genesis 24:16, "a virgin, neither had any man known her". I grant "virgin" names her state when spoken of, defined by "neither had any man known her". [L3] Luke 1:27 names Mary "a virgin" at the angel's word.

---

**LINK 6: NARROWED TO:** The conception was by the Holy Ghost apart from a man (Links 1–3 as narrowed). The child is "the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" as the one God raises up (Acts 2:30), born of Mary. I do not claim a row names Mary's house. No quoted row says David's seed passes through a living father's loins at the last step.

**Footing**
- [L1] Acts 2:30: "that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne".
- [L3] Psalms 132:11: "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne". God sets him and God raises him up.
- [L3] Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me".
- [L4] The promise names David's body and God's act, and the child's body is described as prepared. Neither verse routes the seed through a father at the last step.

**Presses**
- Acts 2:30: see the footing.
- Hebrews 7:5, "though they come out of the loins of Abraham". [L2] *osphys* (G3751), "loin". I grant loins reach descendants across generations through begetters. [L3] Matthew 1:2 gives that pattern, and Matthew 1:16 does not repeat it at the last step.
- Hebrews 7:14, "our Lord sprang out of Juda". I grant it names his tribe. Joseph's house gives the legal reckoning (Luke 2:4), which I granted. The verb says origin and not route.
- 2 Samuel 7:12, "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels". [L2] *zera'* (H2233), "seed". I grant the seed proceeds from David's body. "I will set up" is God's act (Psalms 132:11).
- Ezra 2:59, "they could not shew their father's house, and their seed". Margin: "or, pedigree". I grant that registers were by fathers' houses. This is a priesthood register and not a statement of how a child is conceived.
- Ezra 2:61, "took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name". [L3] Ezra 2:62: "These sought their register [among] those that were reckoned by genealogy, but they were not found: therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood." The cause given is the register not found. The verse shows a man reckoned after his wife's house.
- Luke 2:48, "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing". [L2] *patēr* (G3962). Granted as a household title, as answered under Link 4.
- 1 Chronicles 28:6, "I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father". I grant it stands beside "Solomon thy son". For Jesus no verse says "Joseph begat" him.

---

## CHALLENGER'S UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES

1. The inference that "came together" is only the taking into the house, which props the objection that a union could have fallen inside the espousal. Quote: "So "before they came together" (Matthew 1:18) is before the taking into his house."
PRESSED WITH:
Matthew 1:18 "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" -- MEANS: the verb is a different word from the one in Matthew 1:24, and it carries conjugal cohabiting. -- [L2] synerchomai (to convene, cohabit conjugally) | [L3] Matthew 1:24 "took unto him his wife"
Deuteronomy 20:7 "hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her" -- MEANS: the wife-title is given before the taking, so it dates no knowing. -- [L2] laqach (to take) | [L3] Matthew 1:20 "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife"
Deuteronomy 22:23 "If a damsel [that is] a virgin be betrothed unto an husband" -- MEANS: the law calls the betrothed one a virgin with an husband. -- [L2] aras (to betroth) | [L3] Luke 1:27 "a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph"

2. The inference that a knowing fell within the espousal and made the child Joseph's, which props the claim that the child came from his loins. Quote: "Footed on these rows: Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins."
PRESSED WITH:
Matthew 1:18 "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" -- MEANS: the child is attributed to the Holy Ghost at the finding, with no knowing stated. -- [L2] heuriskō (to find) | [L3] Matthew 1:20 "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost"
Matthew 1:19 "was minded to put her away privily" -- MEANS: a husband who knew he was the cause would have no ground to put her away. -- [L2] boulomai (to be minded) | [L3] Deuteronomy 22:24 "he hath humbled his neighbour's wife"
Luke 1:34 "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" -- MEANS: she gives no man known as the ground of her question about manner. -- [L2] pōs (in what way?) | [L3] Luke 1:35 "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee"
Genesis 4:1 "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived" -- MEANS: the text states the knowing before the conceiving where it is the cause. -- [L2] yada' (to know) | [L3] Matthew 1:25 "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son"

3. The inference that Elisabeth's case sets God's power beside a husband's act in Mary's case. Quote: "So the appeal to God's power stands beside a husband."
PRESSED WITH:
Luke 1:36 "she hath also conceived a son in her old age... who was called barren" -- MEANS: Elisabeth's difficulty is barrenness and age, and the "also" joins signs without making the means alike. -- [L2] syllambanō (to conceive) | [L3] Luke 1:34 "seeing I know not a man"
Luke 1:13 "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son" -- MEANS: "bear thee" is said to Zacharias. -- [L3] Luke 1:31 "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son" | [L2] syllambanō (to conceive)
Luke 1:35 "that holy thing which shall be born of thee" -- MEANS: the answer to "how" names no husband. -- [L2] kaleō (to call) | [L3] Luke 1:34 "How shall this be"

4. The inference that "as was supposed" carries no verdict and is Luke's usual way of speaking of Joseph. Quote: "So "by usage" is Luke's own way of speaking of Joseph."
PRESSED WITH:
Luke 3:23 "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph" -- MEANS: the narrator qualifies this one statement beside the genealogy. -- [L2] nomizō (to deem) | [L3] Luke 2:44 "But they, supposing him to have been in the company, went a day's journey"
Acts 16:13 "where prayer was wont to be made" -- MEANS: the KJV renders the same root as "wont" for custom and "supposed" for opinion. -- [L2] nomizō (to deem) | [L3] Luke 3:23 "as was supposed"
John 6:42 "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" -- MEANS: the claim of a father is the crowd's speech. -- [L3] John 1:45 "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph" | [L2] patēr (father)

5. The inference that the Holy Ghost cannot be the source of the flesh because flesh goes only with flesh. Quote: "John 3:6 keeps flesh with flesh."
PRESSED WITH:
Luke 1:35 "that holy thing which shall be born of thee" -- MEANS: the flesh is born of Mary, with the Holy Ghost's coming as the cause. -- [L2] kaleō (to call) | [L3] Matthew 1:20 "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost"
Hebrews 10:5 "a body hast thou prepared me" -- MEANS: the body is described as prepared by God. -- [L3] Romans 1:3 "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" | [L2] sperma (seed)
Romans 1:4 "declared [to be] the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness" -- MEANS: the second clause names the Spirit's part without denying the first. -- [L2] pneuma (spirit) | [L3] Romans 1:3 "according to the flesh"

6. The inference that Acts 2:30's loins reach Christ through a father's line to its last step. Quote: "So "the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" (Acts 2:30) reaches Christ through the fathers' line."
PRESSED WITH:
Hebrews 7:10 "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him." -- MEANS: "his father" is an ancestor, so the verse says nothing of how the last step is made. -- [L2] osphys (loin) | [L3] Hebrews 7:5 "though they come out of the loins of Abraham"

Matthew 1:16 "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus" -- MEANS: the "begat" pattern of Matthew 1:2 ends at Joseph, and the child is "born" of the woman. -- [L2] anēr (husband) | [L3] Matthew 1:2 "Abraham begat Isaac"

**LINK 3: NARROWED TO:** Luke 1:34 puts the question of manner on the ground "I know not a man", and Luke 1:35 answers with the Holy Ghost, the power of the Highest, and "born of thee", naming no man. I drop the claim that "come upon" and "overshadow" are seed-words by themselves.

**Footing**
- [L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- [L2] *pōs* (G4459), "an interrogative particle of manner; in what way?"

**Presses**
- Luke 1:31, "thou shalt conceive in thy womb". [L2] *syllambanō* (G4815), "to conceive". I grant it is future. [L3] Luke 1:35, also future, gives the Holy Ghost as what follows the angel's word.
- Luke 1:27, "a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David". [L2] *parthenos* (G3933), "virgin". [L3] Deuteronomy 22:23. Luke names her "a virgin" while "espoused", at the time the angel speaks.

[L3] Luke 1:31 says to Mary "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son", with no "bear thee". Elisabeth's trouble is "barren" and "old age". Mary's is "I know not a man". The "also" joins two signs of God's power and does not make the means alike.
- Acts 1:8, "ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you". [L2] *eperchomai* (G1904), "to come upon". I grant it is power. [L3] Luke 1:35 joins it to "the power of the Highest", and the sentence ends in what is "born of thee".

[L3] Luke 1:35: "therefore also that holy thing". The "also" adds the Holy Ghost's coming as a further ground for the title. [L4] "Therefore" follows the clause just before it.
- Acts 13:33, "in that he hath raised up Jesus again". I grant Psalm 2:7 is applied to the raising. I do not rest the conception on Psalm 2:7. [L3] Romans 1:4: "declared [to be] the Son of God with power... by the resurrection from the dead". The resurrection declares the Son, while Luke 1:35 gives the title before it.
- Luke 1:13, "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son". Answered above under Luke 1:36.

**LINK 4: NARROWED TO:** Matthew 1:16 changes the pattern at its last step. **Footing**

**Presses**

- Matthew 1:20, "Joseph, thou son of David". I grant Joseph's descent (Luke 2:4). That is his house, not a begetting of Jesus.
- Luke 3:23, "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph". [L2] *nomizō* (G3543), "to deem", behind "supposed". [L3] Acts 16:13, "where prayer was wont to be made", renders the same root as custom. [L3] Luke 2:44, "But they, supposing him to have been in the company, went a day's journey", renders it as a thought that proved wrong. **LINK 5: NARROWED TO:** The one of whom the child was "born" is the woman (Luke 1:35 "born of thee"; Matthew 1:16 "of whom", feminine). Paul's clause "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" says what the flesh is, so the flesh reaches him as David's seed through her, if Links 1–3 stand. **LINK 6: NARROWED TO:** The conception was by the Holy Ghost apart from a man (Links 1–3 as narrowed). **Presses**

[L3] Ezra 2:62: "These sought their register [among] those that were reckoned by genealogy, but they were not found: therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood." **LINK 1: SUPPORTED.** "Before they came together" (Matthew 1:18) is before the taking into his house (Matthew 1:24).

**Footing**
- [L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- [L2] *synerchomai* (G4905), "to convene, depart in company with, associate with, or (specially), cohabit (conjugally)." *paralambanō* (G3880), "to receive near, i.e. associate with oneself (in any familiar or intimate act or relation)." Both glosses carry "associate with."

- [L3] Deuteronomy 20:7: "And what man [is there] that hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her? let him go and return unto his house, lest he die in the battle, and another man take her."

  - Matthew writes three steps in order: espoused, then "before they came together," then the finding (1:18).
  - The next joining of the two in the chapter is "took unto him his wife" (1:24). That is the receiving near, into his house, which the law also names as a step after betrothal (Deuteronomy 20:7, "betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her").
  - So the "coming together" of 1:18 is the taking of 1:24.
  - The defender's narrowed Link 1 grants this order in its own words: "espoused, found with child of the Holy Ghost, then coming together."

**Presses**
- **Matthew 1:18**, *synerchomai* (G4905), "cohabit (conjugally)."

**LINK 1 [premise 1]: SUPPORTED**

- [L2] *gennaō* (G1080) means "to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother)". The margin gives it as "begotten", and the source named for it is the Holy Ghost.
- [L4] The "for" gives its reason by naming a source for the thing begotten in her, "of the Holy Ghost". The pregnancy was found before any coming together (Matthew 1:18), and Joseph "was minded to put her away privily" because of it (Matthew 1:19). Footing: Matthew 1:18-20 and the lexicon gloss of G1080. The reason removes the cause of that purpose by naming a source other than Joseph.

*Answers to the pressed verses:*

- **2 Samuel 7:14 and 1 Chronicles 28:6.**
  - [L1] 1 Chronicles 28:6: "Solomon thy son, he shall build my house ... for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father."
  - Where a begetter is addressed, the text says "thy son", and God's choosing is added to it.
  - In Matthew 1:21 the angel says: "And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS." There is no "thy son" and no "thee."
  - [L3] Luke 1:13 shows the contrast: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son."
  - The angel gives Zacharias the phrase "bear thee" and gives Joseph only "she shall bring forth".
- **John 1:13 and 1 John 5:1.**
  - [L1] John 1:13: "not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God."
  - The verse itself sets "of God" against "of man". For the men it names, *gennaō* is figurative, "to regenerate" (G1080). The pregnancy of Matthew 1:18 is literal, "found with child".
  - [L1] 1 John 5:1 supplies the same figure: "that begat ... begotten of him".
- **Romans 1:3.**
  - [L1] Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh". *sperma* (G4690) means "seed", and *sarx* (G4561) means "flesh".
  - I hold that the child is of David's seed according to the flesh.
  - [L3] Genesis 3:15: "thy seed and her seed". Seed is there predicated of the woman, with no man named. So Romans 1:3 does not name Joseph.
- **Matthew 1:21, Luke 1:62-63.**
  - [L1] Luke 1:62: "they made signs to his father".
  - Luke calls Zacharias "father" there because Luke 1:13 said "bear thee".
  - [L3] Luke 1:31 gives the same naming act to Mary: "shalt call his name JESUS".
  - [L1] Matthew 1:24 shows that Joseph named him as one "bidden" by the angel. Naming by command is not a statement of begetting.

**LINK 1 [premise 2]: SUPPORTED**

- [L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

- [L2] *dynamis* (G1411) means "miraculous power". [L2] *eperchomai* (G1904) means "to supervene ... come upon".

*Answers to the pressed verses:*

**LINK 2: SUPPORTED**

- [L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

Footing: Matthew 1:18, 1:25, Luke 1:31, 1:34. The KJV gives no human act that could have produced the pregnancy.

*Answers to the pressed verses:*

- **Matthew 1:24, Deuteronomy 20:7, Deuteronomy 22:24.**
  - [L2] *paralambanō* (G3880) means "to receive near, i.e. associate with oneself". Granted, the law calls a betrothed woman a wife, and Matthew 1:20 says "thy wife".
  - Matthew 1:18 itself distinguishes: "espoused to Joseph, before they came together". The label "wife" is not a union.
  - [L1] Luke 2:5: "Mary his espoused wife, being great with child". At the journey Luke still words her state as "espoused".
- **Genesis 4:1.** [L1] "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived". The canon's pattern of begetting is knowing. Matthew 1:25 denies the knowing until the birth, and Luke 1:34 denies it at the annunciation.
- **Matthew 1:19-20.** The row gives "minded to put her away privily" and "while he thought on these things". Either way, the row does not give an act of knowing.
- **Isaiah 7:16, 8:3, 8:4, 8:18.**

  - [L3] Isaiah 7:11: "ask it either in the depth, or in the height above". The Lord's sign is of that scale.
  - Granted, Isaiah 8:18 calls begotten children "signs and ... wonders". It does not make them the sign of 7:14, which is worded "virgin".

**LINK 3: SUPPORTED**

- [L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph". [L2] *nomizō* (G3543) means "to deem by usage".
- [L1] Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus". [L2] *gennaō* (G1080) "properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother".

Luke qualifies Joseph's sonship by "supposed" and does not qualify "his mother". Footing: Matthew 1:16, Luke 3:23, G1080, G3543. So Joseph's fatherhood is by marriage and naming, not by begetting.

*Answers to the pressed verses:*

- **Luke 2:27, 2:41, 2:48.**
  - Granted, Luke 2:27 and 2:41 say "parents". [L1] Luke 2:33 says "Joseph and his mother marvelled", and Luke 2:43 says "Joseph and his mother knew not [of it]".
  - Luke's own narration uses both forms. "Parents" says who has charge of the child. It does not say who begat him.
  - [L1] Luke 2:48: "thy father and I". The child answers at once in Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" That puts the father's name on the other side.
- **Luke 2:51.** [L1] "was subject unto them". Subjection to those in charge does not state begetting. [L3] Luke 2:49 stands directly before it.
- **Matthew 1:3, 1:5.** [L1] Matthew 1:3: "Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar". There the active "begat" names the father alongside the mother. In Matthew 1:16 the active is withheld from Joseph.
- **Matthew 1:17.**
  - [L1] "from the carrying away into Babylon unto Christ [are] fourteen generations".
  - The count tallies a reckoned line. [L3] Ruth 4:10 shows the canon reckoning a child to a name that is not the begetter's: "to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance". [L3] Matthew 1:5 has "Booz begat Obed of Ruth".
- **Acts 16:13.** Granted, *nomizō* (G3543) is a verb of custom. In Luke 3:23 it marks the opinion held about Joseph's sonship and sets it against "Jesus himself".

**LINK 4: NARROWED TO:** Galatians 4:4 and Genesis 3:15 as a supporting pattern, in which a woman is named as the human source and no man is named.

- [L1] Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law".
- [L1] Genesis 3:15: "between thy seed and her seed".
- [L2] *sperma* (G4690) means "seed".
- [L4] In both rows the human source named is a woman. In Galatians 4:4 the sender and the Son's origin is God, "his Son". Footing: Galatians 4:4, Genesis 3:15 and G4690. I grant that Job 14:1, Job 15:14, Matthew 11:11, Genesis 16:10 and Genesis 24:60 are general idioms and prove no exclusion alone. The limb I drop is any claim that "of a woman" by itself excludes a father. The pattern is held with the other links.

**LINK 5: NARROWED TO:** the claim that Luke 3:23-31 gives a David-line which, unlike Matthew 1:12, does not run by "Jechonias begat Salathiel", and which reaches Christ otherwise than by Joseph's begetting. I drop the claim that the KJV states in so many words that Heli is Mary's father.

- [L1] Luke 3:27: "which was [the son] of Salathiel, which was [the son] of Neri". [L1] Matthew 1:12: "Jechonias begat Salathiel". The names recur, but in Luke Salathiel's father is Neri, not Jechonias. So the pressed Luke 3:27 does not touch Jeremiah 22:30: "no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David".
- [L1] Luke 3:31: "which was [the son] of Nathan, which was [the son] of David". Footing: Luke 3:23, 3:27, 3:31 and Matthew 1:12, 1:16.

*Answers to the pressed verses:*

- **Numbers 1:18 and Ezra 2:61-62.**
  - Granted, [L1] Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers".
  - [L1] Ezra 2:61: a priest "which took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name". So the canon gives a man reckoned under his wife's father's name. [L3] Numbers 36:8: "shall be wife unto one of the family of the tribe of her father".

- **Hebrews 7:5, 7:10, 7:14.** [L1] Hebrews 7:14: "our Lord sprang out of Juda". The verse says out of Judah. It does not say through whom.
- **Haggai 2:23, Jeremiah 22:24, Jeremiah 18:8.** Granted, Haggai 2:23 sets Zerubbabel as a signet. That is no reason to put the child on the line Jeremiah 22:30 bars when the Luke line has another route. I hold both verses.
