- [L1] Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- [L1] Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"
- [L2] *gennaō* (G1080) means "to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother)". The margin gives it as "begotten", and the source named for it is the Holy Ghost.
- [L4] The "for" gives its reason by naming a source for the thing begotten in her, "of the Holy Ghost". The pregnancy was found before any coming together (Matthew 1:18), and Joseph "was minded to put her away privily" because of it (Matthew 1:19). Footing: Matthew 1:18-20 and the lexicon gloss of G1080. The reason removes the cause of that purpose by naming a source other than Joseph.

*Answers to the pressed verses:*

- **2 Samuel 7:14 and 1 Chronicles 28:6.**
  - [L1] 1 Chronicles 28:6: "Solomon thy son, he shall build my house ... for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father."
  - Where a begetter is addressed, the text says "thy son", and God's choosing is added to it.
  - In Matthew 1:21 the angel says: "And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS." There is no "thy son" and no "thee."
  - [L3] Luke 1:13 shows the contrast: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son."
  - The angel gives Zacharias the phrase "bear thee" and gives Joseph only "she shall bring forth".
- **John 1:13 and 1 John 5:1.**
  - [L1] John 1:13: "not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God."
  - The verse itself sets "of God" against "of man". For the men it names, *gennaō* is figurative, "to regenerate" (G1080). The pregnancy of Matthew 1:18 is literal, "found with child".
  - [L1] 1 John 5:1 supplies the same figure: "that begat ... begotten of him".
- **Romans 1:3.**
  - [L1] Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh". *sperma* (G4690) means "seed", and *sarx* (G4561) means "flesh".
  - I hold that the child is of David's seed according to the flesh.
  - [L3] Genesis 3:15: "thy seed and her seed". Seed is there predicated of the woman, with no man named. So Romans 1:3 does not name Joseph.
- **Matthew 1:21, Luke 1:62-63.**
  - [L1] Luke 1:62: "they made signs to his father".
  - Luke calls Zacharias "father" there because Luke 1:13 said "bear thee".
  - [L3] Luke 1:31 gives the same naming act to Mary: "shalt call his name JESUS".
  - [L1] Matthew 1:24 shows that Joseph named him as one "bidden" by the angel. Naming by command is not a statement of begetting.

**LINK 1 [premise 2]: SUPPORTED**

- [L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- [L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- [L2] *dynamis* (G1411) means "miraculous power". [L2] *eperchomai* (G1904) means "to supervene ... come upon".
- [L4] The angel's answer to a question about a conception names the Holy Ghost and the power, and names no man. The "therefore" stands in the same verse as those two clauses and follows them. Footing: Luke 1:34-35 and G1411.

*Answers to the pressed verses:*

- **Luke 1:32.** [L1] "the throne of his father David" gives the heir's office. Verse 35 gives the ground for the title "Son of God" after the coming and the overshadowing. [L3] Luke 1:31 says "thou shalt conceive in thy womb", so Mary's conception is future at the angel's word, and the angel names the Holy Ghost as its means.
- **Luke 1:36-37 and Luke 1:13.**
  - [L1] Luke 1:36: "she hath also conceived a son in her old age". [L1] Luke 1:37: "For with God nothing shall be impossible."
  - Elisabeth's sign was given to Zacharias as "bear thee a son" (Luke 1:13). Mary is told "born of thee" (Luke 1:35).
  - Verse 37 follows a question from one who "know[s] not a man" (Luke 1:34).
- **Acts 1:8 and Luke 9:34.** [L1] Acts 1:8: "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you". In Acts 1:8 the Spirit's coming produces power. In Luke 1:35 it is followed by the product, "that holy thing which shall be born of thee." [L1] Luke 9:34: "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them". *episkiazō* (G1982) means "to invest with preternatural influence". It is divine presence, with no man as agent.
- **Psalms 2:7.**
  - [L1] Psalms 2:7: "this day have I begotten thee". [L3] Acts 13:33, Hebrews 5:5 and Hebrews 1:5 apply it with God as the one who begets.
  - The same Matthew 1:20 margin word "begotten" names the Holy Ghost as source. No row puts a man there.

**LINK 2: SUPPORTED**

- [L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- [L1] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son".
- [L1] Luke 1:34: "seeing I know not a man". [L2] *ginōskō* is the verb stated in the present, and Mary speaks it at the angel's word.

Mary says she knows no man when the angel speaks, and the conception is stated as future: "thou shalt conceive" (Luke 1:31). Matthew 1:25 then says "knew her not" up to the birth. Footing: Matthew 1:18, 1:25, Luke 1:31, 1:34. The KJV gives no human act that could have produced the pregnancy.

*Answers to the pressed verses:*

- **Matthew 1:24, Deuteronomy 20:7, Deuteronomy 22:24.**
  - [L2] *paralambanō* (G3880) means "to receive near, i.e. associate with oneself". Granted, the law calls a betrothed woman a wife, and Matthew 1:20 says "thy wife".

**LINK 3: SUPPORTED**

- [L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph". [L2] *nomizō* (G3543) means "to deem by usage".
- [L1] Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus". [L2] *gennaō* (G1080) "properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother".

Luke qualifies Joseph's sonship by "supposed" and does not qualify "his mother". Footing: Matthew 1:16, Luke 3:23, G1080, G3543. So Joseph's fatherhood is by marriage and naming, not by begetting.

*Answers to the pressed verses:*

- **Luke 2:27, 2:41, 2:48.**
  - Granted, Luke 2:27 and 2:41 say "parents". [L1] Luke 2:33 says "Joseph and his mother marvelled", and Luke 2:43 says "Joseph and his mother knew not [of it]".

- **Luke 2:51.** [L1] "was subject unto them". Subjection to those in charge does not state begetting. [L3] Luke 2:49 stands directly before it.
- **Matthew 1:3, 1:5.** [L1] Matthew 1:3: "Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar". There the active "begat" names the father alongside the mother. In Matthew 1:16 the active is withheld from Joseph.

  - [L1] "from the carrying away into Babylon unto Christ [are] fourteen generations".

**LINK 4: NARROWED TO:** Galatians 4:4 and Genesis 3:15 as a supporting pattern, in which a woman is named as the human source and no man is named.

- [L1] Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law".
- [L1] Genesis 3:15: "between thy seed and her seed".
- [L2] *sperma* (G4690) means "seed".
- [L4] In both rows the human source named is a woman. In Galatians 4:4 the sender and the Son's origin is God, "his Son". Footing: Galatians 4:4, Genesis 3:15 and G4690. I grant that Job 14:1, Job 15:14, Matthew 11:11, Genesis 16:10 and Genesis 24:60 are general idioms and prove no exclusion alone. The limb I drop is any claim that "of a woman" by itself excludes a father. The pattern is held with the other links.

**LINK 5: NARROWED TO:** the claim that Luke 3:23-31 gives a David-line which, unlike Matthew 1:12, does not run by "Jechonias begat Salathiel", and which reaches Christ otherwise than by Joseph's begetting. I drop the claim that the KJV states in so many words that Heli is Mary's father.

- [L1] Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph". [L1] Luke 3:23: "the son of Joseph, which was [the son] of Heli". Joseph is given two fathers. Luke's wording carries no "begat" and sits beside "as was supposed". [L2] *gennaō* (G1080) is the verb Matthew uses.
- [L1] Luke 3:27: "which was [the son] of Salathiel, which was [the son] of Neri". [L1] Matthew 1:12: "Jechonias begat Salathiel". The names recur, but in Luke Salathiel's father is Neri, not Jechonias. So the pressed Luke 3:27 does not touch Jeremiah 22:30: "no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David".
- [L1] Luke 3:31: "which was [the son] of Nathan, which was [the son] of David". Footing: Luke 3:23, 3:27, 3:31 and Matthew 1:12, 1:16.

*Answers to the pressed verses:*

- **Numbers 1:18 and Ezra 2:61-62.**
  - Granted, [L1] Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers".
  - [L1] Ezra 2:61: a priest "which took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name". So the canon gives a man reckoned under his wife's father's name. [L3] Numbers 36:8: "shall be wife unto one of the family of the tribe of her father".
  - Ezra 2:62 cuts the other way as well: the register check is why such a line stood.
- **2 Samuel 7:12, Acts 2:30.** [L1] Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh". The loins named are David's. The promise runs through generations, and it does not name Joseph. [L3] Genesis 3:15 names seed of the woman alone. [L2] *osphys* (G3751) means "loins".
- **Hebrews 7:5, 7:10, 7:14.** [L1] Hebrews 7:14: "our Lord sprang out of Juda". The verse says out of Judah. It does not say through whom.
- **Haggai 2:23, Jeremiah 22:24, Jeremiah 18:8.** Granted, Haggai 2:23 sets Zerubbabel as a signet. That is no reason to put the child on the line Jeremiah 22:30 bars when the Luke line has another route. I hold both verses.

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 3, LINK ROUND

# LINK ROUND

**LINK 1 [premise 1]: SUPPORTED**

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost". Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The KJV margin on 1:20 reads "Gr. begotten".
- **[L2]** *Gennaō* (G1080) means "to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother)". Matthew 1:20 puts the Holy Ghost in the place of the source of what is begotten in her. It names no human begetter in that clause.
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son". Luke 1:34: "seeing I know not a man".
- **Answer to the pressed witnesses:**
  - 1 John 5:1, "him also that is begotten of him", and 1 John 3:9, "for his seed remaineth in him". Both speak of persons already living who are "born of God". They are a second birth set beside a first, as John 3:6 shows: "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit." Matthew 1:20 speaks of "that which is conceived in her", the child at its first conception, and gives the Holy Ghost as its source. John 3:6 sets two origins side by side, and Matthew 1:20 names the Spirit's.
  - Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh". *Sperma* (G4690) is "something sown, i.e. seed (including the male 'sperm'); by implication, offspring". It is not limited to the male. Genesis 4:25 has Eve say "God, [said she], hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel", and Genesis 3:15 says "her seed". The offspring of the woman is called seed in the KJV.
  - Matthew 1:20 itself, "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost". It names Joseph as the one told and the Holy Ghost as the source. It does not name Joseph as the source.
- **[L4]** Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 give one source for the conception, the Holy Ghost, with *gennaō* (begotten) placed on him. No row names a human begetter in the account. The word *ek* (of) with the Holy Ghost therefore carries the source of this conception, on Matthew 1:20 with G1080 and Matthew 1:18 with Luke 1:34.

**LINK 1 [premise 2]: SUPPORTED**

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:18 puts the finding "before they came together". Deuteronomy 22:24 treats a man's wife found with another as a case for the gate. The angel's "for" answers the intent of 1:19 with a source: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:20).
- **[L2]** *Gar* (G1063) means "for", the reason given for "fear not".
- **Answer to the pressed witnesses:**
  - 2 Samuel 7:14, "I will be his father, and he shall be my son", and Luke 1:32, "the throne of his father David". These give God as father and David as the remote father. *Patēr* (G3962) means "a 'father' (literally or figuratively, near or more remote)". They fit my link, because the father named near the child in the angel's word is God, not Joseph.
  - 1 Chronicles 28:6, "for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father". *Bachar* (H977) means to choose. That is election of a begotten son. Matthew 1:20 gives no election clause but a conceiving "of the Holy Ghost".
  - Matthew 1:21, "thou shalt call his name JESUS", and Luke 1:62, "And they made signs to his father, how he would have him called." The naming is not the father's act only. Luke 1:31 says to Mary "shalt call his name JESUS". Genesis 4:25 says Eve "called his name Seth". Matthew 1:25 says Joseph "called his name JESUS" after the angel told him to. Naming is done by mother and by one who receives the child.
  - Matthew 1:19, "being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example". I accept both grounds he had. The "for" does not replace them. It answers the one fact that made him minded to put her away: she was with child before they came together (1:18).
- **[L4]** The "for" gives the reason Joseph may take her, namely the source of the conception. It rests on Matthew 1:20 with G1063 and on Matthew 1:18 with Deuteronomy 22:24. It does not rest on the naming act.

**LINK 2: NARROWED TO: Matthew 1:16 breaks the "begat" line at Joseph "the husband of Mary", and the birth clause names only Mary.**

I drop the sentence "the birth is traced through the woman alone" as a rule for every household row, and I keep Luke 2:48 as household usage.

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob". Every earlier name is "begat". The last is not "Joseph begat Jesus" but "Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus". *Gennaō* (G1080) is used for both "begat" and "was born".
- **[L2]** The Greek relative "of whom" in Matthew 1:16 is feminine, so it points to Mary alone. Joseph is named "husband", not "father".
- **Answer to the pressed witnesses:**
  - Matthew 11:11, "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist", Job 14:1, "Man [that is] born of a woman", and Luke 1:13, "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son". I grant these name or imply fathers. They do not make Matthew 1:16 do so, since Matthew 1:16 breaks the "begat" form that Matthew 1:2 sets.
  - Luke 2:48, "behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing". It is household speech, and Luke 2:49 answers it: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" Luke 3:23 marks the opinion: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph". Luke 2:44 uses "supposing him to have been in the company" of a belief that was wrong. The word carries a held opinion, which the narrator corrects.
  - Luke 2:51, "and was subject unto them". Subjection is household order, not descent.
  - Genesis 4:25, "another seed". It is the woman's word, and it fits my premise 1 answer.
- **[L4]** The "begat" chain stops at Joseph, on Matthew 1:16 with Matthew 1:2 and G1080. Luke 3:23 qualifies "son of Joseph" with "as was supposed".

**LINK 3: SUPPORTED**

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." Matthew 1:25: "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son".
- **[L2]** *Synerchomai* (G4905) means "come together". *Ginōskō* (G1097) means to know. Both name the coming together of man and wife, and 1:18 denies it up to the finding, while 1:25 denies it up to the birth.
- **[L3]** Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb". At that point the conception is future. Luke 1:34 says "seeing I know not a man". When the conception is announced, Mary knows no man. Luke 1:35 answers "How shall this be" with the Holy Ghost: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- **Answer to the pressed witnesses:**
  - Matthew 1:24, "and took unto him his wife", with Deuteronomy 20:7, "hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her". I grant the three steps: finding, taking, "knew her not till". The challenger's step, "Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal", needs a coming together before the finding. Matthew 1:18 says "before they came together, she was found with child". Matthew 1:25 says no knowing until the birth. The challenger's step has no place in these two verses.
  - Luke 2:5, "Mary his espoused wife, being great with child". "Espoused" is the word of Matthew 1:18's "espoused to Joseph, before they came together". It keeps the espousal status through to the birth.
  - Acts 1:8, "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you", Luke 9:34, "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them", and Acts 5:15, "the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them". I accept that *eperchomai* (G1904) means "come upon" and *episkiazō* (G1982) means "overshadow", with presence and power. The power is the Holy Ghost's own act, and Luke 1:35 gives it as the answer to Mary's question. It names no man, since "seeing I know not a man" is the question.
  - Luke 1:35, "shall be called the Son of God". *Kaleō* (G2564) in 1:32 and 1:35 is the same verb. But "therefore also" in 1:35 follows the clauses of 1:35 itself, "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee". Its antecedent sits in the same sentence.
- **[L4]** The interval from the finding to the birth has no coming together, on Matthew 1:18 and 1:25 with G4905 and G1097. Luke 1:34 and 1:35 agree.

# LINK ROUND

**LINK 1 [premise 1]: SUPPORTED**

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost". Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The KJV margin on 1:20 reads "Gr. begotten".
- **[L2]** *Gennaō* (G1080) means "to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother)". Matthew 1:20 puts the Holy Ghost in the place of the source of what is begotten in her. It names no human begetter in that clause.
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son". Luke 1:34: "seeing I know not a man".
- **Answer to the pressed witnesses:**
  - 1 John 5:1, "him also that is begotten of him", and 1 John 3:9, "for his seed remaineth in him". Both speak of persons already living who are "born of God". They are a second birth set beside a first, as John 3:6 shows: "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit." Matthew 1:20 speaks of "that which is conceived in her", the child at its first conception, and gives the Holy Ghost as its source. John 3:6 sets two origins side by side, and Matthew 1:20 names the Spirit's.
  - Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh". *Sperma* (G4690) is "something sown, i.e. seed (including the male 'sperm'); by implication, offspring". It is not limited to the male. Genesis 4:25 has Eve say "God, [said she], hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel", and Genesis 3:15 says "her seed". The offspring of the woman is called seed in the KJV.
  - Matthew 1:20 itself, "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost". It names Joseph as the one told and the Holy Ghost as the source. It does not name Joseph as the source.
- **[L4]** Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 give one source for the conception, the Holy Ghost, with *gennaō* (begotten) placed on him. No row names a human begetter in the account. The word *ek* (of) with the Holy Ghost therefore carries the source of this conception, on Matthew 1:20 with G1080 and Matthew 1:18 with Luke 1:34.

**LINK 1 [premise 2]: SUPPORTED**

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:18 puts the finding "before they came together". Deuteronomy 22:24 treats a man's wife found with another as a case for the gate. The angel's "for" answers the intent of 1:19 with a source: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:20).
- **[L2]** *Gar* (G1063) means "for", the reason given for "fear not".
- **Answer to the pressed witnesses:**
  - 2 Samuel 7:14, "I will be his father, and he shall be my son", and Luke 1:32, "the throne of his father David". These give God as father and David as the remote father. *Patēr* (G3962) means "a 'father' (literally or figuratively, near or more remote)". They fit my link, because the father named near the child in the angel's word is God, not Joseph.
  - 1 Chronicles 28:6, "for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father". *Bachar* (H977) means to choose. That is election of a begotten son. Matthew 1:20 gives no election clause but a conceiving "of the Holy Ghost".
  - Matthew 1:21, "thou shalt call his name JESUS", and Luke 1:62, "And they made signs to his father, how he would have him called." The naming is not the father's act only. Luke 1:31 says to Mary "shalt call his name JESUS". Genesis 4:25 says Eve "called his name Seth". Matthew 1:25 says Joseph "called his name JESUS" after the angel told him to. Naming is done by mother and by one who receives the child.
  - Matthew 1:19, "being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example". I accept both grounds he had. The "for" does not replace them. It answers the one fact that made him minded to put her away: she was with child before they came together (1:18).
- **[L4]** The "for" gives the reason Joseph may take her, namely the source of the conception. It rests on Matthew 1:20 with G1063 and on Matthew 1:18 with Deuteronomy 22:24. It does not rest on the naming act.

**LINK 2: NARROWED TO: Matthew 1:16 breaks the "begat" line at Joseph "the husband of Mary", and the birth clause names only Mary.**

I drop the sentence "the birth is traced through the woman alone" as a rule for every household row, and I keep Luke 2:48 as household usage.

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob". Every earlier name is "begat". The last is not "Joseph begat Jesus" but "Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus". *Gennaō* (G1080) is used for both "begat" and "was born".
- **[L2]** The Greek relative "of whom" in Matthew 1:16 is feminine, so it points to Mary alone. Joseph is named "husband", not "father".
- **Answer to the pressed witnesses:**
  - Matthew 11:11, "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist", Job 14:1, "Man [that is] born of a woman", and Luke 1:13, "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son". I grant these name or imply fathers. They do not make Matthew 1:16 do so, since Matthew 1:16 breaks the "begat" form that Matthew 1:2 sets.
  - Luke 2:48, "behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing". It is household speech, and Luke 2:49 answers it: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" Luke 3:23 marks the opinion: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph". Luke 2:44 uses "supposing him to have been in the company" of a belief that was wrong. The word carries a held opinion, which the narrator corrects.
  - Luke 2:51, "and was subject unto them". Subjection is household order, not descent.
  - Genesis 4:25, "another seed". It is the woman's word, and it fits my premise 1 answer.
- **[L4]** The "begat" chain stops at Joseph, on Matthew 1:16 with Matthew 1:2 and G1080. Luke 3:23 qualifies "son of Joseph" with "as was supposed".

**LINK 3: SUPPORTED**

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." Matthew 1:25: "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son".
- **[L2]** *Synerchomai* (G4905) means "come together". *Ginōskō* (G1097) means to know. Both name the coming together of man and wife, and 1:18 denies it up to the finding, while 1:25 denies it up to the birth.
- **[L3]** Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb". At that point the conception is future. Luke 1:34 says "seeing I know not a man". When the conception is announced, Mary knows no man. Luke 1:35 answers "How shall this be" with the Holy Ghost: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- **Answer to the pressed witnesses:**
  - Matthew 1:24, "and took unto him his wife", with Deuteronomy 20:7, "hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her". I grant the three steps: finding, taking, "knew her not till". The challenger's step, "Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal", needs a coming together before the finding. Matthew 1:18 says "before they came together, she was found with child". Matthew 1:25 says no knowing until the birth. The challenger's step has no place in these two verses.
  - Luke 2:5, "Mary his espoused wife, being great with child". "Espoused" is the word of Matthew 1:18's "espoused to Joseph, before they came together". It keeps the espousal status through to the birth.
  - Acts 1:8, "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you", Luke 9:34, "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them", and Acts 5:15, "the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them". I accept that *eperchomai* (G1904) means "come upon" and *episkiazō* (G1982) means "overshadow", with presence and power. The power is the Holy Ghost's own act, and Luke 1:35 gives it as the answer to Mary's question. It names no man, since "seeing I know not a man" is the question.
  - Luke 1:35, "shall be called the Son of God". *Kaleō* (G2564) in 1:32 and 1:35 is the same verb. But "therefore also" in 1:35 follows the clauses of 1:35 itself, "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee". Its antecedent sits in the same sentence.
- **[L4]** The interval from the finding to the birth has no coming together, on Matthew 1:18 and 1:25 with G4905 and G1097. Luke 1:34 and 1:35 agree.

**LINK 4: NARROWED TO: Isaiah 7:14 as the KJV words it, "a virgin shall conceive", which Matthew 1:22-23 says was fulfilled. I drop the claim that the depth-or-height offer of Isaiah 7:11 is itself the sign given.**

- **[L1]** Isaiah 7:14: "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son". Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son".
- **[L2]** H5959 (*almah*, the word behind "virgin" in Isaiah 7:14) is rendered "virgin" by the KJV at Genesis 24:43: "when the virgin cometh forth to draw [water]". Genesis 24:16 describes the same girl as "a virgin, neither had any man known her".
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:22: "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet". Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph".
- **Answer to the pressed witnesses:**
  - Isaiah 7:12, "I will not ask, neither will I tempt the LORD". I grant the offer was refused and the Lord then gave his own sign. The sign is what 7:14 says: a virgin conceiving.
  - Isaiah 7:16, "For before the child shall know to refuse the evil, and choose the good". Isaiah 8:3, "I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son". Isaiah 8:8, "O Immanuel". Isaiah 8:18, "I and the children whom the LORD hath given me [are] for signs and for wonders in Israel". I grant that Isaiah's own children are signs in his day. His wife is called "the prophetess", not "a virgin", so Isaiah 8:3 does not carry the 7:14 wording.
  - Proverbs 30:19, "the way of a man with a maid", and Exodus 2:8, "the maid went and called the child's mother". H5959 is used there of a maid's age and of a man's way. Genesis 24:43 with 24:16 is the row where the KJV gives H5959 as "virgin" with the no-man clause.
- **[L4]** The sign is worded "a virgin shall conceive" in Isaiah 7:14 and "a virgin shall be with child" in Matthew 1:23. Footing: those two verses, H5959 at Genesis 24:43, and Genesis 24:16.

**LINK 6: NARROWED TO: Davidic descent in the flesh is compatible with a mother's line and with Joseph's receiving and naming. I do not assert a row naming Mary's tribe.**

- **[L1]** Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh". Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh".
- **[L2]** *Sperma* (G4690) is "seed... by implication, offspring". Genesis 3:15 says "her seed" of the woman. Genesis 4:25 says "another seed" of Eve's son. Seed in the KJV can be the offspring a woman bears.
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David". Matthew 1:24: "took unto him his wife". Matthew 1:25: "he called his name JESUS". Deuteronomy 25:6: "the firstborn which she beareth shall succeed in the name of his brother [which is] dead, that his name be not put out of Israel."
- **Answer to the pressed witnesses:**
  - Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda". It states the tribe and is silent on the line. Hebrews 7:10 ("in the loins of his father") and 7:5 ("out of the loins of Abraham") are the writer's idiom for Levi in Abraham. They name a remote father and do not decide this question.
  - Numbers 1:18, "by the house of their fathers". It is reckoning by the house. Deuteronomy 25:6 shows the name of the house carried by a son whom another man begot: he "shall succeed in the name of his brother [which is] dead". Name and begetter come apart in the law's own row.
  - Genesis 48:5, "[are] mine". Jacob receives and names Ephraim and Manasseh into his own number. Receiving by naming is the act in Genesis 48:5, and Matthew 1:24 and 1:25 give Joseph the same acts.
  - Ezra 2:62, "therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood", with Ezra 2:61, "was called after their name". The priests there were put out because their register was not found. The row concerns the priesthood and does not state a rule for the house of David.
  - Luke 2:4, "because he was of the house and lineage of David". It names Joseph's house. I grant it. It does not decide the flesh line of the child.
  - Luke 1:36, "thy cousin Elisabeth", with Luke 1:5, "of the daughters of Aaron". Exodus 6:23 has Aaron take "Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab" of Judah, so kinship to Aaron's house does not fix a tribe.
  - John 1:45, "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph". It is Philip's word, like John 6:42, "whose father and mother we know". Luke 3:23 marks it with "as was supposed". *Nomizō* (G3543) is "to deem". Acts 16:13, "where prayer was wont to be made", carries custom, and a custom is a held habit. Luke 2:44's "supposing" is a belief that turned out wrong.
- **[L4]** Descent "according to the flesh" in Romans 1:3 fits an offspring through a woman (G4690, Genesis 3:15), and the house is carried by Joseph's receiving and naming (Deuteronomy 25:6, Matthew 1:24-25).

**LINK 2: NARROWED TO: Matthew 1:16 breaks the "begat" line at Joseph "the husband of Mary", and the birth clause names only Mary.**

I drop the sentence "the birth is traced through the woman alone" as a rule for every household row, and I keep Luke 2:48 as household usage.

**LINK 3: SUPPORTED**

**LINK 6: NARROWED TO: Davidic descent in the flesh is compatible with a mother's line and with Joseph's receiving and naming. I do not assert a row naming Mary's tribe.**

- **Answer to the pressed witnesses:**
  - Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda". It states the tribe and is silent on the line. Hebrews 7:10 ("in the loins of his father") and 7:5 ("out of the loins of Abraham") are the writer's idiom for Levi in Abraham. They name a remote father and do not decide this question.
  - Numbers 1:18, "by the house of their fathers". It is reckoning by the house. Deuteronomy 25:6 shows the name of the house carried by a son whom another man begot: he "shall succeed in the name of his brother [which is] dead". Name and begetter come apart in the law's own row.
  - Genesis 48:5, "[are] mine". Jacob receives and names Ephraim and Manasseh into his own number. Receiving by naming is the act in Genesis 48:5, and Matthew 1:24 and 1:25 give Joseph the same acts.
  - Ezra 2:62, "therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood", with Ezra 2:61, "was called after their name". The priests there were put out because their register was not found. The row concerns the priesthood and does not state a rule for the house of David.

- **Answer to the pressed witnesses:**
  - Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda". It states the tribe and is silent on the line. Hebrews 7:10 ("in the loins of his father") and 7:5 ("out of the loins of Abraham") are the writer's idiom for Levi in Abraham. They name a remote father and do not decide this question.
  - Numbers 1:18, "by the house of their fathers". It is reckoning by the house. Deuteronomy 25:6 shows the name of the house carried by a son whom another man begot: he "shall succeed in the name of his brother [which is] dead". Name and begetter come apart in the law's own row.
  - Genesis 48:5, "[are] mine". Jacob receives and names Ephraim and Manasseh into his own number. Receiving by naming is the act in Genesis 48:5, and Matthew 1:24 and 1:25 give Joseph the same acts.
  - Ezra 2:62, "therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood", with Ezra 2:61, "was called after their name". The priests there were put out because their register was not found. The row concerns the priesthood and does not state a rule for the house of David.

Hebrews 7:10 ("in the loins of his father") and 7:5 ("out of the loins of Abraham") are the writer's idiom for Levi in Abraham. They name a remote father and do not decide this question.

**LINK 1: SUPPORTED**

[L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
[L2] *ginōskō* (G1097) means "to know." Matthew 1:25 uses the same word: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
[L3] Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L3] Genesis 4:1: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived."

[L4] Chain:
1. Genesis 4:1 shows the order for a husband's child: knowing, then conceiving.
2. Matthew 1:25 says Joseph "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." That denies the knowing for the whole pregnancy.
3. Matthew 1:18 says she was "found with child" before they came together.
4. So the rows give the reverse of Genesis 4:1's order. The conception stands before any knowing and through to the birth.

The challenger's premise says Joseph "knew Mary his wife within the espousal." That limb is answered by Matthew 1:25 itself. The only knowing the row allows comes after the birth.

Answers to the pressed rows:
- **Luke 1:31**, "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son." [L2] *syllambanō* (G4815), "to conceive," is future here. Mary's question in Luke 1:34 is also future: "How shall this be." It asks how the coming conception will happen, and its ground is "seeing I know not a man." [L3] Luke 1:27 calls her "a virgin espoused," so a coming husband was in view. The question is pointless if a husband were the means.
- **Luke 1:36**, "she hath also conceived a son in her old age." The "also" attaches to "who was called barren" in the same verse. [L3] Luke 1:37: "For with God nothing shall be impossible." The sign is the impossible done, not the husband.
- **Luke 1:13**, "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son." The angel speaks to the husband and says "bear thee." [L3] Luke 1:31 says "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son," with no "bear thee" to any husband.

- **Genesis 24:16**, "a virgin, neither had any man known her." [L2] *yada'* (H3045) means "to know." The verse gives virgin as the state of not being known. [L3] Matthew 1:23: "a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son." The virgin is the one with child.
- **Genesis 25:21**, "Rebekah his wife conceived." Isaac is named in the verse. In Luke 1:35 no man is named.
- **Matthew 1:24**, "took unto him his wife." [L2] *paralambanō* (G3880) means "to take unto oneself." Matthew 1:25 then bounds the abstinence "till she had brought forth." [L2] *heōs* (G2193) means "until." The taking therefore does not date a conception.
- **Matthew 1:25** and **Genesis 4:1** are answered above.
- **Deuteronomy 20:7**, "hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her." The verse separates betrothal from taking. It places no knowing in the betrothal.

**LINK 2 [premise 2]: SUPPORTED**

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"
[L2] *gennaō* (G1080) means "to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother)." The margin gives this verb.
[L3] Matthew 1:18: "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L3] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

[L4] Chain:
1. The verse names the origin of "that which is conceived in her" as the Holy Ghost, using the verb of begetting.
2. Matthew 1:18 gives the same origin before they came together.
3. Luke 1:35's "therefore" is *dio*, which means "wherefore." It draws the result from the Holy Ghost's coming and overshadowing, and gives that as the reason for the title.

Answers to the pressed rows:
- **Matthew 1:20** names Joseph, the son of David. He is the one addressed and told to take his wife. The "of the Holy Ghost" clause is the reason given to him, and the verb is the margin's begetting-verb for what is in her.
- **1 John 5:1** and **John 1:13**, "born of God." [L2] *gennaō* also means "to regenerate." These are the regenerate's rebirth, and they speak of men already born. Matthew 1:20 speaks of "that which is conceived in her," a thing in the womb.
- **Romans 1:3**, "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." The verse names the line of the flesh and does not name a begetter. [L3] Genesis 3:15 says "her seed," so seed is said of a woman's offspring.
- **Acts 1:8**, "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you." The result there is power. The result in Luke 1:35 is "that holy thing which shall be born of thee." [L2] *dynamis* (G1411) means "power." Luke 1:35 gives both power and the birth in one verse.
- **Luke 9:34** and **Acts 5:15** use the overshadowing verb. In Luke 9:34 a cloud overshadows. In Acts 5:15 Peter's shadow passes. Neither verse has a birth. In Luke 1:35 the verb is bound to "that holy thing which shall be born of thee."

**LINK 2 [premise 3]: SUPPORTED**

2. His mercy lies in not making her "a publick example." There is no example to be made of a wife carrying her husband's child.
3. The angel's "for" in Matthew 1:20 answers the fear with the origin of the conception, "of the Holy Ghost."

# LINK ROUND

**LINK 1: SUPPORTED**

[L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
[L2] *ginōskō* (G1097) means "to know." Matthew 1:25 uses the same word: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
[L3] Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L3] Genesis 4:1: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived."

[L4] Chain:
1. Genesis 4:1 shows the order for a husband's child: knowing, then conceiving.
2. Matthew 1:25 says Joseph "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." That denies the knowing for the whole pregnancy.
3. Matthew 1:18 says she was "found with child" before they came together.
4. So the rows give the reverse of Genesis 4:1's order. The conception stands before any knowing and through to the birth.

The challenger's premise says Joseph "knew Mary his wife within the espousal." That limb is answered by Matthew 1:25 itself. The only knowing the row allows comes after the birth.

Answers to the pressed rows:
- **Luke 1:31**, "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son." [L2] *syllambanō* (G4815), "to conceive," is future here. Mary's question in Luke 1:34 is also future: "How shall this be." It asks how the coming conception will happen, and its ground is "seeing I know not a man." [L3] Luke 1:27 calls her "a virgin espoused," so a coming husband was in view. The question is pointless if a husband were the means.
- **Luke 1:36**, "she hath also conceived a son in her old age." The "also" attaches to "who was called barren" in the same verse. [L3] Luke 1:37: "For with God nothing shall be impossible." The sign is the impossible done, not the husband.
- **Luke 1:13**, "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son." The angel speaks to the husband and says "bear thee." [L3] Luke 1:31 says "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son," with no "bear thee" to any husband.
- **Luke 1:24** names "his wife Elisabeth." Luke 1:35 names the Holy Ghost for Mary, and no husband.
- **Genesis 24:16**, "a virgin, neither had any man known her." [L2] *yada'* (H3045) means "to know." The verse gives virgin as the state of not being known. [L3] Matthew 1:23: "a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son." The virgin is the one with child.
- **Genesis 25:21**, "Rebekah his wife conceived." Isaac is named in the verse. In Luke 1:35 no man is named.
- **Matthew 1:24**, "took unto him his wife." [L2] *paralambanō* (G3880) means "to take unto oneself." Matthew 1:25 then bounds the abstinence "till she had brought forth." [L2] *heōs* (G2193) means "until." The taking therefore does not date a conception.
- **Matthew 1:25** and **Genesis 4:1** are answered above.
- **Deuteronomy 20:7**, "hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her." The verse separates betrothal from taking. It places no knowing in the betrothal.

**LINK 2 [premise 2]: SUPPORTED**

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"
[L2] *gennaō* (G1080) means "to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother)." The margin gives this verb.
[L3] Matthew 1:18: "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L3] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

[L4] Chain:
1. The verse names the origin of "that which is conceived in her" as the Holy Ghost, using the verb of begetting.
2. Matthew 1:18 gives the same origin before they came together.
3. Luke 1:35's "therefore" is *dio*, which means "wherefore." It draws the result from the Holy Ghost's coming and overshadowing, and gives that as the reason for the title.

Answers to the pressed rows:
- **Matthew 1:20** names Joseph, the son of David. He is the one addressed and told to take his wife. The "of the Holy Ghost" clause is the reason given to him, and the verb is the margin's begetting-verb for what is in her.
- **1 John 5:1** and **John 1:13**, "born of God." [L2] *gennaō* also means "to regenerate." These are the regenerate's rebirth, and they speak of men already born. Matthew 1:20 speaks of "that which is conceived in her," a thing in the womb.
- **Romans 1:3**, "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." The verse names the line of the flesh and does not name a begetter. [L3] Genesis 3:15 says "her seed," so seed is said of a woman's offspring.
- **Acts 1:8**, "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you." The result there is power. The result in Luke 1:35 is "that holy thing which shall be born of thee." [L2] *dynamis* (G1411) means "power." Luke 1:35 gives both power and the birth in one verse.
- **Luke 9:34** and **Acts 5:15** use the overshadowing verb. In Luke 9:34 a cloud overshadows. In Acts 5:15 Peter's shadow passes. Neither verse has a birth. In Luke 1:35 the verb is bound to "that holy thing which shall be born of thee."
- **Luke 1:32**, "shall be called the Son of the Highest." The title is given there before Mary asks. Verse 35 then gives the reason for the title: the Holy Ghost's coming. [L2] *kaleō* (G2564) means "to call." The "therefore also" carries the reason forward and does not look back to the throne.
- **1 Chronicles 28:6**, "Solomon thy son." [L3] Matthew 1:6: "David the king begat Solomon." That verse states the begetting. No verse states Joseph's begetting of Jesus. Matthew 1:16 says "of whom was born Jesus."

**LINK 2 [premise 3]: SUPPORTED**

[L1] Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
[L2] *paradeigmatizō* (G3856) means "to make a public example." *boulomai* (G1014) means "to be minded." *dikaios* (G1342) means "just."
[L3] Matthew 1:18: "she was found with child."
[L3] Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

[L4] Chain:
1. Joseph's intent follows the finding in Matthew 1:18.
2. His mercy lies in not making her "a publick example." There is no example to be made of a wife carrying her husband's child.
3. The angel's "for" in Matthew 1:20 answers the fear with the origin of the conception, "of the Holy Ghost."

Answers to the pressed rows:
- **Matthew 1:19** gives the intent and both grounds, and I take it as given.
- **Deuteronomy 22:24**, "his neighbour's wife." The verse is the law's penalty for another man. It calls the betrothed woman a wife, and Matthew 1:19 calls Joseph "her husband." Nothing in either verse places a knowing before Matthew 1:25.
- **Deuteronomy 20:7** is answered under Link 1.
- **2 Samuel 7:14**, "I will be his father." The verse speaks of Solomon, who was begotten (Matthew 1:6). The angel's clause in Matthew 1:20 is the Holy Ghost, not the covenant.
- **Matthew 1:21**, "thou shalt call his name JESUS." The angel gives Joseph the naming. [L3] Matthew 1:25: "he called his name JESUS." Naming takes the child into Joseph's house and gives a legal sonship. It does not tell who begat him.
- **Luke 1:62** and **Luke 1:63** name the father's act of naming. They do not carry the begetting.
- **Hebrews 2:14**, "he also himself likewise took part of the same." The verse says flesh and blood. It does not name a father. [L2] *paraplēsiōs* means "in like manner."
- **Hebrews 2:17**, "in all things it behoved him to be made like unto [his] brethren." The verse gives its own purpose: "that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest." [L3] Hebrews 4:15 says "yet without sin." So "all things" is bounded by its purpose.

**LINK 3: NARROWED TO:** The pattern of Matthew 1:2-16 shifts at 1:16 from "begat" to "of whom was born." Matthew 1:16 therefore lists no begetter of Jesus. The exclusion of Joseph as begetter rests on Matthew 1:18-20, not on 1:16 alone.

[L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
[L2] *gennaō* (G1080) is "to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother)."
[L3] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac." Verses 1:3 and 1:6 keep "begat" with a father as subject.

[L4] Joseph is "the husband of Mary." He is not made the subject of "begat" for Jesus, and the feminine "of whom" carries the birth.

Answers to the pressed rows:
- **Matthew 1:3** and **Matthew 1:6** put a mother beside a father who "begat." In Matthew 1:16 no father is the subject of "begat" for Jesus.
- **Matthew 1:1**, "the son of David." [L2] *huios* (G5207) is a son "used very widely of immediate, remote or figuratively, kinship." [L3] Matthew 1:20 addresses Joseph as "thou son of David" and tells him to take Mary. The "son of David" through the house of Joseph is the legal line.

**LINK 4: SUPPORTED**

[L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
[L2] *nomizō* (G3543) means "to deem, to suppose, to hold by custom."
[L3] Luke 2:44: "But they, supposing him to have been in the company, went a day's journey."
[L3] Luke 2:43: "Joseph and his mother knew not [of it]."

[L4] Chain:
1. Luke uses this verb for a supposition that proved mistaken. The child was not in the company (Luke 2:43-44).
2. In Luke 3:23 the narrator sets "as was supposed" against "the son of Joseph."
3. Luke 1:35 says "that holy thing which shall be born of thee."

Answers to the pressed rows:
- **Acts 16:13**, "where prayer was wont to be made." The KJV renders the same verb as a practice, "wont." In Luke 3:23 it renders it "supposed." The verb takes its sense from its subject and object. Luke's own use in Luke 2:44 is a false supposition.
- **Luke 2:48**, "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Mary speaks in the household's words. [L3] Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" The child answers by moving the word "father" to another.
- **Luke 2:41**, "his parents," and **Luke 2:27**, "the parents brought in the child Jesus." These are the narrator's usage for the household that cared for him. They do not state a begetting.
- **Luke 2:33**, "Joseph and his mother marvelled." The verse names Joseph beside Mary. It does not state a begetting.
- **John 6:42**, "the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know." This is the crowd's own knowledge, in the same verse where they dispute "I came down from heaven."
- **John 1:45**, "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph." Philip speaks as the household was known.
- **1 Chronicles 28:6**, "Solomon thy son... I will be his father." David begat Solomon (Matthew 1:6). Luke 2:49 does not set the two fathers beside each other as 1 Chronicles 28:6 does. It sets one against the other.
- **Luke 1:62**, naming as the father's act. Matthew 1:25 says Joseph "called his name JESUS" after the angel's command in Matthew 1:21. That is the legal act of a father who took the child into his house.

**LINK 6: NARROWED TO:** The rows call the flesh "of the seed of David according to the flesh" and "of a woman," and say "that holy thing which shall be born of thee." The begetting of that flesh is named in Matthew 1:20 as of the Holy Ghost. I drop the claim that a row states Mary's descent from David. The KJV does not give her genealogy in a row.

[L1] Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh."
[L1] Galatians 4:4: "made of a woman."
[L2] *zera'* (H2233), "seed," is said of a woman's offspring in Genesis 3:15 and Genesis 4:25.
[L3] Genesis 3:15: "between thy seed and her seed."
[L3] Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father."

[L4] Chain:
1. "Loins" in Hebrews 7:10 reaches Levi through several generations. The word names a descendant in the line and does not fix the last link as a begetting father.
2. Genesis 3:15 shows a woman's seed.
3. Romans 1:3 and Galatians 4:4 can therefore stand together without Joseph as the begetter.

Answers to the pressed rows:
- **Acts 2:30**, "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ." The subject is God, who "would raise up." The "loins" are the same extended loins as Hebrews 7:10.
- **2 Samuel 7:12**, "which shall proceed out of thy bowels." This is said first of Solomon. [L3] Psalm 132:11, "Of the fruit of thy body." The phrase names descent from David's body and is silent on the last link.
- **Hebrews 7:14**, "it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda." [L3] Luke 2:4 says Joseph was "of the house and lineage of David." The enrolment and legal sonship run through Joseph. That is my own "legal father."
- **Hebrews 7:5**, "though they come out of the loins of Abraham." Levi was in Abraham's loins through intervening generations.
- **Numbers 1:18**, "by the house of their fathers." This is the register, the legal reckoning. It fits Joseph's house reckoning the child legally.
- **Ezra 2:62**, "put from the priesthood." Ezra 2:61-62 concerns a priest's register, reckoned by the fathers. It confirms that the legal register runs through Joseph's house.
- **Genesis 4:25**, "hath appointed me another seed." Eve calls the child her seed.
- **Matthew 11:11** and **Job 14:1**, "born of women." They name the mother. Luke 1:13 names John's father, who is "thy wife... shall bear thee."
- **Luke 1:36**, "thy cousin Elisabeth," with **Luke 1:5**, "of the daughters of Aaron." I take these as given. No row states Mary's descent.

blk:
DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 3, LINK ROUND

# LINK ROUND

**LINK 1: SUPPORTED**

Footing:
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The KJV margin reads "[conceived: Gr. begotten]".
- **[L2]** *gennaō* (G1080, to beget, to procreate, "properly, of the father") stands behind "conceived" in that verse.
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- **[L3]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee."
- **[L4]** The verse says what is begotten in her is "of the Holy Ghost," and the margin gives the verb of begetting. The text therefore names the source of the begetting, and that source is not Joseph. The angel gives it as the ground of "fear not."

Answers to each pressed witness:

- **Matthew 1:20** "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
  - *gar* (G1063, for, because) gives the ground of the command. The ground is the Holy Ghost, not Joseph.
  - Joseph's fear is stated in Matthew 1:19: "was minded to put her away privily."
  - Matthew 1:24 "took unto him his wife" is obedience to the command. It is not a claim to have begotten.
- **John 1:13** "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God."
  - I concede the verse is said of believers (John 1:12). I use it only as the pattern that Scripture sets "of God" against "the will of man" in begetting.
  - Luke 1:34 "seeing I know not a man" and Luke 1:35 apply that contrast to the child's conception.
- **1 John 5:1** "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God: and every one that loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him."
  - *gennaō* with "of" names a begetter in the same verse ("him that begat... begotten of him").
  - The verb in Matthew 1:20 carries the same construction, with "the Holy Ghost" in the begetter's place. The press supports the link.
- **John 3:6** "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit."
  - I accept the two kinds. Luke 1:35 puts the flesh in "that holy thing which shall be born of thee," so the flesh is from the mother.
  - Matthew 1:20 puts the begetting in "the Holy Ghost."
- **Luke 1:32** "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."
  - Luke 1:35 begins "therefore also" (*dio kai*). It stands immediately after "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee," which answers Mary's question in Luke 1:34, "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
  - *kaleō* (G2564, to call) names the title. Luke 1:35 gives the cause of that title as the coming upon and overshadowing.
- **1 Chronicles 28:6** "Solomon thy son... I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father."
  - The cause given there is choice (*bachar*, H977, to select). Luke 1:35 gives a different cause: the Holy Ghost coming and the power overshadowing.
  - In 1 Chronicles 28:6 David is named as the begetter ("thy son"). Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35 name no human begetter.
  - Matthew 1:16 changes the verb at the last link from "begat" to "was born."
- **Acts 1:8** "ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you."
  - *eperchomai* (G1904, to come upon) takes its effect from its own verse. Acts 1:8 states the effect as "power" and "witnesses."
  - Luke 1:35 states the effect as "that holy thing which shall be born of thee."
- **Luke 9:34** "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them."
  - *episkiazō* (G1982) carries the gloss "to invest with preternatural influence."
  - In Luke 1:35 the verb stands with "the power of the Highest" (*dynamis*, G1411, power) and its effect is again the birth "of thee."

**LINK 2: NARROWED TO:** Matthew 1:18 puts the finding with child before the coming together, and Luke 1:31 with Luke 1:34 puts the conception after an announcement made to a woman who knows no man. I drop the claim that the span of *heōs* in Matthew 1:25 reaches back to the conception.

Footing:
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- **[L2]** *synerchomai* (G4905) is glossed "to convene... or (specially), cohabit (conjugally)."
- **[L3]** Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb." The conception is future.
- **[L3]** Luke 1:34: "seeing I know not a man." The present state at the announcement is that no man has known her.
- **[L4]** Conception is future at Luke 1:31, and no man has known her at Luke 1:34. She is found with child at Matthew 1:18 before any coming together. No man's knowing therefore stands between the announcement and the conception.

Answers to each pressed witness:

- **Matthew 1:18** "before they came together, she was found with child."
  - The row dates the finding before the coming together. Matthew's own order is finding first, taking later.
- **Matthew 1:19** "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
  - Joseph is her husband in the espousal. I concede that.
  - A man minded to put her away privily is not acting as one who knows the cause. Matthew 1:20 then tells him the cause is "the Holy Ghost."
- **Matthew 1:24** "took unto him his wife."
  - *paralambanō* (G3880) is the taking after the dream. The conception was already found at Matthew 1:18, before this taking.
- **Matthew 1:25** "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
  - I no longer rest the conception on the span of *heōs*.
- **Deuteronomy 20:7** "hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her."
  - This fits the narrowed link. The woman is betrothed and not yet taken in the interval where the finding falls.
  - Luke 2:5 still calls her "his espoused wife, being great with child."
- **Luke 1:34** "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
  - I grant the present tense states her state at that moment. Luke 1:31 makes the conception future from that moment.

**LINK 1: SUPPORTED**

*Premise: "The signet that was plucked from Coniah is set again on his grandson."*

**Footing**

- **[L1]** Jeremiah 22:24: "[As] I live, saith the LORD, though Coniah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah were the signet upon my right hand, yet would I pluck thee thence."
- **[L2]** "Signet" is *chotham* (H2368), a seal-ring. The same word stands in Haggai 2:23.
- **[L3]** Haggai 2:23: "In that day, saith the LORD of hosts, will I take thee, O Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel, saith the LORD, and will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee, saith the LORD of hosts."
- **[L3]** 1 Chronicles 3:17: "And the sons of Jeconiah; Assir, Salathiel his son, [Salathiel: Heb. Shealtiel]"
- **[L4]** These verses form one chain:
  - Jeremiah 22:24 says the LORD plucks the *chotham* from Coniah.
  - 1 Chronicles 3:17 makes Shealtiel Jeconiah's son.
  - Haggai 2:23 has the LORD set the same *chotham* on "the son of Shealtiel."
  - So what was plucked from Coniah is set on Coniah's grandson, by the LORD's own word.

**Answers to the presses**

- **Jeremiah 22:30** ("no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David").
  - **[L1]** Acts 2:30 says God swore "that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."
  - **[L2]** *Osphys* (G3751) means "procreative power."
  - **[L4]** The sworn throne-sitter is fruit of the loins according to the flesh. The defender's route seats a son received in law while the flesh-seed is barred. That cannot be the son Acts 2:30 swears to seat.
  - **[L3]** Matthew 1:12 shows Coniah's line carrying on: "Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel."
  - The bar of Jeremiah 22:30 is answered where the plucked signet is set again (Haggai 2:23). It fits the link.
- **Haggai 2:23** ("I have chosen thee").
  - **[L2]** "Chosen" is *bachar* (H977). It is the verb of 1 Chronicles 28:6: "for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father."
  - **[L4]** The LORD speaks the choosing word of the Davidic son over Coniah's grandson. My link claims the lifting of the plucking, not a throne-sitting by Zerubbabel. It fits the link.
- **Jeremiah 18:8** ("If that nation, against whom I have pronounced, turn from their evil, I will repent of the evil that I thought to do unto them").
  - **[L4]** The oath of Jeremiah 22:24 is the oath to pluck the signet.
  - **[L3]** Haggai 2:23 sets that signet again, "saith the LORD of hosts."
  - The LORD's own later word answers his own pronounced sentence, which is Jeremiah's rule in 18:8. It fits the link.
- **Matthew 1:16 with 1:12.**
  - **[L1]** Matthew 1:1: "The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David."
  - **[L3]** Matthew writes the line "Jechonias begat Salathiel" (1:12) through "Jacob begat Joseph" (1:16) as that generation.
  - **[L4]** The evangelist heads Jechonias's line with "Jesus Christ, the son of David." He sets the line under the throne promise. It fits the link.

**LINK 2: SUPPORTED**

*Premise: the "therefore also" of Luke 1:35 connects back to verse 32.*

**Footing**

- **[L1]** Luke 1:32: "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David:"
- **[L1]** Luke 1:35: "therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- **[L2]** Both verses carry the same verb in the same form, *klēthēsetai*, from *kaleō* (G2564), "to call."
- **[L4]** The chain runs this way:
  - Verse 32 gives the calling, "Son of the Highest," with "the throne of his father David."
  - Verse 35 repeats the calling with "therefore also."
  - The *dio kai* ("therefore") in v.35 connects back to v.32, not forward to biological divine paternity.
  - The title and the throne of his father David are given in Luke 1:32, before Mary asks "How shall this be" in Luke 1:34.

**Answers to the presses**

- **Luke 1:34 and Luke 1:31.**
  - **[L1]** Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb." The conception is future.
  - **[L2]** Luke 1:34 *andra ou ginōskō* is present indicative: her state at the word.
  - **[L3]** The answer's verbs are the verbs of Acts 1:8: "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you" [power...: or, the power of the Holy Ghost coming upon you]. Luke 24:49 calls this "endued with power from on high."
  - **[L4]** The how-question is answered with the power and presence Luke gives the apostles. The calling is grounded back on verse 32. It fits the link.
- **Matthew 1:20 with its margin.**
  - **[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"
  - **[L3]** 1 John 5:1 uses the same begetting-word with "of God" for believers: "every one that loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him. [is born: Gr. has been born]"
  - **[L3]** John 1:13: "born ... of God."
  - **[L4]** "Begotten ... of" God is the text's word for men who have fathers in the flesh. The same row that carries "of the Holy Ghost" names "Joseph, thou son of David" and "Mary thy wife."
  - **[L3]** Matthew 1:18 ("found with child of the Holy Ghost") carries the same "of."

**LINK 3: SUPPORTED**

*Premise: an answer in verbs of power fits a child of David's loins called God's son, as Solomon was.*

**Footing**

- **[L4]** One verse joins "thy son" (out of David's *me'eh*) and "my son" (chosen). Luke's one speech joins "his father David" (1:32) and "the Son of God" (1:35). The shape is the same: a son of the flesh given the covenant title.

**Answers to the presses**

  - **[L1]** In the same answer the angel names "his father David" (Luke 1:32).
  - **[L3]** Acts 2:30 names that father's "loins."

  - **[L3]** Job 14:1 uses "born of a woman" of all men: "Man [that is] born of a woman [is] of few days, and full of trouble. [few...: Heb. short of days]"

**LINK 4: SUPPORTED**

*Premise: Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal.*

**Footing**

- **[L1]** Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."
- **[L2]** *Osphys* (G3751) means "procreative power."
- **[L3]** 2 Samuel 7:12: "which shall proceed out of thy bowels."
- **[L3]** Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived ... [Cain: that is, Gotten, or, Acquired]"
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband."
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"
- **[L3]** Deuteronomy 22:24: "his neighbour's wife."
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
- **[L4]** The chain:
  - The promised seed comes out of a man's procreative power (Acts 2:30; 2 Samuel 7:12).
  - The text's stated means is the husband knowing his wife (Genesis 4:1).
  - The man the text names as husband, son of David, is Joseph (Matthew 1:19-20).
  - "Till" bounds the not-knowing to the pregnancy after the taking (Matthew 1:25).

**Answers to the presses**

- **Matthew 1:18 ("before they came together").**
  - **[L3]** Matthew 1:24 sets what came together: "took unto him his wife."
  - **[L3]** The law names that step through the defender's own witness, Deuteronomy 20:7: "hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her."
  - **[L4]** "Came together," taken as the taking into his house (cohabiting), dates the finding before the taking. The espousal stands before it. It fits the link.

  - **[L1]** Matthew names the grounds of the intent: "being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example."
  - **[L3]** The angel answers a fear: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife" (1:20). He grounds it ("for") in the child's covenant origin, the "begotten ... of" of 1 John 5:1.

  - **[L2]** *Ou ginōskō* is present indicative.
  - **[L3]** Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive," which is future.
  - **[L1]** Luke 1:27: "a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David."
  - **[L4]** Her state at the word stands before a future conception, inside an espousal to a son of David. It fits the link.
- **Deuteronomy 20:7 ("wife ... not taken").**
  - **[L3]** Deuteronomy 22:24 puts the betrothed under the name "his neighbour's wife." It stones the other man "because he hath humbled his neighbour's wife."
  - **[L4]** The law guards the betrothed as the husband's own wife. Within that bond the knowing is his. It fits the link.
- **Matthew 1:23 with Isaiah 7:14.**
