**LINK 6 [premise 1]: NARROWED TO:** the line is registered in Joseph's house by Joseph's taking and naming, and the flesh-seed of David reaches the child as "made" of the woman. I drop only the sweeping words "with no step needing Joseph's loins" as a claim resting on the registration alone.

- **Registration.**
  - [L1] Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife." Matthew 1:21: "thou shalt call his name JESUS." Matthew 1:25: "he called his name JESUS."
  - [L2] *paralambanō* G3880 (to receive near, to associate with oneself) is the taking. *kaleō* G2564 (to call) is the naming.
  - [L3] Luke 2:4: "because he was of the house and lineage of David."
  - [L4] Joseph, of David's house, takes the child into it and names him. That is registration by the man whose house it is.
- **Flesh-seed.**
  - [L1] Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." Galatians 4:4: "made of a woman."
  - [L2] Both verses use *ginomai* G1096 (to become, be made). Neither uses the begetting verb *gennaō* G1080 (to procreate, properly of the father).
  - [L3] Genesis 3:15: "between thy seed and her seed."
  - [L4] The same "made of" names the woman as the source of the child's flesh and the seed of David as its stock. Matthew 1:18, Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35 put the conception "of the Holy Ghost." Joseph's begetting is therefore not the channel. By elimination, the Davidic flesh came through the woman. DG-61 does not require a row that states it.
- **Hebrews 7:10.** [L1] "For he was yet in the loins of his father." [L2] *patēr* G3962 (father, near or more remote) shows "father" can be a remote ancestor. [L4] Levi's loins-presence came through generations of fathers and mothers, so loins-language does not require Joseph's act at each step.
- **Ezra 2:61-62.** [L1] The man "was called after their name" and so lost his place. [L3] Luke 1:27 and Luke 2:4 keep Joseph's own name and house unchanged. The Ezra case is a priest dropping his own father's name, so it does not parallel a child named into the house of the man who took him.

**LINK 6 [premise 2]: SUPPORTED.**
- [L1] Jeremiah 22:30: "Write ye this man childless... for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David."
- [L2] *kiy* H3588 (for, because) is the "for" that explains "childless." *zera'* H2233 (seed) is the word that stands barred.
- [L3] Matthew 1:12: "Jechonias begat Salathiel." Matthew 1:17: "from the carrying away into Babylon unto Christ."
- [L4] "Childless" is explained by the "for" clause. It means no seed of his prospers on the throne, so Salathiel's birth does not contradict it. The genealogy that runs from Jechonias to Christ passes through Joseph (Matthew 1:16). A child of Joseph's loins would therefore be Jeconiah's seed.
- **Haggai 2:23.** [L1] "will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee." The promise is to Zerubbabel personally. [L3] Jeremiah 22:24 ("I live, saith the LORD") is sworn, and Haggai does not say a seed sits on the throne.
- **Jeremiah 18:8.** [L1] The rule is conditional: "If that nation... turn from their evil." Jeremiah 22:30 states no such condition.

**LINK 6 [premise 3]: SUPPORTED.**
- [L1] Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"
- [L2] *gennaō* G1080 (to procreate, properly of the father) is the margin's "begotten." The verb that names the father's act is given "of the Holy Ghost."

**LINK 6 [premise 1]: NARROWED TO:** the line is registered in Joseph's house by Joseph's taking and naming, and the flesh-seed of David reaches the child as "made" of the woman. I drop only the sweeping words "with no step needing Joseph's loins" as a claim resting on the registration alone.

- **Registration.**
  - [L1] Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife." Matthew 1:21: "thou shalt call his name JESUS." Matthew 1:25: "he called his name JESUS."
  - [L2] *paralambanō* G3880 (to receive near, to associate with oneself) is the taking. *kaleō* G2564 (to call) is the naming.
  - [L3] Luke 2:4: "because he was of the house and lineage of David."
  - [L4] Joseph, of David's house, takes the child into it and names him. That is registration by the man whose house it is.
- **Flesh-seed.**
  - [L1] Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." Galatians 4:4: "made of a woman."
  - [L2] Both verses use *ginomai* G1096 (to become, be made). Neither uses the begetting verb *gennaō* G1080 (to procreate, properly of the father).
  - [L3] Genesis 3:15: "between thy seed and her seed."
  - [L4] The same "made of" names the woman as the source of the child's flesh and the seed of David as its stock. Matthew 1:18, Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35 put the conception "of the Holy Ghost." Joseph's begetting is therefore not the channel. By elimination, the Davidic flesh came through the woman. DG-61 does not require a row that states it.
- **Hebrews 7:10.** [L1] "For he was yet in the loins of his father." [L2] *patēr* G3962 (father, near or more remote) shows "father" can be a remote ancestor. [L4] Levi's loins-presence came through generations of fathers and mothers, so loins-language does not require Joseph's act at each step.
- **Ezra 2:61-62.** [L1] The man "was called after their name" and so lost his place. [L3] Luke 1:27 and Luke 2:4 keep Joseph's own name and house unchanged. The Ezra case is a priest dropping his own father's name, so it does not parallel a child named into the house of the man who took him.

**LINK 6 [premise 2]: SUPPORTED.**
- [L1] Jeremiah 22:30: "Write ye this man childless... for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David."
- [L2] *kiy* H3588 (for, because) is the "for" that explains "childless." *zera'* H2233 (seed) is the word that stands barred.
- [L3] Matthew 1:12: "Jechonias begat Salathiel." Matthew 1:17: "from the carrying away into Babylon unto Christ."
- [L4] "Childless" is explained by the "for" clause. It means no seed of his prospers on the throne, so Salathiel's birth does not contradict it. The genealogy that runs from Jechonias to Christ passes through Joseph (Matthew 1:16). A child of Joseph's loins would therefore be Jeconiah's seed.
- **Haggai 2:23.** [L1] "will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee." The promise is to Zerubbabel personally. [L3] Jeremiah 22:24 ("I live, saith the LORD") is sworn, and Haggai does not say a seed sits on the throne.
- **Jeremiah 18:8.** [L1] The rule is conditional: "If that nation... turn from their evil." Jeremiah 22:30 states no such condition.

**LINK 6 [premise 3]: SUPPORTED.**
- [L1] Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"
- [L2] *gennaō* G1080 (to procreate, properly of the father) is the margin's "begotten." The verb that names the father's act is given "of the Holy Ghost."
- [L3] Matthew 1:18: "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost," before they came together.
- [L4] The "for" gives the reason Joseph need not fear. That reason is the source of the conception. If Joseph were the source, the reason would give him nothing.
- **Luke 1:13.** [L1] "Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard." The ground there is the prayer. The ground in Matthew 1:20 is the source.
- **1 John 5:1 and John 1:13.** [L2] *gennaō* is "figuratively, to regenerate." [L3] 1 John 5:1 speaks of believers: "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God." That is a second birth, and Matthew 1:20 is a first conception.
- **Hebrews 2:14-17.** [L1] "took part of the same... took on [him] the seed of Abraham." These verses name sharing flesh and blood, not the manner of origin. [L1] Hebrews 2:17 ties likeness to the office: "that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest."
- **2 Samuel 7:14 and 1 Chronicles 28:6.** The sonship there is by choice: "I have chosen him [to be] my son." Luke 1:35 differs: "that holy thing which shall be born of thee."

**LINK 2: SUPPORTED.**
- [L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- [L2] *ginōskō* G1097 (to know) is the verb behind Mary's "know." [L3] Genesis 4:1: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived."
- [L4] The question asks the means. The answer gives the Holy Ghost's coming and the power's overshadowing, and Joseph is not named. The "therefore also" follows the Holy Ghost and power clause in the same verse. If the answer were "by Joseph after the wedding," the question would be idle.
- **Luke 1:36-37.** [L1] Elisabeth was "called barren." That is the impossible case Luke 1:37 meets. [L4] "also" sets her beside Mary as two works of God. Her conception was by her husband (Luke 1:13). Mary's question is about having no man. The angel names Elisabeth as the lesser sign and gives Mary the greater answer.
- **Acts 1:8 and Luke 9:34.** [L1] "come upon you" and "overshadowed them" are God's power and presence. [L3] Luke 1:35 joins "the power of the Highest" to the overshadowing. That is the power that supplies where no man's act is.
- **Acts 13:33.** [L1] "this day have I begotten thee" is applied to the resurrection. [L3] Hebrews 5:5 repeats it. The title can have several grounds, and Luke 1:35's "therefore also" adds one.

**LINK 3: SUPPORTED.**
- [L1] Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."

A conception by an ordinary husband is no sign from the Lord himself.

**LINK 4: SUPPORTED.**

- [L2] *paradeigmatizō* G3856 (to expose to infamy) is the "public example." *dikaios* G1342 (equitable, just) is "just."

- **Luke 2:48 and Luke 2:27, 33, 41.** [L2] *patēr* G3962 is "father (literally or figuratively, near or more remote)," so the word does not by itself mean begetter. [L3] Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" The child sets his Father against Mary's "thy father," which is the household title of the man who took and named him (Matthew 1:24-25).
- **John 1:45, John 6:42, Luke 4:22.** [L1] John 6:42: "whose father and mother we know? how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?" These are the words of the crowd and of Philip, not of the angel.
- **Luke 3:23.** [L1] "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph." Luke sets this in parentheses as what was supposed. [L3] Luke 1:35 gives his own earlier account of the source.

**LINK 6 [premise 1]: NARROWED TO:** the line is registered in Joseph's house by Joseph's taking and naming, and the flesh-seed of David reaches the child as "made" of the woman. I drop only the sweeping words "with no step needing Joseph's loins" as a claim resting on the registration alone.

- **Registration.**
  - [L1] Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife." Matthew 1:21: "thou shalt call his name JESUS." Matthew 1:25: "he called his name JESUS."
  - [L2] *paralambanō* G3880 (to receive near, to associate with oneself) is the taking. *kaleō* G2564 (to call) is the naming.
  - [L3] Luke 2:4: "because he was of the house and lineage of David."
  - [L4] Joseph, of David's house, takes the child into it and names him. That is registration by the man whose house it is.
- **Flesh-seed.**
  - [L1] Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." Galatians 4:4: "made of a woman."
  - [L2] Both verses use *ginomai* G1096 (to become, be made). Neither uses the begetting verb *gennaō* G1080 (to procreate, properly of the father).
  - [L3] Genesis 3:15: "between thy seed and her seed."
  - [L4] The same "made of" names the woman as the source of the child's flesh and the seed of David as its stock. Matthew 1:18, Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35 put the conception "of the Holy Ghost." Joseph's begetting is therefore not the channel. By elimination, the Davidic flesh came through the woman. DG-61 does not require a row that states it.
- **Hebrews 7:10.** [L1] "For he was yet in the loins of his father." [L2] *patēr* G3962 (father, near or more remote) shows "father" can be a remote ancestor. [L4] Levi's loins-presence came through generations of fathers and mothers, so loins-language does not require Joseph's act at each step.
- **Ezra 2:61-62.** [L1] The man "was called after their name" and so lost his place. [L3] Luke 1:27 and Luke 2:4 keep Joseph's own name and house unchanged. The Ezra case is a priest dropping his own father's name, so it does not parallel a child named into the house of the man who took him.

**LINK 6 [premise 2]: SUPPORTED.**
- [L1] Jeremiah 22:30: "Write ye this man childless... for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David."

- [L3] Matthew 1:12: "Jechonias begat Salathiel." Matthew 1:17: "from the carrying away into Babylon unto Christ."
- [L4] "Childless" is explained by the "for" clause. It means no seed of his prospers on the throne, so Salathiel's birth does not contradict it. The genealogy that runs from Jechonias to Christ passes through Joseph (Matthew 1:16). A child of Joseph's loins would therefore be Jeconiah's seed.
- **Haggai 2:23.** [L1] "will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee." The promise is to Zerubbabel personally. [L3] Jeremiah 22:24 ("I live, saith the LORD") is sworn, and Haggai does not say a seed sits on the throne.
- **Jeremiah 18:8.** [L1] The rule is conditional: "If that nation... turn from their evil." Jeremiah 22:30 states no such condition.

**LINK 6 [premise 3]: SUPPORTED.**
- [L1] Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"
- [L2] *gennaō* G1080 (to procreate, properly of the father) is the margin's "begotten." The verb that names the father's act is given "of the Holy Ghost."
- [L3] Matthew 1:18: "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost," before they came together.
- [L4] The "for" gives the reason Joseph need not fear. That reason is the source of the conception. If Joseph were the source, the reason would give him nothing.
- **Luke 1:13.** [L1] "Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard." The ground there is the prayer. The ground in Matthew 1:20 is the source.
- **1 John 5:1 and John 1:13.** [L2] *gennaō* is "figuratively, to regenerate." [L3] 1 John 5:1 speaks of believers: "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God." That is a second birth, and Matthew 1:20 is a first conception.
- **Hebrews 2:14-17.** [L1] "took part of the same... took on [him] the seed of Abraham." These verses name sharing flesh and blood, not the manner of origin. [L1] Hebrews 2:17 ties likeness to the office: "that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest."
- **2 Samuel 7:14 and 1 Chronicles 28:6.** The sonship there is by choice: "I have chosen him [to be] my son." Luke 1:35 differs: "that holy thing which shall be born of thee."

**LINK 2: SUPPORTED.**
- [L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- [L2] *ginōskō* G1097 (to know) is the verb behind Mary's "know." [L3] Genesis 4:1: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived."
- [L4] The question asks the means. The answer gives the Holy Ghost's coming and the power's overshadowing, and Joseph is not named. The "therefore also" follows the Holy Ghost and power clause in the same verse. If the answer were "by Joseph after the wedding," the question would be idle.
- **Luke 1:36-37.** [L1] Elisabeth was "called barren." That is the impossible case Luke 1:37 meets. [L4] "also" sets her beside Mary as two works of God. Her conception was by her husband (Luke 1:13). Mary's question is about having no man. The angel names Elisabeth as the lesser sign and gives Mary the greater answer.
- **Acts 1:8 and Luke 9:34.** [L1] "come upon you" and "overshadowed them" are God's power and presence. [L3] Luke 1:35 joins "the power of the Highest" to the overshadowing. That is the power that supplies where no man's act is.
- **Acts 13:33.** [L1] "this day have I begotten thee" is applied to the resurrection. [L3] Hebrews 5:5 repeats it. The title can have several grounds, and Luke 1:35's "therefore also" adds one.

**LINK 3: SUPPORTED.**

- **Isaiah 8:3.** [L1] The child there is named "Mahershalalhashbaz." Isaiah 7:14 names "Immanuel," so the child there is a different child with a different name. [L1] Isaiah 7:11, 14: "Ask thee a sign of the LORD thy God... the Lord himself shall give you a sign." [L2] Matthew 1:23 quotes it with *parthenos* G3933 (a maiden; an unmarried daughter). A conception by an ordinary husband is no sign from the Lord himself.

**LINK 4: SUPPORTED.**

- [L2] *paradeigmatizō* G3856 (to expose to infamy) is the "public example." *dikaios* G1342 (equitable, just) is "just."

- [L4] The "public example" fear exists only if the child is another man's. A just man who knew he was the father would have neither the fear nor the putting away. The verse's "will" verbs state his decision, and its grounds ("just," "public example") show what he took the conception to be.
- **Luke 2:48 and Luke 2:27, 33, 41.** [L2] *patēr* G3962 is "father (literally or figuratively, near or more remote)," so the word does not by itself mean begetter. [L3] Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" The child sets his Father against Mary's "thy father," which is the household title of the man who took and named him (Matthew 1:24-25).
- **John 1:45, John 6:42, Luke 4:22.** [L1] John 6:42: "whose father and mother we know? how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?" These are the words of the crowd and of Philip, not of the angel.
- **Luke 3:23.** [L1] "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph." Luke sets this in parentheses as what was supposed. [L3] Luke 1:35 gives his own earlier account of the source.

- [L4] The "for" gives the reason Joseph need not fear. That reason is the source of the conception. If Joseph were the source, the reason would give him nothing.
- **Luke 1:13.** [L1] "Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard." The ground there is the prayer. The ground in Matthew 1:20 is the source.
- **1 John 5:1 and John 1:13.** [L2] *gennaō* is "figuratively, to regenerate." [L3] 1 John 5:1 speaks of believers: "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God." That is a second birth, and Matthew 1:20 is a first conception.
- **Hebrews 2:14-17.** [L1] "took part of the same... took on [him] the seed of Abraham." These verses name sharing flesh and blood, not the manner of origin. [L1] Hebrews 2:17 ties likeness to the office: "that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest."
- **2 Samuel 7:14 and 1 Chronicles 28:6.** The sonship there is by choice: "I have chosen him [to be] my son." Luke 1:35 differs: "that holy thing which shall be born of thee."

**LINK 2: SUPPORTED.**
- [L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- [L2] *ginōskō* G1097 (to know) is the verb behind Mary's "know." [L3] Genesis 4:1: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived."
- [L4] The question asks the means. The answer gives the Holy Ghost's coming and the power's overshadowing, and Joseph is not named. The "therefore also" follows the Holy Ghost and power clause in the same verse. If the answer were "by Joseph after the wedding," the question would be idle.
- **Luke 1:36-37.** [L1] Elisabeth was "called barren." That is the impossible case Luke 1:37 meets. [L4] "also" sets her beside Mary as two works of God. Her conception was by her husband (Luke 1:13). Mary's question is about having no man. The angel names Elisabeth as the lesser sign and gives Mary the greater answer.
- **Acts 1:8 and Luke 9:34.** [L1] "come upon you" and "overshadowed them" are God's power and presence. [L3] Luke 1:35 joins "the power of the Highest" to the overshadowing. That is the power that supplies where no man's act is.
- **Acts 13:33.** [L1] "this day have I begotten thee" is applied to the resurrection. [L3] Hebrews 5:5 repeats it. The title can have several grounds, and Luke 1:35's "therefore also" adds one.

**LINK 3: SUPPORTED.**
- [L1] Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
- [L3] Matthew 1:24: "and took unto him his wife."
- [L4] There is no window for a knowing by Joseph. Before the taking she was already with child (Matthew 1:18, 20). After the taking he "knew her not" until the birth (Matthew 1:25). The challenger's "within the espousal" is placed against Matthew 1:18-19, where the pregnancy is found and Joseph is minded to put her away.
- **Luke 1:34, present tense.** [L2] *ginōskō* is in the present tense, but the question is about the means of a conception to come. [L1] Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb." [L4] A woman about to be married would not ask "how" if marriage were the means.
- **Deuteronomy 22:24.** [L1] "his neighbour's wife." [L4] That law punishes the betrothed's lying with another man. Matthew 1:19 shows Joseph facing exactly that law (see LINK 4).
- **Isaiah 8:3.** [L1] The child there is named "Mahershalalhashbaz." Isaiah 7:14 names "Immanuel," so the child there is a different child with a different name. [L1] Isaiah 7:11, 14: "Ask thee a sign of the LORD thy God... the Lord himself shall give you a sign." [L2] Matthew 1:23 quotes it with *parthenos* G3933 (a maiden; an unmarried daughter). A conception by an ordinary husband is no sign from the Lord himself.

**LINK 4: SUPPORTED.**
- [L1] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
- [L2] *paradeigmatizō* G3856 (to expose to infamy) is the "public example." *dikaios* G1342 (equitable, just) is "just."
- [L3] Deuteronomy 22:24: the betrothed who lay with another is stoned.
- [L4] The "public example" fear exists only if the child is another man's. A just man who knew he was the father would have neither the fear nor the putting away. The verse's "will" verbs state his decision, and its grounds ("just," "public example") show what he took the conception to be.
- **Luke 2:48 and Luke 2:27, 33, 41.** [L2] *patēr* G3962 is "father (literally or figuratively, near or more remote)," so the word does not by itself mean begetter. [L3] Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" The child sets his Father against Mary's "thy father," which is the household title of the man who took and named him (Matthew 1:24-25).
- **John 1:45, John 6:42, Luke 4:22.** [L1] John 6:42: "whose father and mother we know? how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?" These are the words of the crowd and of Philip, not of the angel.
- **Luke 3:23.** [L1] "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph." Luke sets this in parentheses as what was supposed. [L3] Luke 1:35 gives his own earlier account of the source.

---

**CHALLENGER'S UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES**

1. The inference that the one Davidic man named is therefore the source of the child's Davidic flesh, which props the keystone. Challenger's words: "Once Mary's descent is conceded, the rows name one Davidic man in that house, and he is Joseph."
PRESSED WITH:
Matthew 1:16 "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ." -- MEANS: the "begat" chain stops at Joseph, and the child is "born" of her. -- [L2] gennaō G1080 (to procreate, properly of the father; by extension of the mother) | [L3] Matthew 1:2 "Abraham begat Isaac"
Matthew 1:20 "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]" -- MEANS: the begetting is assigned to the Holy Ghost, not to the Davidic man. -- [L2] gennaō G1080 (to procreate, properly of the father) | [L3] Matthew 1:18 "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost"
Galatians 4:4 "made of a woman" -- MEANS: the child's being made came of the woman. -- [L2] ginomai G1096 (to become, be made) | [L3] Romans 1:3 "made of the seed of David according to the flesh"
Romans 1:3 "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh" -- MEANS: the seed of David is "made," not begotten, and it is not tied to a man's act. -- [L2] ginomai G1096 (to become, be made) | [L3] Genesis 3:15 "thy seed and her seed"
Hebrews 7:10 "For he was yet in the loins of his father" -- MEANS: loins-descent runs through remote ancestors, not only direct begetting. -- [L2] patēr G3962 (father, near or more remote) | [L3] Acts 2:30 "of the fruit of his loins"
Ezra 2:62 "therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood" -- MEANS: it concerns a man's own descent lost by taking another house's name, not a child named by the man whose house it is. -- [L3] Ezra 2:61 "was called after their name" | [L3] Luke 2:4 "because he was of the house and lineage of David"

PRESSED WITH:

Matthew 1:25 "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" -- MEANS: no knowing from the taking until the birth. -- [L3] Matthew 1:24 "took unto him his wife" | [L3] Genesis 4:1 "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived"
Matthew 1:19 "was minded to put her away privily" -- MEANS: a husband who knew himself the father had no cause to put her away. -- [L2] paradeigmatizō G3856 (to expose to infamy) | [L3] Deuteronomy 22:24 "because he hath humbled his neighbour's wife"
Luke 1:35 "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee" -- MEANS: the answer to how names God's coming and power, not a husband. -- [L2] ginōskō G1097 (to know) in Luke 1:34 | [L3] Luke 1:34 "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

3. The inference that Isaiah's sign came by a husband's approach. Challenger's words: "The sign came by a husband's approach."
PRESSED WITH:
Isaiah 7:14 "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel." -- MEANS: the sign is a conception by a virgin. -- [L2] parthenos G3933 (a maiden; an unmarried daughter), the word Matthew 1:23 uses | [L3] Isaiah 7:11 "ask it either in the depth, or in the height above"
Isaiah 8:3 "Call his name Mahershalalhashbaz." -- MEANS: the child of Isaiah 8:3 bears a different name from Immanuel. -- [L3] Isaiah 7:14 "shall call his name Immanuel" | [L3] Matthew 1:23 "Behold, a virgin shall be with child"
Luke 1:27 "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph" -- MEANS: Mary is named a virgin before the conception. -- [L2] parthenos G3933 (a maiden; an unmarried daughter) | [L3] Matthew 1:23 "Behold, a virgin shall be with child"

PRESSED WITH:

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 3, LINK ROUND

# LINK ROUND

**LINK 1: SUPPORTED**

**Footing.**
- [L1] Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- [L2] *ek* (G1537), "out of," is the preposition behind "of the Holy Ghost." It names the source.
- [L1] Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The margin reads "Gr. begotten."
- [L2] *gennaō* (G1080) means "to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother)."
- [L4] The thing begotten in her has the Holy Ghost as its source, and the finding is dated "before they came together." A covenant act dated after a person exists cannot supply that source. A conception can, so the dating stands on Matthew 1:18 and the lexical ground together.

**Answers to the pressed verses.**
- **Matthew 1:20** ("Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost"). The row has two parts. The address "thou son of David" names the house Joseph brings to the taking. The "for" clause gives the source of the thing conceived. 2 Samuel 7:14 ("I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men") is spoken to David of a seed who may sin. Luke 1:35 names the one conceived "that holy thing."
- **Luke 1:15** ("he shall be filled with the Holy Ghost, even from his mother's womb"). [L2] The verb is "filled with," said of a person already there. Matthew 1:20 says the thing conceived is "of" (*ek*) the Holy Ghost. Filling and source are different words in different verses.
- **Jeremiah 1:5** ("Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee"). God knows and sanctifies one he says he "formed." Jeremiah 1:1 names his father. The verse does not call him "of" God.
- **1 Chronicles 22:10** ("he shall be my son, and I [will be] his father"). [L3] 1 Chronicles 28:6 gives the ground of that sonship: "I have chosen him [to be] my son." Sonship by choice is the stated ground there. Luke 1:35 grounds the title on the conception ("therefore also").
- **1 John 5:1** ("every one that loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him") and **John 1:13** ("Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God"). [L2] *gennaō* is used figuratively there, "to regenerate." John 1:13 sets "of God" against "of the will of man." Matthew 1:18 states a physical finding, "found with child."
- **Acts 1:8, 1 Samuel 16:13, Luke 9:34, Acts 5:15.** I grant that "come upon" and "overshadow" can mean empowerment and presence. Each verse is read with its stated result. Acts 1:8 gives "ye shall receive power... ye shall be witnesses." Luke 1:35 gives "that holy thing which shall be born of thee." The Holy Ghost's coming upon David in 1 Samuel 16:13 produces no conception. Luke 1:35's coming produces one.
- **Luke 1:35** ("therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God"). [L2] *dio kai* ("wherefore also") sits inside Luke 1:35, after "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee." The reason it gives for the title is that coming and overshadowing. Luke 1:32 gives the title, and Luke 1:35 gives its ground.
- **Luke 1:36-37** ("she hath also conceived a son in her old age"; "For with God nothing shall be impossible"). Luke 1:36 says Elisabeth "was called barren." Her conception is the sign offered for a greater work. Luke 1:35 answers Mary's "seeing I know not a man" (Luke 1:34) with "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee."

---

**LINK 2: SUPPORTED**

**Footing.**
- [L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" [L2] *ginōskō* (G1097) is "to know." It is in the present tense, said before the conception.
- [L1] Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb." The conception is future from that moment.
- [L3] Luke 1:35 answers the "how" with "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee." The means given is not a man.
- [L3] Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- [L4] The question assumes her present not-knowing. The answer gives a source other than a man. The finding is dated before any coming together. So the conception has no male parent.

**Answers to the pressed verses.**
- **Luke 1:34:** granted as present tense. The chain above rests on that tense plus Luke 1:31's future "shalt conceive" and Luke 1:35's answer.
- **Matthew 1:24** ("took unto him his wife") and **Matthew 1:25** ("And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son"). [L2] *paralambanō* (G3880) is "to receive near." I grant that the taking opens the span of 1:25. Matthew 1:18 dates the pregnancy "before they came together," so the pregnancy precedes the taking. Joseph's knowing is excluded from the taking to the birth by 1:25, and from before the finding by 1:18. The challenger's "Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal" has no moment left.
- **Genesis 4:1** ("Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived") and **Genesis 4:25** ("And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son"). The ordinary means is the husband knowing his wife. Mary's "I know not a man" (Luke 1:34) names that means as absent. Luke 1:35 names another means.
- **Deuteronomy 22:24** ("his neighbour's wife") and **Luke 2:5** ("Mary his espoused wife"). I grant that the betrothed is a wife in law. Luke 2:5 also calls her "espoused," and Matthew 1:18 says "before they came together." A wife in law who had not come together is stated by the text itself.
- **Matthew 1:19** ("Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily"). I grant that justice and mercy are his stated grounds. A just man who found his wife with child (Matthew 1:18) took her to be with child by another. [L3] Matthew 1:20 then answers that ground: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." If he knew himself the father, "of the Holy Ghost" would answer nothing. The fear of Luke 1:13 and Luke 1:30 is a response to the angel's appearing. Luke 1:12 says "when Zacharias saw him, he was troubled, and fear fell upon him." Matthew 1:20's fear carries its object: "to take unto thee Mary thy wife."
- **Isaiah 8:3, 8:4, 8:18, 7:16, 7:14.** Isaiah 8:3 says "I went unto the prophetess" (margin "approached"), and the child is called "Mahershalalhashbaz." Isaiah 7:14 gives "Immanuel" and "a virgin shall conceive." [L3] Genesis 24:16 defines "virgin" as "a virgin, neither had any man known her," and Genesis 24:43 uses the same noun for Rebekah. [L2] *'oth* (H226), "a sign," is the same word in 7:14 and 8:18. The content of the sign in 7:14 is the virgin's conceiving. The child of 8:3-4 comes through a "going" to the prophetess.

---

**LINK 3: NARROWED TO: Matthew 1:16 breaks the genealogy's verb for Jesus. Joseph is "the husband of Mary," and Jesus is "born" "of whom," that is, of Mary. Luke 3:23's "as was supposed" marks Joseph's fatherhood as one of reckoning.**

I drop the sweeping form of the quoted sentence. The narrowed limb stands as follows.

**Footing.**
- [L1] Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus." [L3] Matthew 1:12: "Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel." Every earlier link has the father as the subject of "begat."
- [L2] *gennaō* (G1080) is "to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother)." It is active ("begat") in the links before Jesus and passive ("was born") for Jesus. The relative "whom" is feminine singular and points to Mary.
- [L4] Joseph is called "the husband of Mary" and is not named as subject of a "begat" for Jesus. The line of fathers ends at Joseph, and Jesus is born of Mary.

**Answers to the pressed verses.**
- **Matthew 1:3** ("Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar") and **Matthew 1:5** ("Booz begat Obed of Ruth"). I grant that "of" names the mother beside a begetting father. In those verses the begetting father is the subject. In 1:16 the verb passes to "was born," and Joseph is not its subject.
- **Matthew 11:11** ("Among them that are born of women"). I grant it is said of men who had fathers. My narrowed link does not rest on "born of women" alone. It rests on the changed verb of 1:16 and the "for" of 1:20.
- **Luke 3:23** ("being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph"). [L2] *nomizō* (G3543) is to deem by usage. [L3] Acts 16:13 ("where prayer was wont to be made") gives the usage sense. Acts 14:19 gives the same verb in a case that proved false: "supposing he had been dead." Acts 14:20 shows Paul "rose up." The parenthesis marks what was supposed.
- **Luke 2:48** ("thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing"). Mary's word is answered at once in **Luke 2:49**: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" The child sets another Father against hers. Luke 2:50 adds, "And they understood not the saying which he spake unto them."
- **Luke 2:41** ("his parents") and **Luke 2:27** ("when the parents brought in the child Jesus"). It is the household word. The same pen writes "Joseph and his mother" (Luke 2:33) and "as was supposed" (Luke 3:23).
- **John 6:42** ("whose father and mother we know? how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?"). The speakers disbelieve the very claim in the same verse. They give the town's reckoning. **John 1:45** is Philip's wording, "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph," and the "supposed" of Luke 3:23 qualifies the reckoning.
- **Matthew 1:21** ("thou shalt call his name JESUS") and **Luke 1:62** ("they made signs to his father"). [L3] Luke 1:31 says to Mary, "shalt call his name JESUS." Genesis 4:25 says of Eve, "called his name Seth." Naming is spoken to Mary and done by Eve. It is not a father's act only. Matthew 1:25 ("he called his name JESUS") records Joseph's obedience.

---

**LINK 4: NARROWED TO: God is the child's Father by the conception of Luke 1:35 and by his own word at Luke 2:49. Joseph is the husband and the reckoned father ("as was supposed," Luke 3:23). Hebrews 2's likeness is stated for suffering and high priesthood.**

**Footing.**
- [L1] Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" [L3] Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." The child answers Mary's "thy father" with "my Father's."
- [L1] Luke 1:35: "therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." [L2] *dio kai* ("wherefore also") grounds the title on the Holy Ghost's coming.
- [L4] The child names God as his Father in reply to "thy father." Luke 1:35 grounds the title on the conception. Luke 3:23 marks Joseph's fatherhood as supposed.

**Answers to the pressed verses.**
- **1 Chronicles 28:6** ("I have chosen him [to be] my son") and **2 Samuel 7:14** ("I will be his father, and he shall be my son"). [L2] *'ab* (H1) is "father, in a literal and immediate, or figurative and remote application." Solomon's sonship is by choice and may be chastened "with the rod of men." The title in Luke 1:35 is "therefore" from the conception.
- **Luke 1:32** ("shall be called the Son of the Highest"). The title is given there. Luke 1:35 gives its ground ("therefore also").
- **Psalm 2:7** ("Thou [art] my Son; this day have I begotten thee"). The verse begins "I will declare the decree." **Acts 13:33** ("in that he hath raised up Jesus again") and **Hebrews 5:5** are about the day he is declared and installed. **Hebrews 1:5** asks "unto which of the angels said he at any time," so it is a title above angels.
- **Romans 1:4** ("declared [to be] the Son of God with power... by the resurrection from the dead"). The margin reads "declared: Gr. determined." **Romans 1:3** says "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David." He is "his Son" before he is "made of the seed." [L3] John 6:42 has the child say "I came down from heaven."
- **Hebrews 2:14** ("he also himself likewise took part of the same"). The children "are partakers" and he "took part." The verb is his own act of taking. **Hebrews 2:16** ("he took on [him] the seed of Abraham") names the seed he took.
- **Hebrews 2:17** ("in all things it behoved him to be made like unto [his] brethren"). The verse states its purpose: "that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest." [L3] Hebrews 4:15 gives the exception: "in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin."
- **Psalm 139:13** ("thou hast covered me in my mother's womb") and **Hebrews 10:5** ("when he cometh into the world, he saith... a body hast thou prepared me"). In Hebrews 10:5 the speaker "cometh into the world" and speaks of a body prepared for "me." David in Psalm 139:13 describes God covering him in the womb as one who began there.

---

**LINK 5 [premise 5]: NARROWED TO: Numbers 1:18's reckoning "by the house of their fathers" is a registry in which a house's name passes to a child by law. "Sprang out of Juda" in Hebrews 7:14 names the tribe he arose from. I drop the claim that Numbers 1:18 itself states the taking.**

**Footing.**
- [L1] Deuteronomy 25:6: "the firstborn which she beareth shall succeed in the name of his brother which is dead, that his name be not put out of Israel." A child begotten by one man is reckoned in another's name.
- [L1] Genesis 48:5: "Ephraim and Manasseh... are mine; as Reuben and Simeon, they shall be mine." Jacob takes his grandsons into the register.
- [L3] Ezra 2:61: "which took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name." A name passes by taking.
- [L4] The registry of the house of the fathers (Numbers 1:18) admits names passing by law and not by loins alone. Joseph is "of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4), and he took Mary (Matthew 1:24).

**Answers to the pressed verses.**
- **Hebrews 7:14** ("our Lord sprang out of Juda"). [L2] *anatellō* (G393) is "to (cause to) arise." [L3] Matthew 5:45 says "he maketh his sun to rise" with the same verb. The sense is arising, and the verse is about the tribe.
- **Numbers 1:18** and **Numbers 1:2.** [L2] *yalad* (H3205) is "to bear young... to beget... to show lineage... declare pedigrees... be the son of." The verse says "by the house of their fathers." **Footing.**

**Answers to the pressed verses.**
- **Matthew 1:20** ("Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost"). The row has two parts. The address "thou son of David" names the house Joseph brings to the taking. The "for" clause gives the source of the thing conceived. 2 Samuel 7:14 ("I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men") is spoken to David of a seed who may sin. Luke 1:35 names the one conceived "that holy thing."

[L2] *gennaō* is used figuratively there, "to regenerate." John 1:13 sets "of God" against "of the will of man." Matthew 1:18 states a physical finding, "found with child."
- **Acts 1:8, 1 Samuel 16:13, Luke 9:34, Acts 5:15.** I grant that "come upon" and "overshadow" can mean empowerment and presence. Each verse is read with its stated result. Acts 1:8 gives "ye shall receive power... ye shall be witnesses." Luke 1:35 gives "that holy thing which shall be born of thee." The Holy Ghost's coming upon David in 1 Samuel 16:13 produces no conception. Luke 1:35's coming produces one.

[L2] *dio kai* ("wherefore also") sits inside Luke 1:35, after "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee." The reason it gives for the title is that coming and overshadowing. Luke 1:32 gives the title, and Luke 1:35 gives its ground.

Her conception is the sign offered for a greater work. Luke 1:35 answers Mary's "seeing I know not a man" (Luke 1:34) with "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee."

**LINK 2: SUPPORTED**

**Footing.**

**Answers to the pressed verses.**
- **Luke 1:34:** granted as present tense. The chain above rests on that tense plus Luke 1:31's future "shalt conceive" and Luke 1:35's answer.

I grant that the taking opens the span of 1:25. Matthew 1:18 dates the pregnancy "before they came together," so the pregnancy precedes the taking. **LINK 1: SUPPORTED**

Matthew 1:20 [L1]: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]". Matthew 1:18 [L3]: "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." Luke 1:35 [L3]: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee".

[L4] Matthew 1:18 dates that source "before they came together," and Matthew 1:20 and 1:18 together name one source. The chain is: the begetting verb (L2), the source named in 1:20 (L1), and the date in 1:18 (L3).

*Presses answered:*

- John 1:13, "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God." [L2] The verse names three human sources: *haima* (G129, blood, "kindred"), *thelēma* (G2307, will) and *anēr* (G435, "a man... husband"). The verse sets "of God" against the male source. The believers' birth is *gennaō* in its figurative sense, "to regenerate" (G1080), and it comes after "received him" and "power to become" (John 1:12 [L3]). Matthew 1:20 is the literal sense, with "in her" and "before they came together" (1:18). That is the fit, and it is not a second origin added to a father's.
- 1 John 5:1, "every one that loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him." The subjects are "Whosoever believeth," and the margin reads "has been born." That is a birth after believing.
- 1 John 3:9, "for his seed remaineth in him." [L2] *menō* (G3306, to abide) shows *sperma* (G4690) there as an indwelling nature. This is the figurative use, and Matthew 1:20 has a womb.
- John 3:6, "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit." For the child, the flesh is "born of thee" (Luke 1:35 [L3]) and the Spirit is "come upon thee." That fits my link and gives no male seed.
- Romans 1:4, "according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead." Paul's "declared" is set "by the resurrection." Romans 1:3 reads "made of the seed of David": *ginomai* (G1096, to become) with *sperma* (G4690, "by implication, offspring"). Offspring in 2 Samuel 7:12 [L3] is "thy seed... which shall proceed out of thy bowels," and it is descent. Both orders are granted and neither names Joseph's seed.

**LINK 2: SUPPORTED**

Luke 1:34 [L1]: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" Luke 1:35 [L1]: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." Luke 1:37 [L3]: "For with God nothing shall be impossible."

[L2] *epérchomai* (G1904, "to supervene... influence") and *episkiázō* (G1982, "to invest with preternatural influence") name God's power on Mary. *dió* ("therefore") in 1:35 ties the title to the coming upon, in the same sentence.

[L4] Mary asks "How" (1:34). The reply opens with the agent (1:35) and ends with 1:37. The chain is: the question (L1), the agent verbs (L2), the "therefore" and the closing verse (L3).

*Presses answered:*

- Luke 1:32, "shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David". Verse 32 states the title. Verse 35 states the ground, "therefore also." Both stand, and the covenant does not remove the ground given to Mary's "How."
- Acts 1:8, "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you". Luke 9:34, "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them". Acts 5:15, "the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them". In each, God's power or presence comes upon and the effect follows. In Luke 1:35 the effect is "that holy thing which shall be born of thee."
- Luke 1:36, "she hath also conceived a son in her old age: and this is the sixth month with her, who was called barren." The "also" joins two conceptions as signs of God's power. Elisabeth's is placed on a named husband (Luke 1:13 [L3], "shall bear thee a son"). Mary's is answered with "come upon thee" after "I know not a man."

**LINK 3: NARROWED TO:** the conception is "of the Holy Ghost" and found "before they came together." I drop any claim about the word "virgin" alone.

**LINK 4: NARROWED TO:** Joseph's naming and the greeting "son of David" do not prove begetting. Joseph receives the child by the angel's word. I drop "guardian" as a separate claim.

- Luke 1:13 and 1:63. The angel's "thou shalt call" is the same act given to Mary in Luke 1:31.

- Luke 2:33, "Joseph and his mother marvelled," and Luke 2:43, "Joseph and his mother knew not [of it]." These are the narrator's own words, and they name "Joseph."

**LINK 6: NARROWED TO:** the flesh-descent from David is carried by the woman out of whom the child is born. The legal house is Joseph's (Luke 2:4), and I grant that.

[L4] The chain is: David's promise (Acts 2:30), its address to Mary (Luke 1:32 and 1:35), and the two fathers named for Joseph (Luke 3:23 and Matthew 1:16).

*Presses answered:*

Ezra 2:62, "put from the priesthood." These are the register by the father's house, and I grant it as the legal reckoning. My narrowed link concerns the flesh.

# LINK ROUND: CHALLENGER

---

**LINK 1: SUPPORTED.**

Premise (my words, kept): "An espoused damsel who had not yet been taken speaks truly in the present tense, and the conceiving the angel names lies ahead (Luke 1:31)."

**Footing**
- **[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- **[L2]** *syllambanō* (G4815), "to clasp... specially, to conceive," stands future in Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS." *ginōskō* (G1097, to know) in Luke 1:34 gives her state when the angel spoke.
- **[L3]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David." She is espoused when the angel comes. Deuteronomy 20:7: "that hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her." Betrothal comes first and the taking follows.
- **[L4]** The angel speaks to a virgin espoused to Joseph (Luke 1:27). She states her present state (Luke 1:34), and the angel names the conceiving as future (Luke 1:31). The defender granted that Luke 1:31 is future to Luke 1:34. The conceiving therefore falls within the espousal, where the rows call them husband and wife: "Joseph her husband" (Matthew 1:19), "Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20), "his neighbour's wife" (Deuteronomy 22:24). The canon's stated means of conceiving is the husband's knowing: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived" (Genesis 4:1). "Knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" (Matthew 1:25) bounds the abstinence to the pregnancy after the taking (Matthew 1:24). So, at [L4] on those rows, Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal.

**Answers to the presses**

MEANS [CR3] P1.1: "the conceiving ahead is answered by the Holy Ghost's coming"
- **[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- **[L2]** *eperchomai* (G1904, to come upon) is the verb of Acts 1:8: "ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses." There the coming brings power upon persons, who then do the act ("ye shall be witnesses"). *episkiazō* (G1982, to overshadow) is the cloud of Luke 9:34, "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them," and the shadow of Acts 5:15, "the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them." In both rows it is presence over persons.
- **[L3]** Luke 1:32 gives the title and the throne first: "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David." Luke 1:36 then sets Mary beside Elisabeth with "also": "thy cousin Elisabeth, she hath also conceived a son." Elisabeth's son came to her husband: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son" (Luke 1:13).
- **[L4]** Luke 1:35 answers "How shall this be" with power and presence upon the woman, as Acts 1:8 gives power upon the apostles for their own act. The "therefore also" (*dio kai*) in Luke 1:35 connects back to Luke 1:32, where the title and "the throne of his father David" were already given before Mary's question. So 1:35 answers what the child shall be called. The conceiving remains Luke 1:31's "thou shalt conceive in thy womb," set beside Elisabeth's conceiving by her husband (Luke 1:13, 1:36). The Holy Ghost's coming fits the conceiving ahead as power upon her, and it fits the link.

MEANS [CR3] P1.2: "her three months at Elisabeth's lie between the angel's word and the finding"
- **[L1]** Luke 1:56: "And Mary abode with her about three months, and returned to her own house."
- **[L2]** *menō* (to abide) with *hypostrephō* (to return): after the abode she returns to "her own house," the house of an espoused damsel not yet taken (Deuteronomy 20:7, "hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her").
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." Matthew 1:24 names the step that "came together" points to: "took unto him his wife."
- **[L4]** I grant the order the defender gives: the angel's word, three months at Elisabeth's, the return home, then the finding. Every point in that order lies within "espoused to Joseph" (Matthew 1:18). "Before they came together" dates the finding before the taking of Matthew 1:24, the step Deuteronomy 20:7 separates from betrothal. The three months therefore sit inside the espousal, where she is "Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20). The press fits the link: it places the span within the espousal the link names.

---

**LINK 2: NARROWED TO:** The sign of Isaiah 7:14 is given in Isaiah's day, bounded by Isaiah 7:16's time-measure. The children Isaiah names as signs came in his own house through his approach to the prophetess (Isaiah 8:3, 8:18). Matthew's fulfilment falls on a virgin espoused to a husband (Luke 1:27; Matthew 1:20). I drop any claim that the child of Isaiah 8:3 bears the name Immanuel.

**Footing**
- **[L1]** Isaiah 8:3: "And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son." Margin: "went: Heb. approached."
- **[L2]** *qârab* (H7126), "to approach... join, be near." *nᵉbîyʼâh* (H5031), "a prophetess... by association a prophet's wife."
- **[L3]** Isaiah 8:18: "Behold, I and the children whom the LORD hath given me [are] for signs and for wonders in Israel." Isaiah 7:16: "For before the child shall know to refuse the evil, and choose the good, the land that thou abhorrest shall be forsaken of both her kings."
- **[L4]** The sign's own measure is set in Isaiah's day (7:16). Isaiah calls the children given him "signs" (8:18), and they came by the prophet's approach to his wife (8:3). The sign-children of Isaiah's day came through a husband.

**Answers to the presses**

MEANS [CR3] P2.1: "the sign-child of Isaiah 8 is named differently from Immanuel"
- **[L1]** Isaiah 8:8: "the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel."
- **[L2]** *qârâʼ* (H7121, to call, to give a name) stands in Isaiah 7:14, "shall call his name Immanuel," with the 1611 margin "or, thou, O virgin, shalt call." It stands again in Isaiah 8:3, "Call his name Mahershalalhashbaz."
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:21 and 1:23 give one child two names. "Thou shalt call his name JESUS" (1:21) and "they shall call his name Emmanuel" (1:23, margin "or, his name shall be called"), and 1:25 ends "he called his name JESUS."
- **[L4]** In Matthew one child carries a given name, JESUS, and a sign-name, Emmanuel. A difference of names therefore fits one sign. Isaiah 8:8 addresses Immanuel inside the Assyrian overflow of Isaiah's own day ("he shall pass through Judah"). I keep only the limb that the sign stands in Isaiah's day among the children given to the prophet (8:18). The two names fit the narrowed link.

MEANS [CR3] P2.2: "the KJV's "virgin" carries the unknown-by-man sense in its cross-reference"
- **[L1]** Genesis 24:43: "when the virgin cometh forth to draw [water]."
- **[L2]** *'almah* (H5959) is the word here and in Isaiah 7:14. The KJV gives the same word as "maid" at Exodus 2:8 ("the maid went and called the child's mother"), as "damsels" at Psalm 68:25, and as "maid" at Proverbs 30:19 ("the way of a man with a maid"). Genesis 24:16 uses a second word, *bethulah* (H1330, virgin), and adds its own clause: "a virgin, neither had any man known her."
- **[L3]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph." Isaiah 7:14: "a virgin shall conceive."
- **[L4]** I hold the KJV's "virgin" at Isaiah 7:14 as written. It names the woman's state when the word is given, and the verb that follows, "shall conceive," is future to that state. Luke 1:27 gives the same order: "a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph," to whom the angel then says "thou shalt conceive" (Luke 1:31). **Answers to the presses**

MEANS [CR3] P3.1: "the verb is *anatellō*, not the loins word of Hebrews 7:5"
- **[L1]** Hebrews 7:14: "our Lord sprang out of Juda."
- **[L2]** *anatellō* (G393, to rise, spring up) is the root of *anatolē* (G395), "a rising of light... dayspring, east," the word of Matthew 2:1 ("wise men from the east"). The verb names the springing. Its source is the phrase *ex Iouda*, "out of Juda."
- **[L3]** Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father." Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh."
- **[L4]** The same chapter gives the source of a tribe's springing as the father's loins (7:5, 7:10). Acts 2:30 gives Christ's springing as "the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh." *anatellō* names the rising and *ek* names what he rose out of: Judah, measured by loins. The verb fits the link.

MEANS [CR3] P3.2: "a register reckons a child to a house by name, not only by begetting"
- **[L1]** Deuteronomy 25:6: "the firstborn which she beareth shall succeed in the name of his brother [which is] dead."
- **[L2]** *shem* (H8034, name, "a mark or memorial of individuality") rides on "the firstborn which she beareth," a begotten firstborn of the dead man's own house, his brother's child.
- **[L3]** Genesis 48:5: "thy two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, which were born unto thee... [are] mine." These are Jacob's grandsons, born to his son Joseph.
- **[L4]** In both rows the name-reckoning sits on a begetting inside the same seed line: a brother's firstborn in Deuteronomy 25:6 and a son's sons in Genesis 48:5. The register reckons by name within a line already carried by begetting. That fits the link: the name of Judah's house is carried by the loins of Judah's house.

MEANS [CR3] P3.3: "the reckoning to Joseph is a supposal"
- **[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was [the son] of Heli."
- **[L2]** *nomizō* (G3543), "properly, to do by law (usage), i.e. to accustom... deem or regard: suppose, be wont." *enomizeto* is the same form as Acts 16:13: "where prayer was wont to be made." There the custom held true, for "we sat down, and spake unto the women which resorted [thither]."
- **[L3]** Luke 2:48, in the same writer: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Luke 2:41: "his parents went to Jerusalem every year." Luke 2:4: "he was of the house and lineage of David."
- **[L4]** The verb carries reckoning by usage of law. Context decides its truth: it is false at Luke 2:44 and true at Acts 16:13. Luke's own context reckons Joseph as father: Mary's "thy father" (2:48), the narrator's "his parents" (2:41), and Joseph "of the house and lineage of David" (2:4). The reckoning of Luke 3:23 stands with those rows and fits the link.

---

**LINK 4: SUPPORTED.**

Premise (kept): The woman bears, and the seed is David's.

**Footing**
- **[L1]** Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh."
- **[L2]** *sperma* (G4690, seed) with *kata sarka* (G4561, "flesh... as the means of kindred"). *osphys* (G3751, loins) in Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh."
- **[L3]** 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels." Luke 1:27: "a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David."
- **[L4]** The seed proceeds out of David's body (2 Samuel 7:12) and comes down by loins (Acts 2:30). The man of David's house to whom the bearer is espoused is named "Joseph, of the house of David" (Luke 1:27) and "Joseph, thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20). The woman bears, and the seed is David's through the named man of his house.

**Answers to the presses**

MEANS [CR3] P4.1: "the source named is the woman"
- **[L1]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law."
- **[L2]** *gynē* (G1135), "a woman; specially, a wife." The woman named is the wife the angel names: "Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20).
- **[L3]** The defender granted that "of a woman" is said of men with fathers: Job 14:1, "Man [that is] born of a woman," and Matthew 11:11, "them that are born of women... John the Baptist," whose father is named in Luke 1:13. Genesis 4:25: "Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son... another seed."
- **[L4]** The woman is the bearer, as Eve bore Seth whom Adam begat (Genesis 4:25). The same verse sets him "made under the law," the law that counts "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:2). The woman as the one who bears fits the seed through the man, and it fits the link.

MEANS [CR3] P4.2: "the begetting verb takes the Holy Ghost as source"
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:20, whole: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." Margin: "conceived: Gr. begotten."
- **[L2]** *gennaō* (G1080), "to procreate... figuratively, to regenerate," with *ek* (out of). The same *ek* with God is said of believers: "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God" (1 John 5:1), and John 1:13 "born... of God." Those believers were men born of fathers in the flesh.
- **[L3]** John 3:6: "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit." 2 Samuel 7:14: "I will be his father, and he shall be my son," spoken of David's seed "out of thy bowels" (7:12).
- **[L4]** Within one row the angel names "Joseph, thou son of David," "Mary thy wife," and "of the Holy Ghost." The *gar* (for) grounds the command "fear not to take." The child is the seed God claims as his own, "I will be his father" (2 Samuel 7:14), the covenant-origin marker. *ek* with God stands beside fleshly fathers in 1 John 5:1 and John 1:13. The two kinds stay two, as John 3:6 keeps them. So "of the Holy Ghost" fits the son of David named in the same row, and it fits the link.

MEANS [CR3] P4.3: "David is called the child's father in the angel's word to Mary"
- **[L1]** Luke 1:32: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."
- **[L2]** *patēr* (G3962), "a 'father' (literally or figuratively, near or more remote)." David is the remote father.
- **[L3]** Luke 1:27, the same scene: "a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David." Luke 2:4: "of the house and lineage of David."
- **[L4]** A remote father's seed comes by the near fathers of his house. In this scene Luke attaches "of the house of David" to "a man whose name was Joseph" (1:27). Luke 1:32 gives the title and throne before Mary's question in 1:34. The remote father David fits the near father of David's house, and it fits the link.

---

**LINK 5: NARROWED TO:** Matthew 1:19 states Joseph's intent and its two grounds: "being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example." The angel answers that intent with "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife." The release Joseph intended (*apoluō*) fits a husband sparing his wife the public showing that the finding of Matthew 1:18 brought. I drop the limb "whatever he knew."

**Footing**
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
- **[L2]** *paradeigmatizō* (G3856), "to show alongside (the public), i.e. expose to infamy." *apoluō* (G630), "to free fully... relieve, release, dismiss... set at liberty." *lathra* (G2977), "privately."
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:18: "she was found with child." Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife."
- **[L4]** The finding of a child before the taking (1:18) brought the risk of public showing. A just husband, unwilling to expose her, was minded to release her privately (1:19). The angel answers a fear of taking ("fear not to take"). Joseph then "took unto him his wife" (1:24). The narrowed link stands on the verse's own two grounds and the angel's own answer.

**Answers to the presses**

MEANS [CR3] P5.1: "Joseph's purpose was divorce, which a husband who knew himself the father had no cause for"
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
- **[L2]** *apoluō* (G630) carries "release... set at liberty" as well as divorce. *paradeigmatizō* (G3856) gives the cause the verse itself names: unwillingness to expose her to infamy.
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child." Deuteronomy 22:24: "ye shall bring them both out unto the gate of that city." The law brings a betrothed damsel's case to the public gate.
- **[L4]** The verse names its own cause: justness and unwillingness to make her a public example. A child found before the taking (1:18) set a betrothed wife before the gate of Deuteronomy 22:24. That exposure lay on the finding, and the finding came before the taking whoever the father was. A just husband releasing her privily spares her that showing. The angel then meets his fear, "fear not to take," and grounds the taking in the covenant claim on the child (1:20). That is a cause the verse states, and it fits the narrowed link.

MEANS [CR3] P5.2: "the knowing of a betrothed damsel there is by a man other than her husband, and it is stoned"
- **[L1]** Deuteronomy 22:24: "the man, because he hath humbled his neighbour's wife: so thou shalt put away evil from among you."
- **[L2]** *'ishshâh* (H802), "a woman... wife." The law names the betrothed damsel "wife."
- **[L3]** Genesis 4:1: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived." Matthew 1:20: "Mary thy wife."
- **[L4]** I grant the verse's case: another man, stoned at the gate. What the row gives my link is its word for the betrothed, "wife," and its public gate, which is the "publick example" Joseph was unwilling to make (Matthew 1:19). A husband's knowing of his own wife is the knowing Genesis 4:1 names. The stoning falls on "his neighbour's" act, and the husband's own wife is "Mary thy wife." It fits the narrowed link.

---

**LINK 6: NARROWED TO:** The signet the LORD swore to pluck from Coniah (Jeremiah 22:24) the LORD himself sets on Coniah's grandson: "will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee" (Haggai 2:23). The throne is the LORD's to give to David's seed (Luke 1:32; Acts 2:30). I drop the claim that Jeremiah 18:8 is the instrument.

**Footing**
- **[L1]** Haggai 2:23: "will I take thee, O Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel, saith the LORD, and will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee."
- **[L2]** *bāchar* (H977, to choose) is the LORD's election verb, the same verb the defender named at 1 Chronicles 28:6, "I have chosen him [to be] my son."
- **[L3]** Jeremiah 22:24: "though Coniah... were the signet upon my right hand, yet would I pluck thee thence." Matthew 1:12: "Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel."
- **[L4]** The same LORD and the same signet appear in both rows. He plucks it from Coniah and sets it, by choosing, on Coniah's seed (Matthew 1:12). Coniah's seed carries the LORD's chosen signet, and the throne rests on the LORD's gift: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David" (Luke 1:32).

**Answers to the presses**

MEANS [CR3] P6.1: "the pronounced sentence is on Coniah's seed on David's throne"
- **[L1]** Jeremiah 22:30: "a man [that] shall not prosper in his days: for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David, and ruling any more in Judah."
- **[L2]** *zera'* (H2233, seed). The sentence on the man is bounded "in his days." The sentence on his seed concerns "sitting... and ruling any more in Judah."
- **[L3]** Acts 2:30: "he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne." Matthew 1:16 carries Coniah's line to "Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
- **[L4]** The LORD who pronounced the sentence is the LORD who gives the throne: "the Lord God shall give" (Luke 1:32), "he would raise up Christ to sit" (Acts 2:30). Matthew sets Coniah's line in Christ's own record (1:12, 1:16). The sitting is God's raising, and the signet is already restored within that seed (Haggai 2:23). The sentence and the gift both stand in the LORD's mouth, and the gift fits the narrowed link.

MEANS [CR3] P6.2: "the sentence is sworn by the LORD's life"
- **[L1]** Jeremiah 22:24: "[As] I live, saith the LORD, though Coniah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah were the signet upon my right hand, yet would I pluck thee thence."
- **[L2]** *chay* (living) is the oath-word. Its object is "pluck thee thence," the plucking of the signet from Coniah.
- **[L3]** Haggai 2:23: "will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee, saith the LORD of hosts."
- **[L4]** The oath plucks the signet from Coniah himself, and the plucking was done to him. The same LORD then makes Coniah's grandson "as a signet," by his own word and choosing. The oath stands whole on Coniah, and the LORD's choosing stands whole on Zerubbabel. Both fit the narrowed link.

MEANS [CR3] P6.3: "Zerubbabel is a governor, not one ruling on David's throne"
- **[L1]** Haggai 1:1: "Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah." Margin: "governor: or, captain."
- **[L2]** *pechah* (governor). He holds the office of governor while carrying the chosen signet (Haggai 2:23).
- **[L3]** Acts 2:30: "he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."
- **[L4]** I grant it: Zerubbabel governs and carries the signet, and the sitting waits for God's raising of David's seed (Acts 2:30; Luke 1:32). That is the narrowed link. The LORD restores the signet to Coniah's seed, and the LORD gives the throne. The defender's own [L4], that the throne "rests on God's gift (Luke 1:32)," agrees with it.

---

**ASSUMPTION CHARGED in the defender's LINK 6 [L4]:** "The flesh reaches the child through the woman addressed in Luke 1:32."
ASSUMES: the woman addressed is of the house of David.
ROWS GIVE: "a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David" (Luke 1:27); "thy cousin Elisabeth" (Luke 1:36), who is "of the daughters of Aaron" (Luke 1:5).
