blk:
DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 3, LINK ROUND

# LINK ROUND

**LINK 1: NARROWED TO:** Matthew 1:18 and Matthew 1:25 bound the conceiving and the pregnancy. Luke 1:34 gives Mary's state when she asked. I drop the claim that Luke 1:34's present tense alone spans the whole period.

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- **[L2]** *sunerchomai* (to come together). The finding with child is dated before the coming together, and the source is named in the same clause.
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." Matthew 1:24: "and took unto him his wife."
- **[L3]** Luke 1:56: "And Mary abode with her about three months, and returned to her own house."
- **[L4]** The conceiving is future to Luke 1:34 (Luke 1:31, "thou shalt conceive in thy womb"). Matthew 1:18 finds it done before the coming together. From the taking (1:24) to the birth Joseph "knew her not" (1:25). Luke 1:56 puts her three months in her own house between the two. The span from conceiving to birth is covered. I grant the challenger's own point that Luke 1:31 is future to Luke 1:34. The "knowing within the espousal" is the challenger's [L4]. Matthew 1:18 gives the source of the child as "of the Holy Ghost", not a husband.

Pressed witnesses:
- **Luke 1:31** "And, behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son." *Syllambanō* (to conceive) is future. Luke 1:35 answers how: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee."
- **Matthew 1:24** "and took unto him his wife." *Paralambanō* (to receive near, take unto). The taking is the step after which Matthew 1:25 runs "till". That is the limb I keep.
- **Isaiah 7:14** "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."
  - [L2] *'almah* (H5959), which the KJV renders "virgin" here.
  - [L3] Genesis 24:43 "when the virgin cometh forth to draw [water]" is the same Hebrew word. Genesis 24:16 says of that same person, "a virgin, neither had any man known her."
  - [L4] The word the KJV gives in Isaiah 7:14 carries the unknown-by-man sense in its own cross-reference.
- **Isaiah 8:3** "And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son." *Qârab* (to approach), margin "Heb. approached". Here the woman is "the prophetess" (*nᵉbîyʼâh*, a prophet's wife), already a wife. The child is told "Call his name Mahershalalhashbaz", not Immanuel.
- **Isaiah 7:16** "For before the child shall know to refuse the evil, and choose the good, the land that thou abhorrest shall be forsaken of both her kings."
- **Isaiah 8:4** "For before the child shall have knowledge to cry, My father, and my mother."
  - Each verse gives a time-measure for a child. Isaiah 8:4 follows the naming of Mahershalalhashbaz (8:3), and its measure ends in "the riches of Damascus". That does not merge the two children.
- **Isaiah 8:8** "the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel." Immanuel is addressed as owner of the land. Matthew 1:23 gives the interpretation: "God with us".
- **Isaiah 8:18** "Behold, I and the children whom the LORD hath given me [are] for signs and for wonders in Israel."
- **[L4]** Isaiah's children are signs in his day. Matthew 1:22 states the fulfilment of the virgin sign in the child of 1:18-20: "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet."

**LINK 2: SUPPORTED.**

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The margin reads "conceived: Gr. begotten."
- **[L2]** *gennaō* (G1080), which the lexicon glosses "to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother)". It is joined to *ek* (out of) with the Holy Ghost as source.
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:18, "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost", names the same source before the coming together.
- **[L4]** The verb of fathering takes the Holy Ghost as its source in the angel's row. The finding (1:18) and the angel's *gar* (for) clause (1:20) both carry it.

Pressed witnesses:
- **Deuteronomy 20:7** "that hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her." The taking is a later step. Matthew 1:20, "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife", puts Joseph before it.
- **Deuteronomy 22:24** "the man, because he hath humbled his neighbour's wife." The man here is "his neighbour's", that is, a man other than the husband. The verse shows a betrothed damsel's being known by a man not her husband, and that case is stoned. It gives no knowing by a husband.
- **John 1:13** "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God."
  - [L2] It denies *haima* (blood), *thelēma* (will) and *anēr* (man) as the cause.
  - [L3] John 3:4, "can he enter the second time into his mother's womb, and be born?" shows the believer's birth "of God" is a second birth.
  - [L4] For believers it is figurative regeneration (the G1080 lexicon: "figuratively, to regenerate") after a fleshly birth.
- **1 John 5:1** "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God." This is the same second birth. Matthew 1:20 names one conceiving in Mary, and its source is the Holy Ghost.
- **John 3:6** "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit." The two kinds are two births of the believer. Romans 1:3 uses *ginomai* (to become, be made) for the flesh taken, not *gennaō* (to beget).
- **Acts 1:8** "ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you." *Eperchomai* (to come upon) brings *dunamis* (power).
- **Luke 9:34** "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them." *Episkiazō* (to overshadow).
- **Acts 5:15** "that at the least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them."
- **[L4]** Luke 1:35 reads "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." It is the angel's answer to Luke 1:34's "How shall this be". Its *dio kai* (therefore also) ties "that holy thing which shall be born of thee" to the coming and the overshadowing. Acts 1:8's power and Acts 5:15's healing are what the same verbs bring there. Luke 1:35 names "the power of the Highest" over the woman who asked about conceiving.

**LINK 3: NARROWED TO:** In Matthew 1:2-15 each child is the object of "begat", and Matthew 1:16 shifts the form for the one case Matthew 1:18-20 then gives to the Holy Ghost. I drop the claim that the passive alone proves the point.

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus."
- **[L2]** *ex hēs* (of whom) is feminine singular, so the one named as source is Mary alone. *Egennēthē* (was born) is passive.
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:2: "Jacob begat Judas and his brethren." Matthew 1:20 then supplies the source.
- **[L4]** "Begat" governs Joseph. The next clause drops it and names the mother alone.

Pressed witnesses:
- **Matthew 1:3** "And Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar." The begetter has "begat", and the mother follows.
- **Matthew 1:5** "Booz begat Obed of Ruth." This is the same pattern. In 1:16 the "begat" attaches to Joseph, and the child is not its object.
- **Matthew 2:1** "when Jesus was born in Bethlehem." I grant that the passive names the birth. My footing is the 1:16 shift, with 1:20.
- **Matthew 1:21** "thou shalt call his name JESUS." Luke 1:31 gives the same command to Mary, "shalt call his name JESUS", and Luke 1:60 has the mother naming: "his mother answered and said, Not so; but he shall be called John." Genesis 4:25: "she bare a son, and called his name Seth". Joseph's naming (Matthew 1:25) is the son of David taking the child into his house (Matthew 1:20).
- **Luke 1:13** and **Luke 1:62** show that the father may name. Luke 1:60 and Luke 1:31 show that the mother also names, so naming is no mark of the begetter.

**LINK 4: NARROWED TO:** A husband who knew himself the father had no cause to put her away. Luke 2:48 is met by Luke 2:49.

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
- **[L2]** *boulomai* (to be minded) with *apoluō* (G630, to free fully, divorce). The act proposed is a divorce.
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:20: "while he thought on these things... fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
- **[L4]** Joseph's purpose was to end the bond. A man who took himself to be the father has no cause to divorce the mother. The angel meets his thought with the source: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost". I accept that *paradeigmatizō* (to expose to infamy) names a public showing. The question is why a husband who was the father would divorce her at all.

Pressed witnesses:
- **Matthew 1:19** and **Matthew 1:18** are answered above. Matthew 1:18 puts the finding before the coming together, with "of the Holy Ghost" in the same clause.
- **Luke 2:48** "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." *Patēr* (G3962, father, near or more remote). Luke 2:49 gives the answer in the same scene: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" Luke 2:50 says "they understood not the saying which he spake unto them."
- **Luke 2:51** "and was subject unto them." Compare Luke 10:17, "even the devils are subject unto us through thy name". The same verb is used of subjection with no kinship.
- **Luke 2:41** "Now his parents went to Jerusalem every year." *Goneis* (parents). Luke 2:43 gives the narrator's own phrase: "Joseph and his mother knew not [of it]."
- **Acts 16:13** "where prayer was wont to be made." This is a custom, not a supposal about a person's relation.
- **Luke 2:44** "supposing him to have been in the company." The supposal was false.
- **Acts 14:19** "supposing he had been dead." This one was false too.
- **[L4]** Luke 3:23, "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph", is the same verb *nomizō* (to suppose) used of a person's relation. The two Lukan cases of supposal about a person (Luke 2:44, Acts 14:19) were both mistaken.
- **1 Chronicles 28:6** "I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father." *Bāḥar* (to choose) is election wording. Luke 1:35 gives a coming-upon and overshadowing, then "that holy thing which shall be born of thee". I drop any claim that the two forms are the same.

**LINK 5: NARROWED TO:** Hebrews 10:5's prepared body fits Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35, with Hebrews 2:16 as a taking hold. I grant that "of a woman" is said of men with fathers. I grant that "her seed" alone does not exclude a man's seed. Both limbs are dropped.

- **[L1]** Hebrews 10:5: "Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me." The margin reads "thou hast fitted me."
- **[L2]** *katartizō* (to fit, prepare). The body is fitted at his coming into the world.
- **[L3]** Luke 1:35: "the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee."
- **[L4]** The body is God's fitting, and it matches the source Matthew 1:20 names.

Pressed witnesses:
- **Genesis 4:25** "Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son... hath appointed me another seed." *Zera'* (seed). Granted, so I drop "her seed" as a proof.
- **Genesis 16:10** "I will multiply thy seed exceedingly." Granted for the same reason.
- **Hebrews 2:14** "he also himself likewise took part of the same." *Metechō* (to take part in) with "likewise", a similar taking part.
- **Hebrews 2:17** "in all things it behoved him to be made like unto [his] brethren." Hebrews 4:15 limits it: "but was in all points tempted like as [we are, yet] without sin."
- **Hebrews 2:16** "he took on [him] the seed of Abraham." The margin reads "of the seed of Abraham he taketh hold". The object of his taking hold is whom he helps, as the verse sets it against angels.
- **Hebrews 7:5** "though they come out of the loins of Abraham." *Osphys* (loins) is the writer's word for the sons of Levi. For the Lord he writes *anatellō* (to spring up) in Hebrews 7:14.
- **Job 14:1** "Man [that is] born of a woman." Granted that this is said of men with fathers.
- **Matthew 11:11** "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist." Granted.

**LINK 6: SUPPORTED.**

- **[L1]** Luke 1:32: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David." It is spoken to Mary.
- **[L2]** *patēr* (G3962, father, near or more remote), with *didōmi* (to give). The angel names David "his father" to a woman who says "I know not a man" (Luke 1:34).
- **[L3]** Jeremiah 22:30: "for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David, and ruling any more in Judah." Matthew 1:12: "Jechonias begat Salathiel."
- **[L4]** Joseph's line runs through Jechonias (Matthew 1:12). If the throne came by Joseph's seed, it would be "his seed... sitting upon the throne of David", which Jeremiah 22:30 bars. So the throne cannot rest on Joseph's seed. It rests on God's gift (Luke 1:32). The right reaches Joseph's house by his being "thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20). The flesh reaches the child through the woman addressed in Luke 1:32.

Pressed witnesses:
- **Acts 2:30** "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne." *Osphys* (loins). God "raise[s] up", and the flesh descent is David's. Luke 1:32 gives the child "his father David" through the woman.
- **Romans 1:3** "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." *Sperma* (seed) with *ginomai* (to be made). The same writer says in Galatians 4:4 "made of a woman".
- **2 Samuel 7:12** "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels." God "set[s] up", and the seed is David's. It is not tied to a male line through Joseph.
- **Hebrews 7:14** "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda." *Anatellō* (to spring up). Numbers 1:18, "by the house of their fathers", is a register term (*bayith*, house, family). Genesis 48:5 ("are mine"), Deuteronomy 25:6 ("shall succeed in the name of his brother") and Luke 2:4 ("of the house and lineage of David") show houses reckon children by the name and house, as well as by begetting. Joseph named the child (Matthew 1:25).
- **Haggai 2:23** "will I take thee, O Zerubbabel, my servant... and will make thee as a signet."
- **Haggai 1:1** "Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah." He is governor. Jeremiah 22:30's "sitting upon the throne of David, and ruling" is not spent in him.
- **Jeremiah 22:24** "[As] I live, saith the LORD... yet would I pluck thee thence." This is the LORD's oath.
- **Jeremiah 18:8** "If that nation, against whom I have pronounced, turn from their evil, I will repent." This is a condition on a nation turning. Haggai 1:1 names a governor, not a king on David's throne.

**CHALLENGER'S UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES**

1. The inference that the conceiving the angel names lies ahead as a man's act props the "knowing within the espousal" objection. Quote: "An espoused damsel who had not yet been taken speaks truly in the present tense, and the conceiving the angel names lies ahead (Luke 1:31)."

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 3, LINK ROUND

**LINK 1: SUPPORTED**

Matthew 1:20 [L1]: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]". Matthew 1:18 [L3]: "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." Luke 1:35 [L3]: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee".

[L2] The verb behind "conceived" is *gennaō* (G1080, "to procreate (properly, of the father...); figuratively, to regenerate"). Matthew 1:20 puts the Holy Ghost in the source position of that verb, and puts the place "in her."

[L4] Matthew 1:18 dates that source "before they came together," and Matthew 1:20 and 1:18 together name one source. The chain is: the begetting verb (L2), the source named in 1:20 (L1), and the date in 1:18 (L3).

*Presses answered:*

- John 1:13, "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God." [L2] The verse names three human sources: *haima* (G129, blood, "kindred"), *thelēma* (G2307, will) and *anēr* (G435, "a man... husband"). The verse sets "of God" against the male source. The believers' birth is *gennaō* in its figurative sense, "to regenerate" (G1080), and it comes after "received him" and "power to become" (John 1:12 [L3]). Matthew 1:20 is the literal sense, with "in her" and "before they came together" (1:18). That is the fit, and it is not a second origin added to a father's.
- 1 John 5:1, "every one that loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him." The subjects are "Whosoever believeth," and the margin reads "has been born." That is a birth after believing.
- 1 John 3:9, "for his seed remaineth in him." [L2] *menō* (G3306, to abide) shows *sperma* (G4690) there as an indwelling nature. This is the figurative use, and Matthew 1:20 has a womb.
- John 3:6, "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit." For the child, the flesh is "born of thee" (Luke 1:35 [L3]) and the Spirit is "come upon thee." That fits my link and gives no male seed.
- Romans 1:4, "according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead." Paul's "declared" is set "by the resurrection." Romans 1:3 reads "made of the seed of David": *ginomai* (G1096, to become) with *sperma* (G4690, "by implication, offspring"). Offspring in 2 Samuel 7:12 [L3] is "thy seed... which shall proceed out of thy bowels," and it is descent. Both orders are granted and neither names Joseph's seed.

**LINK 2: SUPPORTED**

Luke 1:34 [L1]: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" Luke 1:35 [L1]: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." Luke 1:37 [L3]: "For with God nothing shall be impossible."

[L2] *epérchomai* (G1904, "to supervene... influence") and *episkiázō* (G1982, "to invest with preternatural influence") name God's power on Mary. *dió* ("therefore") in 1:35 ties the title to the coming upon, in the same sentence.

[L4] Mary asks "How" (1:34). The reply opens with the agent (1:35) and ends with 1:37. The chain is: the question (L1), the agent verbs (L2), the "therefore" and the closing verse (L3).

*Presses answered:*

- Luke 1:32, "shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David". Verse 32 states the title. Verse 35 states the ground, "therefore also." Both stand, and the covenant does not remove the ground given to Mary's "How."
- Acts 1:8, "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you". Luke 9:34, "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them". Acts 5:15, "the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them". In each, God's power or presence comes upon and the effect follows. In Luke 1:35 the effect is "that holy thing which shall be born of thee."
- Luke 1:36, "she hath also conceived a son in her old age: and this is the sixth month with her, who was called barren." The "also" joins two conceptions as signs of God's power. Elisabeth's is placed on a named husband (Luke 1:13 [L3], "shall bear thee a son"). Mary's is answered with "come upon thee" after "I know not a man."

**LINK 3: NARROWED TO:** the conception is "of the Holy Ghost" and found "before they came together." I drop any claim about the word "virgin" alone.

Matthew 1:18 [L1]: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." Matthew 1:25 [L3]: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son".

[L2] *héōs* (G2193, "until") bounds Joseph's not knowing at the birth. *yada* (H3045, to know) at Genesis 4:1 comes before "she conceived." Matthew 1:18 puts the conception before the coming together.

[L4] Genesis 4:1 [L3] reads "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived." Matthew 1:18 reverses that order. The chain is Matthew 1:18 (L1), *héōs* (L2) and Genesis 4:1 (L3).

*Presses answered:*

- Genesis 4:25, 16:10, 24:60. In each the husband's knowing is stated, or the verse is spoken of mothers who bore to husbands. Luke 1:34 and Matthew 1:25 state the opposite for Mary.
- Isaiah 8:3, "And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived". [margin: Heb. approached] This is a separate act, recorded after the sign of Isaiah 7:14, and it names "the prophetess." Isaiah 7:11 sets the sign as one to "ask it either in the depth, or in the height above." Matthew 1:22 [L3] reads "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled."
- Isaiah 8:4, "cry, My father, and my mother." That is the child of Isaiah's sign.
- Deuteronomy 22:24, "his neighbour's wife." I grant that the law calls the betrothed a wife. That fits Matthew 1:20, "Mary thy wife."
- Matthew 1:24, "took unto him his wife." The taking is after the finding, and the "till" of 1:25 bounds Joseph's not knowing her.

**LINK 4: NARROWED TO:** Joseph's naming and the greeting "son of David" do not prove begetting. Joseph receives the child by the angel's word. I drop "guardian" as a separate claim.

Matthew 1:21 [L1]: "thou shalt call his name JESUS". Matthew 1:20 [L3]: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife".

[L2] *qārā'* (H7121, "to call out... give name") is said of the mother at Genesis 4:25 [L3], "and called his name Seth." Luke 1:31 [L3] gives the same naming to Mary: "and shalt call his name JESUS." Matthew 1:16 [L3] reads "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus." The chain of "begat" (Matthew 1:2) ends at "husband of Mary," and the verb passes to birth "of whom."

[L4] The same act is assigned to the mother, so the naming is not the mark of the begetter. This rests on Genesis 4:25 (L1/L3) and *qārā'* (L2).

*Presses answered:*

- Matthew 11:11, "born of women," and Job 14:1, "born of a woman." I grant that this is said of men with fathers. My link does not rest on it.
- Luke 1:13 and 1:63. The angel's "thou shalt call" is the same act given to Mary in Luke 1:31.
- Luke 2:4, "of the house and lineage of David." This is Joseph's house, and I grant it.
- Genesis 4:1 is answered at LINK 3.

**LINK 5: SUPPORTED**

Luke 3:23 [L1]: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph". Luke 2:49 [L3]: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?"

[L2] *nomizō* (to deem or hold by usage) is the verb behind "supposed" in Luke 3:23. Acts 16:13 [L3] shows the same verb as "wont." Both name what is held, and Luke 3:23 puts it in brackets as "supposed." [L2] *patēr* (G3962) is the word in Luke 2:48 and in 2:49.

[L4] Mary says "thy father" (2:48) and the child answers "my Father's" (2:49). The chain is 3:23 (L1), *nomizō* (L2) and 2:49 (L3).

*Presses answered:*

- Luke 2:48, 2:27, 2:41. These are household usage "after the custom of the law" (2:27).
- Luke 2:33, "Joseph and his mother marvelled," and Luke 2:43, "Joseph and his mother knew not [of it]." These are the narrator's own words, and they name "Joseph."
- John 1:45, "the son of Joseph." That is Philip's speech. John 6:42 [L3] reads "whose father and mother we know," spoken by those who murmured.
- 1 Chronicles 28:6, "I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father." This is "chosen." Matthew 1:20 has "conceived... of the Holy Ghost."
- Psalms 2:7, "this day have I begotten thee." Acts 13:33 [L3] applies it to "raised up Jesus again." It names a day, and Matthew 1:20 names the womb. Both fit.

**LINK 6: NARROWED TO:** the flesh-descent from David is carried by the woman out of whom the child is born. The legal house is Joseph's (Luke 2:4), and I grant that.

Luke 1:32 [L1]: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David". Luke 1:35 [L3]: "born of thee". Acts 2:30 [L3]: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ".

[L2] *ginomai* (G1096, to become) stands in Romans 1:3 [L3], "made of the seed of David." Luke 3:23 [L3] reads "which was [the son] of Heli," and Matthew 1:16 [L3] reads "Jacob begat Joseph." Two fathers are named for Joseph.

[L4] The chain is: David's promise (Acts 2:30), its address to Mary (Luke 1:32 and 1:35), and the two fathers named for Joseph (Luke 3:23 and Matthew 1:16).

*Presses answered:*

- Job 14:1, "of a woman," is granted at LINK 4.
- Romans 1:3, "made of the seed of David." See LINK 1.
- Acts 2:30, "fruit of his loins." Hebrews 7:10, "he was yet in the loins of his father." Hebrews 7:14, "our Lord sprang out of Juda." Numbers 1:18, "by the house of their fathers." Ezra 2:62, "put from the priesthood." These are the register by the father's house, and I grant it as the legal reckoning. My narrowed link concerns the flesh.
- Luke 1:27, "a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David." That is the legal house, granted.

**CHALLENGER'S UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES**

1. The seed order is placed on Joseph by the greeting. "The Spirit order is "of the Holy Ghost," and the seed order is set on the man the angel greets as "son of David."" PRESSED WITH:
Matthew 1:16 "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ." -- MEANS: the "begat" chain stops at "the husband of Mary" and the birth is "of whom" -- [L2] *gennaō* (G1080, to beget; to be born) | [L3] Matthew 1:2 "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob"
Matthew 1:18 "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." -- MEANS: the conception is found before any coming together -- [L2] *héōs* (G2193, until) | [L3] Matthew 1:25 "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son"

2. "Also" places Mary's conception beside Elisabeth's. "The "also" (*kai*) of Luke 1:36 puts Mary's conception beside that one." PRESSED WITH:
Luke 1:34 "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" -- MEANS: Mary's conception is asked as without a man, unlike Elisabeth's -- [L2] *yada* (H3045, to know, "lie by man") | [L3] Luke 1:13 "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son"
Luke 1:35 "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee" -- MEANS: God's power is the named agent of Mary's conception -- [L2] *episkiázō* (G1982, to invest with preternatural influence) | [L3] Luke 1:37 "For with God nothing shall be impossible."

3. Joseph knew Mary in the espousal. "On the seed rows and "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived" (Genesis 4:1), Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal." PRESSED WITH:
Matthew 1:25 "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" -- MEANS: Joseph's not knowing runs to the birth -- [L2] *héōs* (G2193, until) | [L3] Matthew 1:18 "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost"
Luke 1:34 "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" -- MEANS: Mary states that she knows no man -- [L2] *yada* (H3045, to know) | [L3] Matthew 1:20 "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife"

4. The naming is the father's act. "The defender's "legal placing" fits the angel's words less well than the father's act the same angel assigns in Luke 1." PRESSED WITH:
Genesis 4:25 "And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth" -- MEANS: the mother also gives the name -- [L2] *qārā'* (H7121, to call, name) | [L3] Luke 1:31 "and shalt call his name JESUS"
Luke 1:31 "And, behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS." -- MEANS: the same naming is given to Mary -- [L2] *kaléō* (G2564, to call) | [L3] Isaiah 7:14 "and shall call his name Immanuel"

5. Mary's word names the begetter. "Mary, who heard the angel, says "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing" (Luke 2:48)." PRESSED WITH:
Luke 2:49 "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" -- MEANS: the child answers "thy father" with "my Father" -- [L2] *patēr* (G3962, father) | [L3] Luke 2:48 "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing"
Luke 3:23 "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph" -- MEANS: the narrator marks the sonship as supposed -- [L2] *nomizō* (to hold by usage) | [L3] Acts 16:13 "where prayer was wont to be made"
Luke 2:33 "And Joseph and his mother marvelled at those things which were spoken of him." -- MEANS: the narrator himself says "Joseph and his mother" -- [L2] *patēr* (G3962) | [L3] Luke 2:43 "Joseph and his mother knew not [of it]"

6. The flesh-descent runs down to Joseph. "So "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" (Acts 2:30) and "evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda" (Hebrews 7:14) come down that chain to "Joseph, thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20)." PRESSED WITH:
Matthew 1:16 "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ." -- MEANS: the chain of "begat" ends at Joseph, and the birth is "of whom" -- [L2] *gennaō* (G1080) | [L3] Matthew 1:2 "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob"
Luke 1:35 "therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God" -- MEANS: the flesh is "born of thee" -- [L2] *gennaō* (G1080, to procreate; to be born) | [L3] Luke 1:32 "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David"
2 Samuel 7:12 "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels" -- MEANS: David's seed is descent that proceeds out, without naming a begetting by a husband -- [L2] *zeraʻ* (H2233, seed, posterity) | [L3] Romans 1:3 "made of the seed of David according to the flesh"

# LINK ROUND

## LINK 1: SUPPORTED

The link: "of the Holy Ghost" names the source of what was begotten in Mary, and no human begetter is left.

**Footing.**
- [L1] Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The KJV margin reads "[conceived: Gr. begotten]".
- [L2] *gennaō* (G1080): "to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother)". The verb that stands behind "conceived" in Matthew 1:20 is the begetting verb, and the verse names its source as the Holy Ghost.
- [L1] Matthew 1:18: "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." Matthew's own voice names the same source.
- [L4] Matthew 1:20 with *gennaō*, and Matthew 1:18: the begetting verb is given its source in two verses, and the source is the Holy Ghost. A source named for the begetting is a begetter named.

**Answers to the pressed verses.**

**Matthew 1:20** "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The press: it addresses a son of David as husband, and grounds the command to take her.
- I grant the address and the ground. The ground is the clause "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
- [L2] *gennaō* is the verb of that clause, and the clause gives its source as the Holy Ghost.
- [L3] Matthew 1:18 gives the same source at the finding, "before they came together."
- [L4] The "for" supplies a reason, and the reason it supplies is a source named for the begetting. That fits the link.

**1 John 5:1** "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God," and **1 John 4:7** "every one that loveth is born of God." The press: "born of God" is said of men whose fathers begat them.
- I grant it. I do not rest the link on the phrase "born of God" alone.
- [L2] *gennaō* in 1 John is the figurative sense, "to regenerate". It is said of a believer already living.
- [L1] Matthew 1:20 says "that which is conceived in her", and the object is a thing conceived in the womb, not a living believer.
- [L3] John 3:6: "That which is born of the Spirit is spirit." Regeneration of a living man is a second birth. Matthew 1:20 and 1:18 speak of the conceiving.

**John 3:6** "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit." The press: the child's flesh is born of the flesh.
- I grant it. Flesh is born of flesh.
- [L1] Genesis 2:23: "bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh", said of a woman. [L3] Luke 1:35: "that holy thing which shall be born of thee."

- I grant the two clauses stand nearest. What they ground is stated in the result clause: a CALLING (*kaleō*), "shall be called the Son of God."
- [L2] *eperchomai* (G1904, to come upon) stands in Luke 1:35 and in Acts 1:8. [L3] Acts 1:8: "But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me ... [power...: or, the power of the Holy Ghost coming upon you]." Its result is power and witness, in men already born.
- [L2] *episkiazō* (G1982, to overshadow) stands in Luke 1:35 and in Luke 9:34. [L3] Luke 9:34: "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them." This is the presence-cloud.
- [L3] Romans 1:4 gives the title its declaration: "declared [to be] the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead: [declared: Gr. determined]."
- [L4] The two near clauses name presence and power upon her. They ground the naming of the child as holy and as Son of God. That naming is the title already given in verse 32 with David's throne, and Romans 1:4 declares it by the resurrection.
- It fits the link: the nearest clauses supply the reason for the calling, and the calling with "also" reaches back to verse 32.

## LINK 4: SUPPORTED

The link: Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal.

**Footing.**
- [L1] 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels."
- [L1] Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."
- [L1] Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh."
- [L3] Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain ... [Cain: that is, Gotten, or, Acquired]."
- [L1] Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband." Matthew 1:20: "Mary thy wife." Deuteronomy 22:24: "his neighbour's wife."
- [L2] *anēr* (G435, husband) and *gynē* (G1135, wife) stand in Matthew 1:19-20. *yada'* (H3045) in Genesis 4:1 carries the lexicon sense "lie by man."
- [L4] Chain:
  1. The promised seed is out of a man's bowels and loins, according to the flesh.
  2. The canon's stated means of begetting is the husband knowing his wife (Genesis 4:1).
  3. The man Matthew names as her husband from the espousal is Joseph, "son of David" (Matthew 1:20).
  4. So Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins.

**Answers to the presses.**

MEANS [CR3] P4.1: "the knowing is dated after the birth, not before the conceiving"

- [L1] Matthew 1:24-25: "took unto him his wife: And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
- [L2] *heōs* (G2193, until) marks a span of time, "until (of time and place)."
- [L3] Deuteronomy 20:7: "what man [is there] that hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her?" The law names a betrothal before the taking.
- [L4] The "knew her not" of 1:25 follows "took unto him his wife" (1:24). Its span runs from the taking to the birth. The espousal stands before the taking, in the time Deuteronomy 20:7 calls "betrothed a wife ... not taken her."
- So Genesis 4:1's order holds inside the espousal: knowing, then conceiving. The finding follows (1:18), then the taking (1:24), then the abstinence "till" the birth (1:25).
- It fits the link: the abstinence 1:25 bounds belongs to the pregnancy after the taking.

MEANS [CR3] P4.2: "the finding with the source named is dated before the coming together"

- I grant the order. The coming together is the taking (*paralambanō*, G3880, to receive near), which the defender also granted.
- [L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- [L3] Deuteronomy 22:23: "a damsel [that is] a virgin be betrothed unto an husband." In the betrothal the man is already "an husband" (*'ish*, H376, man, husband).
- [L4] The finding falls in the espousal, "espoused to Joseph." Deuteronomy 22:23 calls the espoused man her husband in that same time. The conceiving within the espousal belongs to the husband the verse names, Joseph.
- "Of the Holy Ghost" names the origin from God, as Link 1 shows from 2 Samuel 7:12-14.
- It fits the link.

MEANS [CR3] P4.3: "Mary names her condition when told she shall conceive"

- I grant it. [L2] *ginōskō* (G1097, to know) is present indicative in "I know not a man." It states her condition at that hour.
- [L1] Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David." Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb."
- [L3] Luke 1:36: "thy cousin Elisabeth, she hath also conceived a son in her old age." Luke 1:13: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son." Elisabeth's conceiving came by her husband, "bear thee."
- [L4] Her condition at the hour is present. The conceiving is future ("shalt"), to a woman espoused to a named man. The angel's "also" in 1:36 sets her coming conception beside Elisabeth's, which came by her husband.
- It fits the link: the present condition of an espoused wife stands before a future conception by the husband Luke names in 1:27.

## LINK 5: SUPPORTED

The link: a just husband who willed to spare her a public showing yielded to that public consideration, "privily."

**Footing.**
- [L1] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
- [L2] Two verbs carry the verse:
  - *thelō* (G2309) stands behind "willing." Its gloss is "to determine (as an active option from subjective impulse)."
  - *boulomai* (G1014) stands behind "was minded." The *thelō* gloss contrasts it: *boulomai* "properly denotes rather a passive acquiescence in objective considerations."
  - *paradeigmatizō* (G3856) is "expose to infamy."
- [L3] Matthew 1:20: "But while he thought on these things ... Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The angel answers his thought with "fear not."
- [L4] Chain:
  - His own will (*thelō*) was to spare her infamy.
  - His mind to put away (*boulomai*) is the verb of yielding to outside considerations.
  - The angel meets that thought by removing fear (*phobeō*) and grounding the taking in God's claim.
  - So the putting away was a yielding, which the angel's word reversed.

**Answers to the presses.**

MEANS [CR3] P5.1: "the justice is carried by the putting away, which a man who knew himself the father could not do justly"

- [L1] Deuteronomy 22:23: "If a damsel [that is] a virgin be betrothed unto an husband, and a man find her in the city, and lie with her."
- [L2] *'ish* (H376, man, husband) stands twice in that verse: "an husband" and "a man." There are two men, and the guilty one is the second.
- [L3] Matthew 1:19 calls Joseph "her husband." He stands in the place of the first man of Deuteronomy 22:23.
- [L4] A husband who knew his own betrothed is "an husband" of 22:23, the one to whom she is betrothed.
  - *dikaios* (G1342, just) is "equitable (in character or act)."
  - His equity is stated in the verse: "not willing to make her a publick example."
  - His putting away is *boulomai*, a yielding to outside considerations.
- It fits the link: Matthew carries his justice in sparing her infamy. The putting away is the yielding that the angel's "fear not" (1:20) turned into "took unto him his wife" (1:24).

MEANS [CR3] P5.2: "the man who lay with the betrothed is brought out with her as the guilty one"

- I grant it.
- [L1] Deuteronomy 22:24: "and the man, because he hath humbled his neighbour's wife: so thou shalt put away evil from among you."
- [L3] Deuteronomy 22:23 names her as "betrothed unto an husband."
- [L4] The guilty man's charge is that he humbled "his neighbour's wife," the wife of another man. The betrothed's own husband is the "husband" of 22:23, whose wife she is. The gate law sets the guilt on the man who lay with another man's betrothed.
- It fits the link: Joseph, "her husband," stands as the husband of 22:23.

## LINK 6: NARROWED TO: Joseph performs the naming the angel gives him, the act Luke 1:62-63 gives the father in the settling of a name, and it joins the rows that name him "her husband" and "thy father." I drop the claim that the command alone marks the begetter.

**Footing for the kept limb.**
- [L1] Matthew 1:21: "And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins. [JESUS: that is, Saviour, Heb]" Matthew 1:25: "and he called his name JESUS."
- [L2] *kaleō* (G2564, to call, to name) stands in Matthew 1:21 and 1:25.
- [L3] Luke 1:62-63: "And they made signs to his father, how he would have him called. And he asked for a writing table, and wrote, saying, His name is John."
- [L3] Luke 2:48: "behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."
- [L4] Chain:
  - In Luke 1:62-63 the company turns to the father to settle the name, and his word settles it.
  - Matthew gives the settling act to Joseph: "he called his name JESUS."
  - Mary's own mouth names Joseph "thy father" (Luke 2:48).
  - So the naming stands with the father-rows.

**Answers to the presses.**

MEANS [CR3] P6.1: "the same command to call the name is given to Mary"

- I grant it.
- [L1] Luke 1:31: "and shalt call his name JESUS."
- [L3] Luke 1:60, 63: "his mother answered and said, Not [so]; but he shall be called John" and "His name is John." In John's case the mother speaks the name and the father settles it.
- [L4] Both parents carry the naming of John. The father's word closes it.
- In Jesus' case the command goes to Mary (Luke 1:31) and to Joseph (Matthew 1:21), and Joseph performs it (Matthew 1:25).
- It fits the narrowed link: the John pattern has both parents naming, with the father's act settling the name.

MEANS [CR3] P6.2: "the margin gives the virgin as the one who calls the name"

- [L1] Isaiah 7:14: "and shall call his name Immanuel. [shall call: or, thou, O virgin, shalt call]"
- [L3] Isaiah 8:3: "Then said the LORD to me, Call his name Mahershalalhashbaz. [went: Heb. approached]" In the sign's own setting the LORD commands the naming of the son of the approach to the husband, Isaiah.
- [L4] The margin gives the mother a naming, as Luke 1:31 does. Isaiah 8:3 gives the husband the naming of the sign's son.
- It fits the narrowed link: mother and husband both carry the naming in Isaiah, as in Luke 1:60-63.

MEANS [CR3] P6.3: "Joseph's naming stands in the verse of "knew her not", as obedience to the bidding"

- I grant the obedience.
- [L1] Matthew 1:24-25: "did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife: And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."
- [L3] The bidding was spoken to "Joseph, thou son of David" in Matthew 1:20, about "Mary thy wife," with the ground "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
- [L4] The obedience is a son of David performing on his wife's firstborn son the act Luke 1:62-63 gives the father. The span of 1:25 runs from the taking to the birth, as Link 4 shows by *heōs* (until).
- It fits the narrowed link.

**Put to the defender:** Hebrews 7:14 says, "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood." The law reckons by "their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:18). How is it evident, given that law?

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 3, LINK ROUND

# LINK ROUND

## LINK 1: SUPPORTED

The link: "of the Holy Ghost" names the source of what was begotten in Mary, and no human begetter is left.

**Footing.**
- [L1] Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The KJV margin reads "[conceived: Gr. begotten]".
- [L2] *gennaō* (G1080): "to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother)". The verb that stands behind "conceived" in Matthew 1:20 is the begetting verb, and the verse names its source as the Holy Ghost.
- [L1] Matthew 1:18: "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." Matthew's own voice names the same source.
- [L4] Matthew 1:20 with *gennaō*, and Matthew 1:18: the begetting verb is given its source in two verses, and the source is the Holy Ghost. A source named for the begetting is a begetter named.

**Answers to the pressed verses.**

**Matthew 1:20** "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The press: it addresses a son of David as husband, and grounds the command to take her.
- I grant the address and the ground. The ground is the clause "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
- [L2] *gennaō* is the verb of that clause, and the clause gives its source as the Holy Ghost.
- [L3] Matthew 1:18 gives the same source at the finding, "before they came together."
- [L4] The "for" supplies a reason, and the reason it supplies is a source named for the begetting. That fits the link.

**1 John 5:1** "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God," and **1 John 4:7** "every one that loveth is born of God." The press: "born of God" is said of men whose fathers begat them.
- I grant it. I do not rest the link on the phrase "born of God" alone.
- [L2] *gennaō* in 1 John is the figurative sense, "to regenerate". It is said of a believer already living.
- [L1] Matthew 1:20 says "that which is conceived in her", and the object is a thing conceived in the womb, not a living believer.
- [L3] John 3:6: "That which is born of the Spirit is spirit." Regeneration of a living man is a second birth. Matthew 1:20 and 1:18 speak of the conceiving.

**John 3:6** "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit." The press: the child's flesh is born of the flesh.
- I grant it. Flesh is born of flesh.
- [L1] Genesis 2:23: "bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh", said of a woman. [L3] Luke 1:35: "that holy thing which shall be born of thee."
- [L4] John 3:6 with Genesis 2:23 and Luke 1:35: a woman's flesh is flesh, and the child is "born of thee". The flesh side of John 3:6 is satisfied by the mother.

**Romans 1:4** "declared [to be] the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead." The press: sonship stands beside flesh of David's seed.
- I grant the pair.
- [L1] Romans 1:3: "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh." The Son is the subject before he is "made".
- [L2] *ginomai* (G1096): "to become (come into being)".
- [L4] Romans 1:3-4: the "declared" of verse 4 is a declaration "by the resurrection from the dead", and the "made" of verse 3 is the becoming. The two verses set a Son already spoken of who is made of David's seed. They do not set Joseph as the one who made him.

**1 Chronicles 28:6** "I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father," and **2 Samuel 7:14** "I will be his father, and he shall be my son."
- I grant that David's son and God's son are one person in these verses.
- [L1] 1 Chronicles 28:6 says "I have chosen him", an act of choosing. [L1] 2 Samuel 7:14 continues "If he commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men."
- [L3] Hebrews 1:5 sets this promise beside "Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee". [L1] Matthew 1:20 states a begetting with its source.
- [L4] Solomon's sonship is a chosen sonship over a son whose father is David. Matthew 1:20 names the Holy Ghost as the source of the thing conceived. They are different footing.

**2 Samuel 7:12** "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels." The press: God's fatherhood is a covenant word over the son out of David's bowels.
- I grant that the seed proceeds out of David.
- [L1] Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him." [L2] *patēr* (G3962): "father (near or more remote)".
- [L4] Loins and bowels language is used across generations, so it does not fix a single father at the last step.

## LINK 2: SUPPORTED

The link: the answer to Mary's "How?" is a divine act.

**Footing.**
- [L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- [L2] *epercomai* (G1904): "to supervene, i.e. arrive... (figuratively) influence". [L2] *episkiazō* (G1982): "to envelop in a haze of brilliancy; figuratively, to invest with preternatural influence". [L2] *apokrinomai* (G611): "to respond", the verb for "answered" in Luke 1:35 after the question of Luke 1:34.
- [L3] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- [L4] Luke 1:34 with Luke 1:35 and *apokrinomai*: the verse is an answer to the "How", and the answer names acts of the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest upon her.

**Answers to the pressed verses.**

**Luke 1:34** "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" The press: the present indicative states her condition at that hour.
- I grant it. [L2] *ginōskō* (G1097): "to know".
- [L1] Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb", which is the thing she asks about. She asks "How shall this be" about that conceiving, in the condition she names.
- [L4] The reply of Luke 1:35 begins with the Holy Ghost coming upon her. The reply names the means of that conceiving as divine.

**Luke 1:35** "therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." The press: it ends in a naming that adds "also" to the title of verse 32, with *kaleō* (G2564, to call, to name).
- I grant that *kaleō* is in both verses.
- [L4] The "therefore" stands in verse 35, after the two clauses of verse 35 about the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest. The nearest antecedent is those two clauses. "Also" adds the ground to the title already given.

**Luke 1:32** "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David." The press: the title and David's throne are given before verse 34.
- I grant the order.
- [L2] *patēr* (G3962) means "father (near or more remote)". The father-word this verse states is "his father David", and David is the remote father the word covers.
- [L2] *didōmi* (G1325): "to give". The Lord God is the giver of the throne in this verse.
- [L3] Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him." The same word *patēr* is used there of an ancestor generations back.
- [L4] Luke 1:32 with *patēr* and Hebrews 7:10: the verse names David as "his father", the throne comes by God's gift, and the word "father" is used in Scripture of a remote ancestor. So the verse's father-word is met by David as ancestor and God as giver, and it gives no ground for a human begetter at the last step.

**Acts 1:8** "ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you." The press: the coming upon is empowerment of men already born.
- I grant it.
- [L2] *epercomai* is the same verb, and *dynamis* (G1411, "force... miraculous power") is in both verses: "the power of the Highest" in Luke 1:35 and "power" in Acts 1:8.
- [L4] In Acts 1:8 the coming upon of the Holy Ghost produces a result in the person: power received. In Luke 1:35 the result named after the same coming is "that holy thing which shall be born of thee". The verb is the same and the result is named in the verse.

**Luke 9:34** "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them: and they feared as they entered into the cloud," and **Acts 5:15** "the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them." The press: overshadowing is a presence-cloud and a presence that heals.
- I grant both.
- [L2] *episkiazō* in each: "to envelop... to invest with preternatural influence". In Luke 9:34 the cloud overshadowed "them" and they "entered into the cloud". In Acts 5:15 the sick, *asthenēs* (G772, "strengthless"), were laid where the shadow might overshadow them.
- [L4] In both the presence acts upon the person overshadowed. In Luke 1:35 the person is "thee", and "that holy thing which shall be born of thee" follows.

**Luke 1:27** "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David," and **Luke 1:31** "thou shalt conceive in thy womb." The press: the conception is future to an espoused wife.
- I grant it.
- [L1] Luke 1:27 calls her "a virgin", and Luke 1:34 has her say "I know not a man".
- [L3] Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son." [L3] Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son."
- [L4] Luke 1:27, Luke 1:31 and Matthew 1:23: the one who is to conceive is described as a virgin in each. The espousal does not alter that description.

## LINK 3: NARROWED TO: Joseph is the son of David and the husband of Mary, and Jesus is "born of" Mary as the register's own form shows. I drop "by law" as a carrier of David's seed.

**Footing for the kept limb.**
- [L1] Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David." [L1] Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
- [L3] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob." [L3] Matthew 1:3: "And Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar."
- [L2] *gennaō* (G1080) is "properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother".
- [L4] In Matthew 1:2-3 the form is "begat" of each father. At Matthew 1:16 the form changes: Joseph is "the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus". The register carries the active "begat" down to Joseph and breaks it for Jesus.

**Answers to the pressed verses.**

**Matthew 1:16** (quoted above). The press: the passive "born" states the mother's bearing beside "the husband." I grant that. It is the break in the form that I rest on.

**Mark 6:3** "Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary," and **Matthew 13:55** "Is not this the carpenter's son? is not his mother called Mary?" The press: the town names both parents.
- I grant it.
- [L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph." [L3] John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?"
- [L4] The town names him by the father it supposes, and Luke 3:23 sets "as was supposed" on that naming.

**Matthew 11:11** "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist."
- I grant that "born of women" is said of men with fathers. I do not rest the source of Jesus on "of a woman" alone. I rest it on Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:34-35.

**Luke 1:13** "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John."
- I grant it. I answer the naming at Link 4.

**Genesis 4:1** "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain." The press: the husband's knowing is the canon's means of conception.
- I grant it for Adam.
- [L2] *yada'* (H3045) and *ginōskō* (G1097) are both "to know". [L1] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." [L2] *heōs* (G2193): "until".
- [L3] Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 date the conception before the taking: "found with child" before "they came together", and "that which is conceived in her" spoken before Matthew 1:24.
- [L4] Genesis 4:1 puts the knowing first and the conceiving second. Matthew 1:25 dates the "knew her not" through the birth, and Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 show the conceiving already present before the taking. The order of Genesis 4:1 is reversed.

**Luke 2:48** "behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." The press: Mary names Joseph the child's father.
- I grant that Mary says it.
- [L1] Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" [L2] *patēr* (G3962) stands in both verses.
- [L4] Mary says "thy father", and the child's reply in the next verse says "my Father's". The reply sets a second father against the first.

**Acts 2:30** "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne." The press: the throne-seed is fruit of loins.
- I grant it. [L2] *osphys* (G3751): "loin".
- [L3] Psalms 132:11: "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne" [body: Heb. belly]. [L3] Hebrews 7:10: "yet in the loins of his father", with *patēr* "near or more remote".
- [L4] The fruit of David's loins is a descendant, and Hebrews 7:10 uses "loins of his father" of a remote father.

## LINK 4: NARROWED TO: Joseph, being just, was minded to put away a wife he took to have been with another man. I drop the claim that the "not willing to make her a publick example" ground alone proves it.

**Footing for the kept limb.**
- [L1] Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband, being a just [man]... was minded to put her away privily."
- [L2] *dikaios* (G1342): "equitable (in character or act)... innocent, holy". [L2] *apolyō* (G630): "to free fully... divorce".
- [L3] Deuteronomy 22:24: "ye shall bring them both out unto the gate of that city... and the man, because he hath humbled his neighbour's wife." [L3] Deuteronomy 22:23: "a man find her in the city, and lie with her."
- [L4] Matthew 1:19 with *dikaios*, and Deuteronomy 22:23-24: the man who lies with a betrothed wife is the one who "hath humbled his neighbour's wife", and he is brought to the gate with her. A man who knew himself to be that man could not be "just" by putting her away. A man who took her to have been with another could.

**Answers to the pressed verses.**

**Matthew 1:19.** The press: the willing yields to the public showing, with *paradeigmatizō* (G3856, "expose to infamy") and *boulomai* (G1014, "to will").
- I grant the public showing is what he would avoid.
- [L2] *láthra* (G2977): "privately". The means he chose is *apolyō* (G630), a putting away.
